title: Quentin Lake apologized to Justin Herbert for "deli meat" and "seeing ghosts" comments
summary: Rams safety Quentin Lake got plenty of attention for comments he made about intercepting a pass thrown by Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, but on reflection, Lake didn't like the attention he generated.
full_text: Rams safety Quentin Lake got plenty of attention for comments he made about intercepting a pass thrown by Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, but on reflection, Lake didn't like the attention he generated. Lake told the Los Angeles Times that he reached out to Herbert to apologize. On a podcast hosted by Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, Lake laughed about how confident the Rams were heading into the game with the Chargers, seeing how much Herbert has been struggling this season. “He was throwing deli meat out there,” Lake said on the podcast. “He’s seeing ghosts. I don’t know what’s going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one.” Lake and St. Brown were high school teammates, and Lake said that in the moment, he just felt like he was joking around with an old friend. When he saw how far his comments spread, however, Lake felt bad that he came across as disrespecting an opponent. Lake said he texted Herbert but hasn't heard back from him. “I don’t know if he read it,” Lake said. “He probably says, ‘I don’t care about it anymore. I’m not trying to see this. It doesn’t matter. You said what you said.’ But at the same time I . . . felt like it was right for me to at least say,’ Hey, man, I didn’t mean it in any disrespectful way .’” Lake said he considers Herbert "a great quarterback" despite his struggles this season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ravens reportedly tell Derrick Henry they have "no intention" of trading him
summary: Ravens running back Derrick Henry's production has plummeted since quarterback Lamar Jackson was first injured before halftime in a Week 4 win over the Titans.
full_text: Ravens running back Derrick Henry's production has plummeted since quarterback Lamar Jackson was first injured before halftime in a Week 4 win over the Titans. And the Ravens have now lost four games in a row. After Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars, a clearly frustrated Henry (who rarely displays frustration publicly), said he hasn’t mentioned going elsewhere as the trade deadline looms. Now there's this, from Adam Schefter of ESPN: "The Ravens recently informed Henry that they have no intention of trading him , according to league sources." If "no intention" is used in that assertion in the same way that multiple teams have used "no intention" in the past, a trade remains possible. Because intentions can change. The Ravens traded for quarterback Jacoby Brissett in an effort to salvage a potential playoff season. Even after Thursday night's game (which was only the second Jacksonville win in Baltimore since 2000), the Ravens are 4-5 and very much alive for a playoff berth. In our view, the Ravens would trade Henry only if he made a passionate and compelling case to be traded — and if the Ravens are already considering moving on from the soon-to-be 33-year-old tailback after the 2026 season. Henry has two former head coaches on current playoff contenders. Former Titans coach Mike Vrabel leads the 5-3 Patriots. Former Ravens coach John Harbaugh runs the 4-2-1 Giants. The Patriots are without Treveyon Henderson, who will miss his second straight game after developing a sudden and unexplained illness. And the Giants have been linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. So unless "no intention" means "no way," it's still a possibility. At least until 4:00 p.m. ET arrives on Tuesday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Colts are in trade talks regarding QB Daniel Jones
summary: The list of "multiple teams" currently includes the Ravens (who pivoted elsewhere) and the Vikings.
full_text: The Indianapolis fire sale could indeed extend to the man who was supposed to become a franchise quarterback there. According to ESPNFL, the Colts have engaged in trade talks this week regarding Daniel Jones, speaking to "multiple teams." The precise language of the report identifies only one team as actually talking to the Colts. From the article, the Ravens "were one team to check in on Jones." The Ravens ultimately struck a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, whose plunge from No. 1 to No. 3 on the depth chart made it clear to the rest of the league that he was available. The only other team mentioned by name is the Vikings, and the report points only to "[s]peculation" involving Minnesota. (We've been “speculating” about it since the immediate aftermath of Sunday's loss by the Vikings in Detroit.) Past ESPNFL reporting on a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor ultimately listed five teams as talking to the Colts (Giants, Seahawks, Broncos, Packers, Vikings). The fact that other teams weren't mentioned as to Jones suggests that, frankly, there may not be other teams. Really, which current contender would want him? The Vikings are the only potential playoff team that checks the box as possibly needing a starter right now. And only the Vikings and Giants are contenders with which Jones has direct experience. (The Giants wouldn't want a Jones reunion, and Jones surely wouldn't want it, either.) That could change this weekend, obviously. One injury to a starter could alter the dynamics, spurring another contender to pick up the phone and make a push for Jones. The most memorable example of that came 15 years ago, when a broken collarbone to Raiders quarterback Jason Campbell prompted a quick deal for Bengals quarterback Carson Palmer, who had decided he didn't want to play for the team that had drafted him — and who had yet to report. Three years ago, Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins popped an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline, forcing the Vikings to scramble at the deadline to do a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Josh Dobbs. Absent a multi-week injury to a starting quarterback on a contender that doesn't believe its backup can hold down the fort, the Vikings may be the only team that wants Jones at the deadline. The preferences of Daniel Jones become a factor, too. If (as we firmly believe) he's not happy that the Colts folded the tents by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner after a 2-5 start that included an overtime loss to the Chiefs and a toe-to-toe battle with the then-unbeaten Vikings, Jones would have a clear interest in hopping to a contender. The Vikings wanted to keep Jones after the 2024 season. He opted to sign with the Colts in part because he saw a more realistic path to winning the job over 2023 first-rounder Anthony Richardson in Indianapolis than 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy in Minneapolis. If he's told that a return to Minnesota would include being installed immediately as QB1, he'd surely prefer that to a lost season with the Colts. Andd Jones has power over this process. Beyond the basic reality that no team wants a starting quarterback who doesn't want to play for it, the 2027 roster bonus and base salary that become fully guaranteed in March ($10.51 million) are currently guaranteed for injury. The ESPNFL article mentions that Jones could waive the injury guarantee in order to expedite a deal. The reverse of that (Jones refusing to waive the injury guarantee) means that Jones could block a trade, if avoiding a potential eight-figure guarantee for 2027 is a dealbreaker for his prospective employer. Our guess? Right now, only the Vikings currently have interest in Jones. And a trade for Jones becomes a very viable possibility if the Vikings lose to the Bills on Monday with Carson Wentz playing quarterback. Given the possibility that another team will emerge as a competitor to get Jones, it's also possible that the Vikings have already decided to trade for Jones after Monday night's game — win or lose — and that the two teams have agreed to keep it under wraps until Week 9 ends. Either way, if the oft-injured Jones plays on Sunday against the Cowboys and gets injured, that would kill any chance to trade him. That makes it important to monitor Sunday's game carefully. If the Colts apply a quick hook to Jones, it could mean that he's already gone.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Broncos are seeking a tight end trade, Cardinals rebuffed request for Trey McBride
summary: Denver would like to acquire a veteran tight end before Tuesday's trade deadline, but that tight end will apparently not be Arizona's Trey McBride.
full_text: Denver would like to acquire a veteran tight end before Tuesday's trade deadline, but that tight end will apparently not be Arizona's Trey McBride. The Broncos have checked in with multiple teams about potential tight ends they could trade for, and that included the Cardinals, who told the Broncos they're not interested in trading McBride , according to ESPN. McBride is 26 years old and under contract through 2029, so it's no surprise that the Cardinals see him as part of their future, although there's never any harm in one GM calling another to see if a player is available. If the Broncos thought there was any chance they could get him, it was smart to ask. The Broncos' top tight end, Evan Engram, has just 13 catches for 136 yards this season. Sean Payton would love to get more production out of the tight end position than that. It won't be a surprise if several more teams with potentially available veteran tight ends hear from the Broncos between now and Tuesday.
author: Michael David Smith

title: After career-low numbers in 2025, Justin Jefferson's production is even lower in 2026
summary: Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson had his worst season in 2025.
full_text: '' Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson had his worst season in 2025. When a great player like Jefferson has an off year, the hope is that he'll bounce back the next year. That hasn't happened. Jefferson's stats are actually worse across the board in 2026 than they were in 2025, when he seemed to have reached the bottom of what a player his caliber is capable of producing. Last year, Jefferson finished with a career-low 1,048 receiving yards. This year, heading into Week 9, Jefferson has just 335 receiving yards. Last year, Jefferson averaged a career-low 12.5 yards per catch. This year, Jefferson is averaging 12.0 yards per catch. Last year, Jefferson had a career-low 47 receiving first downs. This year, Jefferson has 17 receiving first downs. Last year, Jefferson averaged a career-low 4.9 catches per game. This year, Jefferson is averaging 4.7 catches per game. Last year, Jefferson averaged a career-low 61.6 receiving yards per game. This year, Jefferson is averaging 55.8 yards per game. The major question to ask is whether this means Jefferson has declined, or whether the blame goes to the Vikings' quarterbacks who haven't been able to get him the ball over the last two years. An answer to that question may come on Monday night against the Bills, when Carson Wentz starts in place of Kyler Murray, who has been announced as out with a hamstring injury. Jefferson's best game this year came in Week 1, when he had just two catches for 11 yards early on with Murray in the game, then caught six passes for 81 yards and two touchdowns from Wentz after Murray left with a concussion. Jefferson also had his best games last year catching passes from Wentz: Jefferson averaged 95.4 yards per game in the five games Wentz started in 2025, and averaged just 47.6 yards per game in the 12 games started by J.J. McCarthy and Max Brosmer. If Wentz and Jefferson connect for a big game on Monday night, it may spur Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell to decide Wentz is his quarterback going forward. If Wentz can't get the most out of Jefferson's playmaking abilities on Monday night, the Vikings may decide on Tuesday morning that it's time to go shopping for a new quarterback at the trade deadline.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Myles Garrett: Rams' opponents will have to pick their poison, me or Aaron Donald
summary: Garrett and Donald will play together for the first time on Sunday against the Commanders.
full_text: Rams defensive end Myles Garret and defensive tackle Aaron Donald will finally be on the field together Sunday in Washington, and Garrett says that's going to be bad news for opposing offenses for the rest of the season. Donald did not play in Week 1 because he was still ramping up for the season after returning from his two-year retirement, and Garret hasn't played since Week 1 because of knee surgery. Garrett said the two of them together, two multiple-time Defensive Player of the Year award winners side by side, will present a unique challenge for opposing offenses. "I think offenses really have to pick their poison. Who's going to be freed up this play? I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-one, so we'll have some fun," Garrett said. "Going into this season I never thought I'd have the chance, and as you all know he kept us in suspense for quite a while, so it was very exciting, and I'm looking forward to getting on the field and playing some real snaps with him." Garrett said his poor performance in Week 1 against the 49ers showed him he needed knee surgery, something he would have preferred to avoid. "I was frustrated after the game. I knew that wasn't me, and I was being hampered by something," Garrett said. "I didn't want to miss any time, but I had to be realistic about where I was physically, and I had to make the best choice for me and the team." But now Garrett is back, and he said he and Donald playing together can give the Rams an "elite defense" for the rest of the season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Patrick Mahomes is closing in on the record for most TD passes in a QB's first 10 years
summary: Mahomes has 325 career touchdown passes, counting the playoffs. Peyton Manning had 327 in his first 10 seasons.
full_text: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is three touchdown passes away from the NFL record for the most ever in a player's first 10 seasons. Mahomes, who is in his 10th NFL season, has 325 career touchdown passes, counting the playoffs. Only Peyton Manning, who had 327 touchdown passes in his first 10 years in the league, has had more. So if Mahomes throws for two touchdowns on Sunday against the Jets, he'll tie Manning's record. With three touchdowns, Mahomes will have the record all to himself. As a rookie, Mahomes played in only one game and didn't throw any touchdowns. In the eight and a half seasons since then, Mahomes has 279 touchdown passes in the regular season, and another 46 in the playoffs. Once Mahomes breaks the record, he's likely to own it for a long time. The only active quarterback who's closing in is Josh Allen, who is currently in his eighth NFL season and has 260 career touchdown passes. Allen has a chance of throwing for 68 touchdown passes in the next year and a half and moving ahead of Manning, but he's highly unlikely to finish next season ahead of whatever Mahomes' total is by the end of this season. This is a record Mahomes will own for a long time.
author: Michael David Smith

title: The Vikings could be ready to make a trade for a quarterback, if they lose Monday night
summary: Tuesday could become very interesting, absent a Carson Wentz-led win vs. the Bills.
full_text: Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz? Carson Wentz or Kyler Murray? The answer could be neither. This week's apparent soft benching of Murray, who has a hamstring injury that possibly wouldn't have kept him from playing if the Vikings had beaten the Lions on Sunday, gives Wentz a chance to beat the 6-1 Bills on Monday night. If he pulls it off, Wentz could keep the job for the remainder of the four-game gjallarhorn gauntlet that ends with trips to Wisconsin to play the Packers and Mexico to play the 49ers. If Wentz fails, the Vikings may mobilize. Immediately. The Vikings will have roughly 16 hours after Monday night's game ends to close a deal with another team for a quarterback. On Monday, we made the case for a trade for Colts quarterback Daniel Jones. As the week has unfolded, a variey of indications have emerged that it's a real possibility. Jones, who surely is dismayed by the Colts' decision to prematurely throw in the towel by trading away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Bucker, would likely welcome the chance to return to a team with which he spent a couple of months in 2024 — and to lead the effort to propel the neo-Purple People Eaters to the postseason. The other possibility would be to try to bring Kirk Cousins home. That would be more difficult. At 4-4, the Raiders are on the fringes of contention. Win or lose on Sunday at San Francisco, why disrupt something that's working? Cousins currently ranks third in passing yards with 2,124 and second in touchdown passes with 19. His passer rating of 101.4 is higher than Josh Allen's. Even if the Raiders would be inclined to move Cousins and ride with Fernando Mendoza, it would cost far less to get Jones than it would to get Cousins. Especially since the Colts may already be planning to cut Jones before a $4 million roster bonus comes due in March and $6.51 million of his $33.49 million salary becomes fully-guaranteed. With a new G.M. coming next year, why wouldn't the Colts want a clean slate? Doing so would wipe out $38 million in non-guaranteed cash for 2027. Trading Jones would result in getting value; cutting Jones would get them nothing. It may all come down to Monday night. If Minnesota wins, chances are nothing happens. If Minnesota loses, Tuesday could become a very interesting day.
author: Mike Florio

title: The Protect College Sports Act could be dead
summary: This week's midterm elections will dramatically reshuffle the deck in Congress.
full_text: '' This week's midterm elections will dramatically reshuffle the deck in Congress. And that could keep those who want the Protect College Sports Act from having the cards necessary to get it passed. The last, best hope for a Congressional bailout to the college sports system (at the expense of the athletes in the revenue-generating sports) comes in the upcoming six-week lame-duck session. The bill has cleared the Senate. The House of Representatives, which disbanded in the middle of September to block a push for the impeachment of U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, has done nothing with it. The question now becomes whether the short-timers in the House will muster the will to push their own version of the PSCA through to a successful vote. Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas), who co-sponsored the original bill, seems to realize that if it doesn't happen now it never will. “There is no realistic path to secure the same broad bipartisan support for a new bill in 2027 and beyond,” a spokesperson for the Senate Committee on Commerce, led by Cruz, told The Athletic . “Passing the Senate-approved bipartisan bill through the House and sending it to the President’s desk during the lame duck Congress gives House Republicans an opportunity to close out the 119th Congress with a significant win for President Trump, HBCUs, women’s sports, and student athletes. An attempt to amend it would be a surefire defeat for the colleges and fans counting on PCSA’s enactment.” At this point, do House Republicans want to give Trump a win? Right or wrong, those who won't be coming back in January surely believe they lost their bids for re-election because of him. If so, they'll feel no compulsion to spend time and effort on another presidential pet project at a time when the list of real issues that need to be addressed keeps growing. If anything, the House would pass an amended version that would require reconciliation while the clock on the 119th Congress ticks toward midnight. The fact that the Senate Commerce Committee regards even an attempt to amend the existing bill as a "surefire defeat" for the bill will make the current House members who soon will be former House members even more likely to say, "Why bother?"
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams listed Matthew Stafford with elbow injury because reporters asked about ice on it
summary: On Monday, reporters asked Rams coach Sean McVay about quarterback Matthew Stafford having ice on his throwing arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers.
full_text: On Monday, reporters asked Rams coach Sean McVay about quarterback Matthew Stafford having ice on his throwing arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers. On Wednesday, the Rams listed Stafford as having an elbow injury . Yes, there's a connection. “Really, it's because you guys asked me about it earlier in the week," McVay told reporters on Friday regarding the decision to disclose an elbow injury for Stafford. "It's more semantical than anything else. It's normal, like what he told you guys, but because you guys asked me about him having ice on his elbow. . . . He's been full, hasn't missed any sort of reps so normal management stuff that he's been doing over the last few years.” It conjures memories of the Patriots' one-time habit of listing former quarterback Tom Brady as "probable" with a "right shoulder" injury. That all started because he had ice on his shoulder in the locker room, reporters inquired, and the team decided to just put him on the injury report every week. Has the elbow situation affected Stafford's throwing? “I haven't seen any of that," McVay said. "I told you guys he'd be better equipped to talk about it. He's been a full participant, been awesome. He's spinning the ball. He's been able to activate all parts of the field with great timing, rhythm, and accuracy so he's been great.” So either he has an actual elbow injury that the Rams had been concealing, or he doesn't really have an elbow injury but they listed him as having one because reporters noticed ice on his arm and asked McVay about it. Neither explanation seems to reflect the true spirit of the injury report, which expects real injuries — and only real injuries — to be disclosed. Either Stafford has an elbow injury that was previously hidden or he doesn't have an elbow injury and the claim that he has one is a middle finger to the meddling reporters who were doing their jobs. Neither explanation is a preferred alternative to the unvarnished truth.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saints to have "chip on our shoulder" after Browns' "chirping"
summary: The Saints, like all teams, pay attention to the things said by their upcoming opponents.
full_text: ' The Saints, like all teams, pay attention to the things said by their upcoming opponents. Earlier this week, Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders seemed to make some less-than-flattering comments about the New Orleans defense. The New Orleans defense heard it, loud and clear. "We're gonna come in with a chip on our shoulder , for sure," Saints defensive end Carl Granderson said Friday. "You know, they been chirping a little bit. We heard what the quarterback . . . said. So, you know, we're [going to] come in hot and ready to play. . . . It's gonna be a good game, for sure. We're gonna come out with the [win]." Asked Wednesday by reporters whether he has had a chance to study the Saints defense and to explain what he has seen, Sanders flashed a broad smile. “Yeah, I’ve seen a lot," Sanders said. "When I smile, just know that means something. I’m maturing. I’m maturing. Like, I could have given a decent answer, but now I’m just going to smile whenever it’s just, like, some questions.” The better approach for Sanders would have been to project a poker face, and to give an answer that did nothing to attract the attention of the Saints' defense. So while he says he's maturing, the ultimate level of maturity would consist of providing the most vanilla answer possible, praising the Saints and explaining that it will be a major challenge to beat them. Instead, a Browns player has provided the next opponent — for the second straight week — with a little extra incentive.
author: Mike Florio

title: Drew Rosenhaus after Brandon Aiyuk's meeting with 49ers: "To be continued"
summary: First session ends with no resolution.
full_text: ' It has become abundantly clear that the NFL is delaying the reinstatement of 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list. It has also become abundantly clear that the 49ers hope to squeeze some cash out of Aiyuk before the league lets him back in. It's no surprise, then, that Friday's sit-down between Aiyuk, agent Drew Rosenhaus, and the 49ers did not resolve the situation. "Hey, guys," Rosenhaus told a group of reporters who had staked out the Friday meeting. " To be continued . We don't have any further statements right now. But when we do, we'll let you know." The situation seems pretty simple. Aiyuk arguably owes the 49ers upwards of $13 million. It's one thing for the 49ers to have the ability to chase him around for the cash; it's another for the NFL and the 49ers to delay his reinstatement to the league until he wires the funds. That seems to be precisely where things stand. And the question becomes whether Aiyuk will be willing to strike a deal with the 49ers in order to secure the ability to return to the NFL, with another team.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFC North has 17-3 record against non-NFC North teams
summary: The NFC North is the best division in the NFL.
full_text: ' The NFC North is the best division in the NFL. As evidenced by how the teams of the NFC North have performed against the rest of the league. The Vikings, Bears, Lions, and Packers have a combined record of 17-3 against non-NFC North teams. Via NBC Sports research, the ensuing 85 percent success rate is the highest by any division in the NFL since the 1970 merger. In theory, all four teams of the NFC North could make the playoffs. To do that, however, each would have to finish higher in the wild-card pecking order than the Rams and the Seahawks (assuming the 49ers win the NFC West). This week, two teams of the NFC North have an easier path to victory than the others; the Bears host the Buccaneers and the Lions visit the Dolphins. For the Packers (who play the Patriots in New England) and the Vikings (who play the Bills on Monday night), it will be harder to keep pushing 17-3 to 21-3.
author: Mike Florio

title: In defending his willingness to spend, Jerry Jones may have admitted to tampering
summary: On Friday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tried to reverse the perception/reality that he deliberately underspends on coaches.
full_text: On Friday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tried to reverse the perception/reality that he deliberately underspends on coaches. His explanation regarding the willingness to spend included an important admission. "I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. Unless he was referring to college coaches (or high-school coaches), that's tampering. Period. End of discussion. It could be false — an effort to bolster the idea that, yes, he's willing to spend. Still, the effort to put out the frugality fire he started on Tuesday by ridiculously claiming there’s no correlation between coaching pay and winning included a nonchalant concession that he has tried to pry NFL coaches away from their current teams, in blatant violation of the rules. Will the NFL look into this one? Probably not. Because the league office surely realizes, as the rest of us do, that Jerry was simply saying whatever he had to say to lessen the impact of the accidental truth he told on Tuesday regarding a deliberate reluctance to do whatever he needs to do to make his team as good as it can be.
author: Mike Florio

title: 2026 NFL Trade Deadline live updates: Tracker, deals, news, rumors, analysis
summary: Jeffery Simmons, DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson and more big-name NFL players are on the move.
full_text: '' The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, and PFT has you covered with news and analysis of every trade, potential trade, rumor of a trade and trade that won’t be happening. Here’s what’s happening on the NFL trade front: Jacoby Brissett is headed to Baltimore : The Ravens and Cardinals announced a deal sending the veteran quarterback and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Ravens for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick. Derrick Henry says he's not thinking about changing teams : The Ravens star expressed a desire to help the team improve after a fourth-straight loss. Jonathan Taylor wants to know where he'll finish the season : Taylor said no one likes uncertainty when asked about talk that the Colts will trade him. Chargers say they're not trading Khalil Mack : Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said, " I want Khalil Mack to be here and Khalil Mack wants to be here ." author: Michael David Smith

title: Brandon Aiyuk: I’m back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated
summary: The wide receiver and his agent are meeting with the 49ers about Aiyuk's future.
full_text: ' Brandon Aiyuk will not play for the 49ers again, but his future is in question. The wide receiver arrived at the team's business offices in a van with his agent Friday afternoon to meet with the 49ers and presumably negotiate a resolution. "Obviously, Brandon is here to meet with the team," Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk's agent, said before the meeting, via video from David Lombardi of the San Francisco Standard. "Fortunately, he's feeling good physically. He’s healthy . He's ready to get back to work. Don't really have any comment about where he's going to play. We'll keep that between us and the Niners. But obviously we're here with all the right intentions." Aiyuk last played in a game on Oct. 20, 2024, when he tore the ACL and MCL in his right knee. The relationship between the team and the player fell apart after that, and the 49ers voided the guaranteed money due to his unwillingness to rehab at their facility. The 49ers placed him on the reserve/left squad list on Dec. 13, 2025. Rosenhaus filed a reinstatement request on Oct. 27, but the NFL still hasn’t reinstated him. "Nice to see you all," Aiyuk said. "I’m feeling great, feeling healthy. It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process. But I’m back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League." 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier in the day he "[couldn't] care less" how the meeting went since " it’s been over for our football team for a long time."
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams unexpectedly rule out TE Terrance Ferguson
summary: Rams coach Sean McVay said Friday that Terrance Ferguson would return Sunday barring a setback.
full_text: Rams coach Sean McVay said Friday that Terrance Ferguson would return Sunday barring a setback. The Rams released their injury report and had ruled out Ferguson. Ferguson, who was working his way back from an ankle injury, is now listed with a hamstring injury, too. It's an indication he injured his hamstring at Friday's practice. He was limited in practice all week. Ferguson injured his ankle in Week 3 and went on injured reserve Oct. 2. He returned to practice this week. Tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable, which could leave Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and Max Klare as the available tight ends.
author: Charean Williams

title: Amon-Ra St. Brown listed as questionable for Lions
summary: The Lions ruled out several starters for Sunday's game against the Dolphins and they're still deciding the status of their top wide receiver.
full_text: The Lions ruled out several starters for Sunday's game against the Dolphins and they're still deciding the status of their top wide receiver. Amon-Ra St. Brown was limited in practice on Friday for the third straight day because of a rib injury. St. Brown, who has not missed a game since 2023, is listed as questionable to play. Center Cade Mays (ankle), cornerback D.J. Reed (hip), and defensive end DJ Wonnum (concussion) have all been ruled out. All three players missed practice all week. Linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) was formally ruled out as well. Safety Kerby Joseph (knee) got in another week of practice, but will not be activated from injured reserve this weekend. Running backs Jacob Saylors (neck) and Sione Vaki (ankle) are listed as questionable, so the Lions may be shorthanded behind Jahmyr Gibbs this Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Texans rule out S Reed Blankenship, RB David Montgomery
summary: The Texans ruled out safety Reed Blankenship (hand/concussion) and running back David Montgomery (groin) for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
full_text: The Texans ruled out safety Reed Blankenship (hand/concussion) and running back David Montgomery (groin) for Sunday's game against the Chargers. Coach DeMeco Ryans said earlier in the week that Montgomery would miss his third consecutive game. He is week-to-week but has not practiced since his injury in Week 5. Woody Marks has taken over as the team's workhorse back. Blankenship will miss his second consecutive game. He underwent hand surgery after the Week 6 victory over the Jaguars and still hasn't cleared concussion protocol. M.J. Stewart will again start opposite Calen Bullock. Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (groin), defensive back Jalen Pitre (shoulder) and offensive tackles Braden Smith (ankle) and Blake Fisher (thumb) have no injury designation.
author: Charean Williams

title: Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Christian Kirk ruled out
summary: The 49ers ruled out three wide receivers and have another who is questionable.
full_text: The 49ers ruled out three wide receivers and have another who is questionable. Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) will not play against the Raiders. Demarcus Robinson (ankle) is questionable. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Kirk injured his meniscus earlier this week but provided no details. Evans has not played since Oct. 19 when he aggravated his Achilles. Samuel has not played since Oct. 11 when he strained his hamstring. Evans has 27 receptions for 420 yards and three touchdowns, and Samuel has 16 catches for 206 yards and three touchdowns. Safety Marques Sigle (ankle), defensive back Upton Stout (shoulder), defensive back Siran Neal (knee/foot) and cornerback Nate Hobbs (adductor) are questionable. Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee/calf) has no injury designation, meaning he is expected to play for the first time since injuring his calf in Week 3.
author: Charean Williams

title: S Talanoa Hufanga questionable for Sunday's game

Hufanga had a second consecutive limited practice on Friday after missing Wednesday's session. Until Thursday, he had played or practiced since his injury in Week 5 against the Chargers. Wide receiver Pat Bryant (ankle) is also listed as questionable, but he was listed as a full participant for the third consecutive day. Bryant had his 21-day return-to-practice window opened this week. The Broncos will have to activate him from injured reserve on Saturday to make him eligible to play this week. He has not played since Week 4 against the 49ers. Outside linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hip) was added to the team's practice report on Friday as a full participant. He is also questionable for the game. title: Kyle Shanahan on Brandon Aiyuk's meeting with 49ers: I couldn't care less
summary: The wide receiver and his agent will meet with team officials later today.
full_text: ' 49ers team officials will meet with wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk and his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, at the team's business offices in an hour. Coach Kyle Shanahan said it has nothing to do with him. “No clue. Your guess is as good as mine," Shanahan told reporters Friday when asked what he expected out of the meeting. "I [couldn't] care less." Aiyuk last played in a game on Oct. 20, 2024, when he tore the ACL and MCL in his right knee. The relationship between the team and the player fell apart after that, and the 49ers voided the guaranteed money due to his unwillingness to rehab at their facility. The 49ers placed him on the reserve/left squad list on Dec. 13, 2025. Rosenhaus filed a reinstatement request on Oct. 27, but the NFL still hasn’t reinstated him. The only certainty is Aiyuk will never play for the 49ers again. "It's been over for our football team for a long time," Shanahan said. "So, I don't hear much except questions about him today, but not too big of a deal for me to answer. "I look at this as zero to do with our football team. Anything that has zero to do with our football team, especially during the season, I will give zero thoughts to."
author: Charean Williams

title: RB Cam Skattebo doubtful, but WR Malik Nabers has no injury designation
summary: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said he would be ready to go despite missing Thursday's practice with a knee injury.
full_text: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said he would be ready to go despite missing Thursday's practice with a knee injury. Indeed, the team's Friday injury report confirms that. Nabers does not have a designation after returning to full participation on Friday. He was not on the injury report Wednesday. It’s unknown whether Nabers' current knee issue is the same knee as the torn ACL he had in his right knee last season. Coach John Harbaugh called it “an in-season type thing.” “It's not an issue. He'll be full-go for the game," Harbaugh said. Nabers leads the team with 48 receptions for 605 yards and two touchdowns. Running back Cam Skattebo, though, is doubtful with a hamstring injury. He did not practice all week. Skattebo leads the team with 98 carries for 418 yards and two touchdowns. He has added 11 catches for 76 yards. The Giants signed running back Eric Gray to the practice squad as insurance earlier this week. Wide receiver Charlie Jones (hand) is questionable. He has two catches for 66 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Brandon Aiyuk plans to meet with 49ers at team's business offices, not team facility
summary: 49ers tight end George Kittle was right, sort of.
full_text: ' 49ers tight end George Kittle was right, sort of. Receiver Brandon Aiyuk won't " get in " the team facility on Friday, because he's not trying to. Per agent Drew Rosenhaus, Friday's meeting will happen at the team's business offices and not at the team's practice facility. That makes the session not a formal reporting-for-duty by Aiyuk, in the hopes of forcing the team's hand. As explained earlier today, the NFL still hasn’t reinstated Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list — even though Rosenhaus filed the request on October 27. Instead, it's a meeting presumably aimed at negotiating a resolution to the situation. The 49ers pushed to reporters on Thursday night the idea that Aiyuk's return to the NFL is tied to the $13 million the team believes he owes in previously paid signing bonus. That shouldn't be part of the analysis as to whether he's reinstated by the league, whether the 49ers put him on the roster again, and/or whether the 49ers cut him. But they're making it an issue, because they can tie his ability to play to his willingness to wire the disputed funds to the team. So that's what's happening. The brakes already have been applied to what should have been an administrative and automatic process. The league and the 49ers are working together to help the team get money back from Aiyuk before Aiyuk is permitted to get back into the league. Then there's the fact that an active arrest warrant is pending for Aiyuk, arising from a speeding incident. The business meeting could potentially be interrupted by an attempt to enforce a specific item of police business.

title: Nick Sirianni admits that he misled reporters about quarterback situation
summary: Instead of covering up one lie with another lie, Sirianni opted to tell the truth that he hadn't.
full_text: How do you know when a football coach is lying? If he's good at it, you don't. Because they all do. Particularly in so-called "must-lie" situations. There's an art to it. A way to conceal a lie with another lie. On Friday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted not to lie about the fact that he lied on Monday when he told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee would not be benched. " Tanner’s our guy ," Sirianni said. "We're not making any changes there." On Wednesday, the Eagles made a change there, elevating Joe Milton over McKee. The move was announced after Sirianni had his midweek media availability, which prevented him from being asked questions about the change in position from "Tanner's our guy" to "Tanner's not our guy." On Friday, Sirianni finally faced the music regarding his comments from Monday. In lieu of coming up with an explanation premised on the idea that what he said was true when he said it and circumstances changed, Sirianni surprisingly admitted that he wasn't telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth to reporters and, in turn, the fans. "I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute," Sirianni said. "Again, I'm not real shy with you guys. I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y'all have to do, but I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I'm always going to protect the team first and foremost. "Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there's a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside." In an industry where the truth is only told when it's coincidental to strategic interests, it's jarring that Sirianni told the truth that he was lying. It would have been easy to say, "We took a more careful look at the situation after Monday." Or, even more simply, "We changed our mind. Shit happens." Instead, Sirianni opted to say, essentially, "Bullshit happens." Instead of bothering to concoct a cover story regarding his lie, he said, essentially, "Yeah. I lied. I'll do it whenever I feel like I have to." That's the most important thing to remember. Coaches lie whenever they feel like they have to. Despite that fact, reporters and fans routinely take their words at face value, swallowing the bullshit while saying, "Thank you, sir, may I have another?" So thank you, Nick, for making my job a little easier. In my first week of law school, one of the professors said, "The most important thing I can do for you is to give you a good crap filter." Because crap is everywhere. Usually, the people spewing it don't admit it. When they do, it provides a tangible reminder as to whatever they say in the future. For Sirianni, that's the most problematic aspect of his decision to tell the truth about lying. There's now an "Exhibit A" to which anyone and everyone can point as to anything and everything he says when assessing whether he's being straight with reporters and, in turn, with fans.

title: NFL week 9 anytime TD best bets: Look for Jonah Coleman and Joe Milton III to find end zone
summary: Target strong value in the red zone this week with five picks, including rookie runner Jonah Coleman against a reeling Panthers defense
full_text:
This week in the NFL , Shedeur Sanders will look to win his first start of the season against the New Orleans Saints , the Joe Milton III era begins in Philadelphia; we have an epic interconference battle in New England between the Patriots and Packers , and the Chicago Bears will try to win their fourth-straight game in prime time against Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Last week we hit on Braelon Allen (+125) and Brian Thomas Jr . (+330). Let's see what we have cooking up for Week 9.
Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a first-year player.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Rookie running back Jonah Coleman may have stolen the Denver Broncos ' RB1 job during their Week 8 come-from-behind victory against the Kansas City Chiefs . He rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, and also led the team in receiving with 63 yards on four receptions. Coleman handled the game-winning drive all by himself, as he took a short pass 51 yards to the Chiefs' 5-yard line, then punched in a touchdown on the very next play. It feels like the Broncos' opponent this week in the Carolina Panthers could be on the downswing with all of their injuries on the offensive line and in the secondary. This Carolina defense has allowed a whopping 42.7 points per game at home this season.
I've cashed on this two weeks in a row, and I'm going to take it again this Sunday. In his two games this season, Josh Jacobs has scored three touchdowns. He hasn't looked like an elite playmaker, having rushed for just 75 yards on 32 carries. In fact, the Packers have the fewest rushing yards (485) by a winning team through eight games in NFL history, according to CBS Sports Research. Still, Jacobs is getting touches in the red zone.
San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a touchdown in the loss to the Atlanta Falcons his last time out, and caught a pass for a loss of four yards.
I don't know if the 49ers blow out the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, but I do know the Raiders have allowed an NFL-high 35.5 points per game over their past five games, and are allowing an NFL-high 6.1 yards per play. It's bad. I think Black finding the end zone is an interesting flier.
The Bears are rolling, having scored 30 points with 350 yards of total offense over three straight games. Luther Burden III is Caleb Williams ' top receiver with 42 catches on 56 targets, but tight end Colston Loveland is right behind him with 33 catches on 51 targets. He's found the end zone twice in the last three games. I'll take him to find pay dirt during a red-zone possession against the Bucs.
Joe Milton III will be making his first professional start this week, and while I don't know if he's one of the best players in the NFL, I think he can be one of the most fun. Milton may have the strongest arm in the NFL, and is more athletic than you think.
In his NFL debut for the Patriots back during the 2024 season, Milton completed 22 of 29 passes for 241 yards and a touchdown. He also rushed 10 times for 16 yards and another touchdown. I think he likes to get out and scramble when the situation allows for it. Maybe that comes in the red zone.
Milton is one of those tantalizing talents where you just wonder if he could actually be a starting quarterback someday. I'm excited to watch him.
With Joe Milton getting a chance to start it's a good time for us to all remember THE PASS pic.twitter.com/WNYd7j9DRd

title: Chargers not interested in Khalil Mack trade, will retain top offensive players despite 0-7 record, per report
summary: The winless Chargers will stick to the status quo
full_text:
The only winless team in the NFL may stand firm at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Despite their deeply disappointing start to the season, the Los Angeles Chargers reportedly have no interest in moving their perceived top trade candidates. According to ESPN , the front office made it clear to other teams that edge rusher Khalil Mack will remain a Charger at the deadline, and any questions regarding quarterback Justin Herbert and wide receiver Ladd McConkey were met with "hard nos."
If the Chargers were to make a deal by Tuesday, Mack would be perhaps the least surprising trade piece considering he is on an expiring contract and continues to play disruptive football from the edge rusher position, which is always in demand. But Los Angeles has always been steadfast in its desire to keep the future Hall of Famer in town through the end of his deal. Mid-round draft capital would be a reasonable return for the 35-year-old , but instead the Chargers repeatedly shut down outside interest in one of their top defensive assets.
"I want Khalil Mack here," coach Jim Harbaugh said this week . "Khalil Mack wants to be here. He's one of the pillars of our team."
It is less surprising that Los Angeles put a fence around Herbert and McConkey since they could remain building blocks for whatever kind of rebuild the franchise undertakes. Herbert remains under team control through 2029, and McConkey's rookie deal runs through the end of next season. When the offense is non-dysfunctional, they are standout players.
The obvious issue, however, is that the offense is dysfunctional this season. Herbert threw more interceptions (10) than any other quarterback in the NFL over the first eight weeks, and his 69.3 passer rating is second-worst only to Daniel Jones among qualifying signal-callers. McConkey is on pace for his least productive season as a pro with only 17 catches across six games.
Moving on from those offensive weapons would likely require the Chargers to sell low, because the offense's overall woes have cast a shadow over both players. That appears to be a non-starter.
The Chargers reportedly do not like the message of giving up on this season. But at 0-7 and with more of their losses coming by more than one possession than not, the hole they dug themselves into over the first two months of the campaign is deeper than that of any other team. There is very little to play for the rest of the way.
Los Angeles is opposed to trading its most valuable tools, but by holding onto them, it is declining to cash in on the potential draft picks it would receive in return. For a team that is clearly not equipped to contend in the near future, rebuilding through the draft would be a logical step forward. Instead, it will keep intact a core that has not won a playoff game in the Harbaugh era.
Player personnel is not the only part of this operation that remains unchanged, either. Harbaugh retained offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel through the bye week, which also came as a surprise since his system is the least productive in the NFL. No team averages fewer points per game than the Chargers at 14.1. The only tangible change to the offense has come in the form of McDaniel moving from the sideline to the box for Week 9.
If the definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results, then the Chargers -- by way of keeping their roster intact and declining to make changes on the coaching staff -- fit that bill.

title: NFL trade deadline: Four Eagles, two more Colts and a starting QB included among top candidates
summary: Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor, Kirk Cousins and more could fetch returns at the trade deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than two weeks away. That means the hot stove will heat up considerably fairly soon. We've already seen multiple high-profile deals this season, with Joey Porter Jr . heading to the Cowboys , Marvin Harrison Jr . heading to the Texans , Quenton Nelson heading to the Seahawks , DeForest Bucker landing with the 49ers and Jeffery Simmons being traded to the Bears , and we could see several more in the coming days, given how wide open the league appears to be at the moment.
With that in mind, we wanted to take a look at some of the top targets who could be on the move. We ranked the top situations that bear the most watching, but with a twist. Some of them are team-wide, meaning there are multiple targets that interested teams could pursue over the next two weeks. There are 25 targets in all. (The Nelson, Buckner and Simmons deals make us 3-for-3 on predicting players that could be dealt, from the original list below. The list has since been updated.)
So without further ado, here's the list...
Saquon Barkley's contract, with all the various option bonuses included, makes dealing with him somewhat financially complicated, but given the Eagles ' struggles, his age, and the fact that teams are looking for explosiveness at running back these days, he makes sense as a target for needy teams. His current injury situation muddies the picture a bit, but that could be cleared up in the coming days and weeks as he gets further away from the hamstring pull.
Moro Ojomo is in the final year of his rookie contract. The Eagles just paid big money to two defensive tackles ( Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis ), so they probably can't afford to keep Ojomo around. He's 25 years old and has shown production upside with 6 sacks last season.
If the Eagles want to get aggressive, they can consider dealing both him and Nolan Smith , whose fifth-year option they picked up for next season but who they probably can't afford to keep in the longer term. Smith is more of a force in the run game than as a pass rusher, but that could still be valuable for teams that need help on the edge.
Dallas Goedert , meanwhile, signed a renegotiated contract with the Eagles this past offseason and is carrying only a $1.3 million base salary. He's not the most dynamic tight end these days, but he's a reliable pass-catcher and blocker, and any team that needs an additional tight end (teams love multi-tight end sets these days) could get interested for a small price.
Nelson is already on the move, traded to the Seahawks for a pair of draft picks. Bucker is gone, too, having been sent back to the 49ers after seven years away.
Jonathan Taylor is one of the best running backs in the NFL and has been able to remain productive even while the Colts ' offense has fallen apart around him. (He's only at 4.2 yards per carry, but he's carrying a 55% rushing success rate, per Pro-Football-Reference.) He's the type of explosive back who can change an offense in the way Kenneth Walker III did for the Chiefs . The contract isn't prohibitive for trade purposes, as the Colts would incur only $10 million in dead money next year if they move him. DeForest Buckner has also been traded away .
Josh Downs has reportedly requested a trade away from Indianapolis, and with the wide receiver in the final year of his rookie contract, the Colts should seriously consider moving him if they're not going to give him a new deal this offseason. He hasn't been particularly productive this year due to Daniel Jones ' struggles, but he's been a per-route star in prior years, so he could help a team in need of receiver depth.
Simmons has already been dealt, heading to the Bears for two first-rounders and more .
Amani Hooker is a very good, very versatile safety (he's played 232 snaps in the box, 127 as a deep safety and 56 as a slot corner so far this year), and those are valuable around the NFL. He still has three years left on his contract, including 2026, so there is a team-control aspect that would be valuable to a potentially acquiring team.
Tony Pollard is in the final year of his deal with only a $6.7 million base salary. He's 29 years old, but if you look under the hood, the numbers show he's actually running pretty well so far this season. He's 10th in yards after contact per attempt among the 39 running backs with 50-plus carries, for example, according to Tru Media. He's also 12th in explosive run rate. He can still play, and help a team in need of a committee back.
Calvin Ridley has completely fallen out of favor in Tennessee and could potentially help a team in need of depth-chart wide receiver help.
Khalil Mack is on a one-year deal with an $8 million base salary. He's got three sacks in six games and has played 71% of the Chargers ' defensive snaps. He's not going to be the player he once was, but any team in need of a rotational pass rusher should give the Chargers a call to see if they can get him for a late pick.
Tuli Tuipulotu only has two sacks in the Chargers' six games, but a deeper look at the numbers reveals a player playing better than that. He's 23rd in pressure rate among 148 players with 100 or more pass-rush snaps, according to Tru Media, and 18th in havoc play rate. He's still just 24 years old and you can get out ahead of his free agency by acquiring him now.
Derwin James , like Jeffery Simmons, recently signed a contract extension, so it would be somewhat surprising to see him get dealt. But he's 31 years old, the Chargers are terrible, and he's one of their most valuable assets. His base salaries for the next three years are also pretty high ($17.5 million, $24.6 million and $21.5 million), so the return might not be as much as the Chargers would be looking for.
Quentin Johnston only has 8 catches for 165 scoreless yards this season, and he's seemingly been surpassed in the target pecking order. He also has an $18 million salary for next season after the Chargers picked up his fifth-year option. So the return is likely to be low, but it's hard to imagine that L.A. wants to keep him around.
Donte Jackson is in the final year of his deal with only a $6 million base salary. He could be of help to any team in need of a cornerback, and there are always teams that need help in the defensive backfield. If the Chargers actually decide to sell, he seems like one of the more likely candidates to move.
Budda Baker has base salaries of $14.4 million and $16.1 million this year and next, but he's a valuable enough player to make those price tags worth it. He's extremely versatile and can play both the run and the pass, whether lined up deep or in the box. He's 30 years old and still likely has several quality seasons left under his belt. The Cardinals aren't going to contend for the postseason, and Baker is their best asset for future value.
Josh Sweat is having a down year, both sack-wise (2 in 7 games) and in terms of his pressure rate (7.9%). And his contract doesn't exactly make that type of production attractive. But his track record over the long term, up to and including last year, is much more impressive, and teams could bet that he has a bounce-back in a more favorable environment. He probably wants a new contract, but that could be worked out once you see him play for your team.
Win over the Jets notwithstanding, the Dolphins look like arguably the worst team in the league this season. Zach Sieler , though, remains a quality player. He hasn't been at his best this season (nobody on the Dolphins has), but we've seen high upside as both a run defender and a pass rusher from the defensive interior. If you can tap back into that, his base salaries over the next few years are very affordable ($44.5 million from 2027 through 2029, none of which is guaranteed).
Jordyn Brooks , like Jeffery Simmons and Derwin James, recently signed an extension. But his deal actually made him easier to trade and gave the Dolphins the benefit of selling to an acquiring team, knowing they'd have Brooks…
author: Jared Dubin

title: Cowboys should consider trading George Pickens: 5 logical destinations at NFL trade deadline
summary: Pickens received only four targets in Dallas' historic collapse against Arizona, adding urgency to the Cowboys' decision before the NFL trade deadline
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Shortly after Chad Ryland 's game-winning field goal went through the uprights to seal a 33-30 comeback, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens flew down the hallway and into the locker room by himself. No other teammate, coach, or staff member moved faster to get into the locker room and out of AT&T Stadium after Dallas made ugly history with its blown 14-point lead.
Pickens first one to the lockers, jogged down the tunnel before most media could even set up @1053thefan pic.twitter.com/RVab4T1c5M
Pickens' lack of targets was glaring. CeeDee Lamb led the way with 11 targets on Sunday while tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford was second with five targets. Pickens caught two passes for 48 yards. Four targets in a game simply isn't enough.
Pickens hasn't been bad this season: his 533 yards receiving rank as the 15th most in the NFL in 2026, just behind Trey McBride and just in front of Garrett Wilson (527) and Ja'Marr Chase (492). He is still on pace to exceed 1,100 receiving yards, but it regularly feels like the Cowboys are leaving production out on the field. Since Schottenheimer blamed Pickens' lack of vigor for run blocking for the team's struggling offense in a loss to the Green Bay Packers, he has 10 targets across the last two games.
"If I had the answer, we'd get him involved. I'm not trying to be rude or whatever it is, but he made some plays. Anytime the ball went his way, he came up with them. He had the one, unfortunately came back for a holding," quarterback Dak Prescott said. ... "I'm not sure about even how many targets he had. As I told y'all before, I go through the reads. [I] try to throw it to the open guy and stay consistent and true to that. And so, I've got to go back and look at the film and see if I missed him, see if we could have went to him more, see if we could have went to CeeDee more. I feel like it was a game that CeeDee didn't have as many catches as per usual, but we still had a chance to win and should have won it."
With the NFL trade deadline coming up in eight days on Nov. 10 and the Cowboys off to a 3-5 start and appearing to be going nowhere, it would make sense for Dallas to field trade calls for Pickens. He is playing out the franchise tag, and he will command near-top-of-the-market value on his second multi-year NFL contract. Dallas will also have to deal with balancing cornerback Joey Porter Jr. 's contract situation, since he, too, is set to be a free agent after the season.
After trading away draft capital to get Porter Jr. and Quinnen Williams, Dallas could use some additional ammunition in its 2027 NFL Draft war chest. So who could be blowing up owner/general manager Jerry Jones' phone for Pickens if word leaks out that they will listen to trade calls for their 25-year-old Pro Bowl wideout? Here is a look at five potential landing spots.
Jerry Jones has shown he doesn't care about sending a young star player to a non-divisional rival: he traded Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers . The pairing of the 49ers and Pickens makes too much sense.
San Francisco is the NFC's top seed through the first eight weeks of the season, and they have $34.98 million in cap space, the third most in the entire league, per OverTheCap.com. There are no financial barriers to this deal.
Plus, they have a glaring need for Pickens given all their wide receiver injuries. Both Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) were ruled out of their last game played in Week 7. Three wide receivers are on their injured reserve list.
Lastly, the 49ers are all in for 2026 because of their aging core. Christian McCaffrey is 30, Evans is 33, Samuel is 30, George Kittle is 33, Kyle Juszcyk is 35, Trent Williams is 38 and DeForest Buckner is 32. Both Fred Warner and Nick Bosa are healthy right now, but they're both 29 with extensive injury histories.
The Chiefs failed to score a game-winning touchdown after having a second-and-goal at the one with 15 seconds left, and Kansas City was outscored 15-0 in the fourth quarter of their narrow 28-24 road loss against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. You know who could have made a significant difference for quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the fourth quarter in Week 8? The 6-foot-3, 200-pound Pickens.
Kenneth Walker III is starting to lose a little steam after being heavily relied upon to carry the Chiefs' offense on his back. After averaging 133 rushing yards per game and 6.3 yards per carry with six rushing touchdowns in Kansas City's first five games of the season, Walker III is now averaging 52.5 rushing yards per game and 3.0 yards per carry without a touchdown in the last two games.
That's because the Chiefs' passing game requires Travis Kelce to be their No. 1 target, something that isn't a sustainable formula over the course of an 18-week season and beyond. Also, it would be incredibly foolish to waste the rest of Mahomes' glory years. The three-time Super Bowl MVP quarterback is 31, but he hasn't been the same high-flying passer that he was with a true No. 1 wide receiver like Tyreek Hill. Without Hill since 2022, Mahomes' production has taken a notable dip.
Average air yards per pass attempt
* Ranks among 37 qualified quarterbacks since 2022
The Buffalo Bills are the AFC's No. 1 seed through the first eight weeks, and they are always in win-now mode with Josh Allen . Yes, the Bills traded for DJ Moore , but he is probably best as Buffalo's No. 2 receiver on a Super Bowl team. He missed Buffalo's last two games with a shoulder injury prior to returning in Week 8, and he hyperextended his knee in the Bills' 36-10 beatdown of the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens .
Allen hasn't had a true WR1 since the 2024 Stefon Diggs trade. Pickens could help him become the league's most efficient passer. That would probably be enough for the Bills to perhaps win their first Super Bowl in franchise history.
The Las Vegas Raiders trading for Pickens would be a case of taking care of the now and the later. The Kirk Cousins-led Raiders are 4-4 and just one game out of the AFC's No. 7 seed. Giving Cousins, whose 19 passing touchdowns rank as the second most in the NFL, Pickens to pair with Brock Bowers could really make Klint Kubiak's offense pop.
Among the players officially listed as wide receivers on the Raiders' roster, Tre Tucker , a 2023 third-round pick, is the best they have. He could also help accelerate Fernando Mendoza's long-term development. Pickens is just two years older than the 23-year-old Mendoza, so the quarterback could spend the bulk of his career with a high-caliber wide receiver in addition to the 23-year-old Bowers at tight end.
Perhaps living in Las Vegas would dull the novelty of going out on The Strip that Pickens and Lamb experienced when they visited for "Monday Night Football" last season.
Despite being 6-1 and the No. 2 seed in the NFC, the Minnesota Vikings have the sixth-lowest scoring offense (20.0 points per game) in the entire NFL. Their lack of rhythm in the passing game is a major reason for that, as their Kyler Murray-quarterbacked passing attack is averaging the second-fewest passing yards per game (165.6) in the entire NFL.
Yes, Minnesota has 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Justin Jefferson and former first-round pick Jordan Addison at wide receiver, but its offense could clearly use another weapon to help Murray find his groove as a Viking. They have been rumored to be in pursuit of Jonathan Taylor , but perhaps Pickens could also help fix the issues on the offensive side of the ball.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Frustrated Derrick Henry responds to trade rumors, Ravens not expected to deal him, per report
summary: Henry was not a happy camper after Baltimore's fourth straight setback
full_text:
After a 4-1 start, the Baltimore Ravens have now lost four straight following Thursday night's lopsided loss to the visiting Jacksonville Jaguars . The Ravens' current plight raised questions about Derrick Henry's future in Baltimore ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
A clearly frustrated Henry fielded questions after Thursday night's loss, and he gave a candid response when directly asked about his future with the Ravens.
"I'm not mentioning me going anywhere else," he said . "I'm saying let's go back to work, try to get better and turn this around."
The stance on a potential Henry trade is not exclusive to the running back himself. According to ESPN , the Ravens are not expected to trade him during the season, and the front office informed him that it has no intentions of doing so. There has reportedly never been any consideration of a deal.
The Ravens have lost four straight games and Derrick Henry is frustrated pic.twitter.com/mpkdiTIIuI
At this point, Henry remains focused on doing what he can to help the Ravens turn their season around. But while his mindset is admirable, there's not much Henry can do to help fix Baltimore's current issues.
Even if Jacoby Brissett plays well, it's going to be hard for the Ravens to make up ground in the AFC North. Baltimore is currently last in the division; they trail the first-place Steelers by 2.5 games. The Ravens are currently three spots out of the AFC's final wild-card spot.
When you add in Lamar Jackson's uncertain future with the team , it might make sense for Baltimore to begin rebuilding now rather than delay the inevitable.
There would have been no shortage of offers if the Ravens decided to trade Henry, who on Thursday night moved into seventh on the NFL's career rushing list. The Vikings , Giants , Patriots, and Packers are among the NFL's playoff-contending teams that could use help at the running back position.
Henry would have figured to command significant compensation on the trade market if the Ravens entertained any offers. While his age — he'll be 33 by the end of the regular season — is a factor that could have hurt his trade value, it would have only taken one team to drive up the price.
A championship is essentially the only thing that has eluded Henry to this point in his career, and a trade might have expedited his search for a Super Bowl. Instead, it looks as though he will have to wait at least another year as the Ravens fall out of contention.

title: NFL trade deadline rumors: Colts' Daniel Jones could get dealt and there's only one team that makes sense
summary: The Vikings are 6-1 despite fielding the league's second-worst passing attack, and a reunion with Kevin O'Connell makes all the sense in the world
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have been one of the busiest teams in the NFL heading into the trade deadline and they might not be done making deals. The Colts have already traded away both Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner , and it appears that there's at least a chance that Daniel Jones could be next.
According to ESPN , the Colts have taken calls from "multiple" teams about Jones' availability and they've been willing to listen to any offer. This doesn't mean that Jones will ultimately be traded, but it does mean that he'll definitely be one of the biggest names to watch between now and Tuesday's deadline.
At one point, Jones looked like he was going to be the Colts' quarterback of the future. Last season, he helped get the Colts off to a 7-1 start before his year was derailed by injuries. He ended up tearing his Achilles in Week 13, which caused him to miss the final four games of the year. Despite the injury, the Colts still decided to sign him to a two-year $88 million extension back in March. The deal included $50 million in guaranteed money and the Colts have already paid most of that out in the form of a $44 million signing bonus .
This means that if a team acquires Jones, it wouldn't cost much from a financial standpoint. The one thing about a potential Jones trade is that there aren't very many trade candidates out there. The ESPN report mentioned that the Ravens had called about his availability, but Baltimore ended up making a deal for Jacoby Brissett .
With the Ravens out, that basically leaves one team that makes sense for Jones, and that's the Minnesota Vikings . The Vikings are off to a 6-1 start and they currently have one of the best defenses in the NFL, but that unit is essentially going to waste right now because Minnesota has an offense that can't move the ball.
The Vikings signed Kyler Murray in the offseason hoping he could spark the offense, but that hasn't happened. He's started six games this season and simply hasn't been effective. The Vikings' passing attack is averaging just 165.6 yards per game this year, which is the second-worst number in the NFL. Murray has also been dealing with multiple injuries, including a hamstring issue that will keep him on the sideline this week.
The Vikings also have Carson Wentz , who will be making his second start of the season in Week 9. Wentz started in Week 2 after Murray suffered a concussion and during that start, he completed just 55% of his passes for 143 yards and zero touchdowns. However, he did play reasonably well while filling in for Murray in Week 1 with three TD passes in a 39-22 win over the Packers .
If Wentz can lead the Vikings to a win over the 6-1 Buffalo Bills on Monday night, that might change the Vikings' mind about making a deal for Jones, but if he struggles, then it wouldn't be surprising at all to see Minnesota try to make a move for a QB before the trade deadline (The Vikings did also have J.J. McCarthy at QB, but they traded him away to the Giants in late September .
One reason Jones would make a lot of sense for Minnesota is that Kevin O'Connell is already familiar with him. Jones spent the 2024 season in Minnesota and the Vikings actually wanted him back, but he ended up signing with the Colts because he felt like he had a better chance to start with them.
The Colts will definitely be a team to watch between now and Tuesday. Besides Jones, they could also trade Jonathan Taylor , but there's no guarantee that will happen.

Another notable injury storyline is with new Seahawks offensive guard Quenton Nelson . Just one week after trading a third-round pick and future fifth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for the eight-time Pro Bowl left guard, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Nelson needs a minor knee procedure. NFL Media reports it's to clean out cartilage, as fragments have been causing an issue. Seattle says Nelson will avoid injured reserve right now, and is week-to-week. That means the Seahawks offensive line will likely revert to their old format, with Grey Zabel at left guard and Anthony Bradford at right guard.
Below, we will break down the final injury reports for all teams set to play on Sunday, beginning with our international game in Spain.
