title: 3 overlooked Joe Burrow throws that helped Bengals defeat Titans
summary: Seven players caught at least one pass from Joe Burrow in Sunday’s 43-36 overtime win for the Bengals over the Tennessee Titans. Samaje Perine and Jack Endries were both only targeted one time. Perine hauled in a nine-yard reception on the second play of overtime, and Endries hauled in a one-yard touchdown that gave the […]
full_text: Seven players caught at least one pass from Joe Burrow in Sunday’s 43-36 overtime win for the Bengals over the Tennessee Titans. Samaje Perine and Jack Endries were both only targeted one time. Perine hauled in a nine-yard reception on the second play of overtime, and Endries hauled in a one-yard touchdown that gave the Bengals a 14-13 lead just before halftime. Coming into this season, there was a lot of conversation about the Bengals’ wide receiver depth behind Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Sunday, though, showed that depth is good heading into mid-November. Mike Gesicki has a touchdown in five straight games and six out of seven overall this season, and Dohnte Meyers has gone from a great training camp story to an integral part of the Bengals’ receiver room and special teams. Burrow has trust in a lot of receivers right now. Several players caught passes from Burrow in the fourth quarter and overtime Sunday in got-to-have-it situations. On a day where Burrow was historically good, three throws are getting overlooked, but they stand out for the growing trust he has in the Bengals deep group of pass catchers and also for how ridiculously accurate and prolific Joe Burrow is at throwing the football. 1. 10:07 4Q — 3rd&3 from the Bengals 34-yard line; Bengals trailing 28-23 Tensions were high in Paycor Stadium going into this play. The Bengals had just turned the ball over on their previous offensive possession, their fourth of the day, and Tennessee cashed in with a touchdown to take the lead. After a Chase Brown run on 2nd&4 gained just one yard, there were boo-birds coming down from the crowd. Then on 3rd&3, Burrow coolly found Mike Gesicki on the right side of the field for 18 yards and a badly needed first down. It was just Gesicki’s second catch of the game, but it would be the first of three receptions for him in the fourth quarter that accumulated 48 yards. Four plays after his third-down reception, Gesicki hauled in a 25-yard touchdown for his sixth score of the season and to give the Bengals a 29-28 lead. Gesicki is now tied for the most touchdowns he’s ever scored in a season, and that was back in 2020, when he caught six touchdowns in his third season with the Dolphins. This season, Gesicki has 17 receptions for 241 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 14.2 yards per reception. Every Mike Gesicki catch so far this season: Touchdown First down First down First down First down Six yards Touchdown Six yards Touchdown Seven yards First down Touchdown Touchdown #WhoDey — SleeperBengals (@SleeperBengals) October 31, 2026 Fourteen of Gesicki’s 17 receptions are for first downs or touchdowns. He set the tone for this season in Week 1, catching five passes for 78 yards and a touchdown, including three catches for 52 yards on the Bengals’ final first-half drive that led to a field goal. Now, Gesicki has a touchdown in five straight games, the longest streak for a tight end in Bengals’ franchise history. 2. 8:03 4Q — 3rd&10 from the Titans’ 48-yard line; Bengals trailing 28-23 Don’t let Gesicki’s emergence and Tee’s career-year overshadow the incredible connection Burrow and Chase have. They’ve been on the same page going all the way back to their first season at LSU in 2018. This play on Sunday shows the timing Burrow and Chase have on a difficult throw as Burrow is getting hit from a defensive stunt. First of all, this play was set up by a 10-yard reception by Chase Brown on 2nd&20, which the Bengals were in after Burrow was sacked on first down. So getting back into third-and-manageable is impressive in and of itself. Then on 3rd&10, the Titans ran a stunt with defensive end Jacob Martin looping around the left side of the Bengals’ offensive line. It gave him a free rush at Burrow, but he didn’t sack him. While he hit him hard, Burrow got rid of the ball just in time and layered a throw around multiple Titans’ defenders to Chase on the far side of the field. It gained 23 yards, and it set up Gesicki’s 25-yard touchdown on the next play. Burrow with the strike to Ja’Marr Chase with pressure bearing down on him pic.twitter.com/c6XAMTLjEW — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Chase had 11 receptions for 141 yards and a touchdown on Sunday, his first game with 100+ receiving yards and his first game with 10+ receptions. Even though Chase “only” has 492 receiving yards through seven games, he still has six touchdowns on the season, touchdowns in three straight games and five of his last six. And if Chase has 10 receptions on Sunday, he’ll tie Michael Thomas for the most games with 10+ receptions by a player in his first six seasons all-time with 18. For what it’s worth, Chase is still on pace for 148 targets, 104 receptions, 1,195 receiving yards, and 15 touchdowns this season. Even if that’s a “down” year, it’d still be a great year. But don’t worry; Chase had eight receptions for 130 yards and two touchdowns the last time the Bengals played the Falcons… and he didn’t even play in the second half of that game. 3. 3:01 4Q — 2nd&3 from the Bengals’ 26-yard line; Bengals trailing 36-29 This is my favorite play of the game. Tennessee just scored what could have been a back-breaking touchdown to take a 36-29 lead. I don’t know about you, but I didn’t know what the Bengals were going to do on their ensuing drive. It felt to me that it could go either way. But after this play, I was confident the Bengals were going to score and tie the game. Burrow was in trouble on this play, but he bounced out of the pocket and started rolling to his left. It wasn’t Chase or Higgins who caught the pass, though. It was Dohnte Meyers. The standout in training camp and the preseason, and who recently starred in the CFL, came across the field and made a diving 18-yard reception to move the chains and get the offense rolling. we not talking bout this play enough 🤦🏽‍♂️🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/JCMkluz14u — Khiicapalot (@Not_Gstreets) November 2, 2026 In that big of a spot, with Burrow escaping the pocket, it was Meyers making an incredible catch to gain the Bengals’ first down on the drive that ultimately tied the game late in the fourth quarter. Five plays later, Tee Higgins caught his second touchdown to tie the game at 36-36. Through seven games, Meyers has 16 receptions for 175 yards. Ten of those catches are for first downs, and he also has one rush for 10 yards that gained a first down against Tampa Bay. On special teams, Meyers has 11 punt returns for 103 yards and a 9.4 average, and he has 25 kick returns for 660 yards and a 26.4 average. Meyers had three receptions for 34 yards on Sunday, including two receptions in the fourth quarter for 27 yards. Joe Burrow is averaging 302.1 passing yards per game. Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both lead the Bengals with 43 receptions. But other players are also stepping up, as evidenced by their performances on Sunday and through seven games this season. The Bengals not only have the best wide receiver duo in the NFL, but they also have one of the NFL’s overlooked but deepest groups of pass catchers. That may be what lifts Joe Burrow to the pole position of the MVP race and ultimately wins him his first MVP award.

title: Shedeur Sanders’ have a shot at Deshaun Watson’s job? Talking to myself about it
summary: Channeling the long-time Cleveland sports media great Terry Pluto, I have found myself talking over whether Week 9 presents an opportunity for QB Shedeur Sanders to take QB Deshaun Watson’s job as the Cleveland Browns starting quarterback. Sanders is set to lead the Browns offense against the New Orleans Saints, but Watson has not been […]
full_text: Channeling the long-time Cleveland sports media great Terry Pluto, I have found myself talking over whether Week 9 presents an opportunity for QB Shedeur Sanders to take QB Deshaun Watson’s job as the Cleveland Browns starting quarterback. Sanders is set to lead the Browns offense against the New Orleans Saints , but Watson has not been ruled out for the game as he progresses through concussion protocol. First things first, can Sanders lead Cleveland to a victory in New Orleans ? That seems like the bare minimum for the second-year quarterback to have a shot at taking over as the team’s full-time starting quarterback. Then… well… welcome into my mind as I think about the future: Me 1: “Of course anything is possible in the NFL; it’s not like Watson was handed the job at the start of training camp, Todd Monken made the decision much later than expected.” Me 2: “Sure, but losing your job because of a one-week concussion is almost unheard of. Often, even missing weeks due to an injury isn’t enough for a quarterback to lose their starting position, unless they were already playing bad enough that a chance was likely anyway, like Kyler Murray this week with the Vikings.” Me 1: “But can we assume Monken cares about NFL norms in any way?” Me 2: “That’s fine, but what about the rest of the roster? Do they want players thinking that something outside of their control or strictly performance-based can upend their spot with the team? Does Monken have a strong enough feel for how the young locker room would be impacted by such a decision?” Me 1: “Great question, self, but what if the roster was already wondering when Sanders would take over already? We have no idea what is going on inside of the locker room.” Me 2: “Of course we don’t. We also know that the Saints defense isn’t very good, so there is a strong chance that Sanders could have a huge game in Week 9, but that Watson would have done the same or better had he been healthy.” Me 1: “Are you ignoring the more Brownsian outcome, that Sanders either struggles or gets dinged up and Watson, cleared Saturday (possibly) of concussion protocol, comes on in relief?” Me 2: “Not really; that outcome sort of closes the book on Sanders for this season, barring a major Watson injury. If that happens, it’s also possible that Dillon Gabriel is given the next shot at starting. So, that ”Browns is the Browns” option just ends this conversation (which psychologically might be best for me/us and the fanbase, but for the team????).“ Me 1: “Do you think readers are following along?” Me 2: “No clue, Jared is a strange creature.” Me 1: “So what is the benefit for the team if Monken turns to Sanders if the Browns win on Sunday and the quarterback has a great game?” Me 2: “From Jimmy Haslam, to Andrew Berry, and down to Monken, the entire Cleveland organization has made it clear that the only thing that matters is winning and producing on the field. If Sanders and Watson really were that close during the QB competition, and Sanders has a huge game in Week 9, making him the starter reinforces that principle.” Me 1: “Sure, but how in the world would one game versus a bad defense be enough to overcome Watson winning the competition to start the year, having multiple 4th-quarter comebacks, and two or three good games this season?” Me 2: “See, that is why we keep talking to ourselves about this. It isn’t that simple. Most believed that Watson would fail early in the season and Sanders would take over. Instead, through Week 7, the veteran looked like he was improving as the season went on.” Me 1: “So… are we ignoring Week 8 versus the Pittsburgh Steelers?” Me 2: “Exactly, which would be very different if his poor performance came in the Week 4 matchup in the AFC North. Instead, the last game Watson played was not good; he could miss Week 9 due to a concussion, and his job is being discussed by a somewhat sane person pretending to be two different people in this article.” Me 1: “Have we come to a conclusion?” Me 2: “Not really. Maybe our readers will be able to fill in some of their thoughts into the conversation. There may be two things both me’s will agree on, and probably most Browns fans: Browns HC Todd Monken will do whatever he wants and be unapologetic about his decisions All that matters is winning football games; if the team is winning, the QB will be supported, whoever it is Do you think there is any chance for Sanders to take over as the Browns starting QB after Week 9, or does Watson get it back no matter what when he’s cleared? title: Browns season heading into Week 9 versus the Saints: Ahead of schedule good enough?
summary: Going into the season, the expectations around the Cleveland Browns were reasonably low. New coaching staff, the youngest roster in the league, uncertainty at the quarterback position, and the team just traded one of the best defensive players of this generation to Inglewood. Fast forward to early November, the Browns are 5-3 and are still […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Going into the season, the expectations around the Cleveland Browns were reasonably low . New coaching staff, the youngest roster in the league, uncertainty at the quarterback position, and the team just traded one of the best defensive players of this generation to Inglewood . Fast forward to early November, the Browns are 5-3 and are still in the playoff hunt in the AFC . Considering how many believed that around this time Cleveland would be in “making mock drafts” territory ( Editor’s Note: I did create one recently , just one), 5-3 is better than what anyone thought. As people will question how good the Browns are, it’s a fair process to go through. However, in this day and age, context is rarely used correctly. Going into the season, Cleveland had one of the easier schedules. In the first 8 games of the season, the Browns were only favored in 1 of their 5 wins, their most recent one: Week 2 @ Buccaneers: 23-19 Week 3 vs Panthers: 21-18 Week 4 vs Steelers: 27-24 Week 6 vs Ravens: 13-10 Week 7 @ Titans: 27-24 Fans’ confidence in the team has waxed and waned throughout the season, but is higher than it was before the season. If you want to argue which win was most impressive, you can make an argument that it was the home win against the Steelers. The final score doesn’t indicate how the game actually went. If you rewatched that game, the Browns looked like the better team throughout, and it was a surprise to everyone watching that night. Winning in the NFL is hard, and it doesn’t matter how you do it. Is Cleveland a good football team? Bad football team? Neither. Average, so far, but young. Offensively, despite their issues, they are better than last year. Having better personnel helps, but the scheme is better than last season. Defensively, the unit isn’t as dominant as last season, but it’s still regarded as one of the better units in the NFL. Progress is being shown even if the results aren’t as impressive. If the team were winless or 1-7, we would argue that the Browns are making any progress at all. Instead, the team is 5-3 and exceeding expectations. It’s possible that the team goes over their win total sooner rather than later , and it’s possible that the team is playing meaningful games towards mid-November and early December. full_text: It is amazing how quickly the NFL season seems to go by, even more so with the Cleveland Browns actually winning football games before the NFL trade deadline . The Browns enter what seems like a must-win game in Week 9 versus the New Orleans Saints , with the result potentially impacting what GM Andrew Berry decides to do at the trade deadline . Rumors have been strong around Cleveland looking at defensive end options . Recently, former Browns DE Jadeveon Clowney’s name hit the market , someone Berry tried to reacquire this offseason. With Shedeur Sanders taking over for Deshaun Watson (concussion protocol) as the starting quarterback this week, a lot of the focus will, rightfully, be on the field in Louisiana, but the rumors around Tuesday’s deadline will continue to swirl as well. According to an Albert Breer rumor, the Browns are looking to be buyers and have two positions in mind: The Browns are actually positioned now as buyers , which is pretty fascinating. Cleveland has looked around at adding a rotational edge rusher and perhaps a blocking tight end, which would free them up to move Harold Fannin Jr. around even more. A tight end addition could have a bigger impact on the Browns offense than an edge rusher does on the defense. HC Todd Monken hasn’t used many extra offensive linemen in the blocking tight end role, leaving Fannin or receivers like Malachi Corley to step in there. Finding a quality blocking tight end could unleash Fannin even further while also helping their run game. An edge rusher could make more direct statistical impact, and a defense can never have too many people to get after the passer. Do you think the Browns will be buyers at the deadline? One fan thinks it actually will be a big win in New Orleans, with one of the problem areas getting it together: It will be interesting to see how our young group responds. title: NFL predictions: Shedeur Sanders vs. Tyler Shough, a battle of last year’s rookie QBs in Browns-Saints
summary: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take on the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. What Happened to the Confidence? The news that Shedeur Sanders would suddenly be starting this week, due to the concussion […]
full_text: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take on the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. What Happened to the Confidence? The news that Shedeur Sanders would suddenly be starting this week, due to the concussion reported by Deshaun Watson , definitely caught us off guard. Due to Watson’s 5-3 record as starter, the boo birds toward him have largely stopped, even though he’s not exactly lighting it up week in and week out. Still, when the news broke, I thought we would see a lot of intrigue from fans regarding Sanders again. Instead, it’s seemed like the opposite. Everyone almost seems resigned to thinking it’ll be a pretty rough game for the second-year quarterback. I guess I’m a bit caught off guard that the reaction has seemed so tame, or almost like fans are chalking this one up as a loss because of Sanders. Going back to last year, Sanders did what I would call a respectable job. I thought he showed he can make a lot of good NFL throws, he stopped the bad habit of backpedaling too much, and he did so behind a terrible offensive line. Despite the pace of sacks that this year’s group is giving up, the eye test still tells me that the Browns’ new offensive line is performing way better than last year’s group was. Sanders had some good outings in training camp, and is facing a Saints defense that ranks near the bottom of the league. My expectation is that Sanders will have a solid 2026 debut against New Orleans. This is also a big game, so I’d expect the team to pull out all the stops if necessary. Assessing the Game There’s a lot to look at for this week’s game, especially pertaining ti the Browns’ run defense and the Saints’ offense. Let’s get into it with some of our miscellaneous notes this week: I was intrigued by the Saints because last year, they won four straight games near the end of last season, and Tyler Shough was turning headlines and looking like the best quarterback of his class. Now, in hindsight, they didn’t face the best competition in those four games, but it was still something to be proud of. This year, they lost a nailbiter of an overtime opener to the Lions 31-30 when they went for the win in extra time instead of the tie, and then they beat the Baltimore Ravens (back when they had Lamar Jackson) the following week. Since then, it’s been much of the same story: Shough plays well and should be taken seriously, but New Orleans can’t get anything going on the ground, averaging just 3.52 yards per carry. Their numbers and commitment to the ground game has been really bad. I know some of you may be thinking, ‘Welp, get ready for that to change against Cleveland,’ but I’m inclined to expect the opposite: this is a game will New Orleans’ run struggles continue, and the Browns’ run defense feels like they are on top of the world with all the run plays they’ll swallow up. The other thing that has been part of the same story is the Saints’ poor run defense and defensive interior. They allow 4.81 yards per carry, which is well worse than even the Titans’ allowed two weeks ago when the Browns found success on the ground. Comparatively speaking, the Steelers’ run defense is ranked among the best in the league Overall, those factors make me see the Browns having a variety of ways they can score on offense, as long as they stay away from delays and procedural errors (easier said than done, obviously). And while Shough has been pass-heavy, that approach should play into Cleveland’s favor against a duo of Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell that is playing very well. One big factor to watch is that Saints WR Jordyn Tyson practiced this week for the first time. The first-round pick hasn’t seen regular season action yet, which is crazy. He is listed as questionable, so we’ll see if he is active or inactive. Carson Schwesinger was a liability last week, but that’s a rarity, even if he is hurt. Hopefully we see a bounceback game from him this week. Jared Verse is driving me a bit crazy. Even if I disregard his stats with the Browns, I don’t like the demeanor he carries in interviews, and I feel like he’s the one that has gotten away with some dumb late hits on quarterbacks this year. I’d be rolling my eyes at some of the stuff he says, and if I’m thinking of it, I bet some teammates are keeping a lid on it too. With all that said, I of course want him to flip the switch and be better for the Browns. Not that I’m comparing him to Myles Garrett , but to a much lesser extent, this would be like Garrett going to the Rams and then suddenly looking like a third-string backup with them and unlike his previous years of productivity. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 3 point underdogs against the Saints. The over/under is 43.5. Quick Hitters Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer talked about what he’s excited to see from Shedeur Sanders : “I’m just excited to see him go play and hopefully let it rip, which I think he’ll do. He did it yesterday in practice. Go lead, be in command, which I think he’s grown tremendously in that area, really since we got here. And I think Monk (Todd Monken) mentioned this the other day, but when you’re going through training camp, and we were splitting, and really all the spring, we were splitting a lot of those reps as we were going through all the installs, and we were able to see him in a lot more reps than probably a typical backup would be, because obviously we were finding out who our quarterback was going to be. So, hopefully he can review back to some of those things if it were to be him, and yeah, let it rip. Play with confidence.” Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg had some very generic responses to his questions this week, which was a bit disappointing. Ultimately, I’ll highlight this one, when he was asked about the team’s defensive ends not having many combined sacks this year: “Our whole defense is built on a collective 11, so it has nothing to do with a position ever. We’re not built that way. When it comes to pressuring the quarterback, it doesn’t matter who the pressure could come from. When it comes to anything we do, it’s a collective 11. It takes all 11 to play great defense, and that will always be our motto together.” Special teams coordinator Bryon Storer was asked about trying different guys out at kick returner lately: “So, we’re trying some different returners back there. We’ve kind of mixed and matched a little bit over the last couple, last game, and we need to block better in the setup zone. We need to, set up our blocking better. We need to make sure that we stay with our man longer without holding. There’s a lot that goes into it. We’ve been drilling it and trying to get better, and it’s a matchup-based play as well. You know, it’s very much like, you have to make sure you have the right people in the right spots. And so, we’re just continuing to learn and improve each and every week, and hopefully we’ll see some progress there soon.” Here are predictions from multiple staff members at DBN: Predictions Chris Pokorny: “I wanted to pick the Browns by a slightly larger margin, but because the Browns’ victories this year have all been by 3 or 4 points only, and I could foresee some rust from the quarterback spot, I have this as a lower-scoring affair.” Browns 20, Saints 17 Jared Mueller : “Something is off with the Browns and I can’t put my finger on it, but I don’t feel comfortable with it. Injuries, Shedeur Sanders and Jared Verse media time, and going on the road with a team coming off the bye all smell trouble for my favorite team. The Saints are far from a good team but have a creative offensive mind, an athletic quarterback, and enough talent on the roster to win games.” Saints 28, Browns 24 Barry Shuck: “I am on the fence with this one. If you look at the Browns’ schedule, they beat the Ravens and the Steelers, and all of their other wins are against mediocre teams.…

summary: There is a fear among fans and media members about the power of “bulletin-board material.” According to the theory, if a player or coach says something negative (either real or perceived) about the upcoming team on the schedule, that quote will be printed out and posted on a bulletin board for everyone on the opposing […]
full_text: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is a fear among fans and media members about the power of “bulletin-board material.” According to the theory, if a player or coach says something negative (either real or perceived) about the upcoming team on the schedule, that quote will be printed out and posted on a bulletin board for everyone on the opposing team to see. It is a bit of an antiquated idea – has anyone actually used a bulletin board since the last millennium? – but it was probably always more about the message than the medium anyway. The real question is just how much does that actually happen across professional sports? These are highly skilled athletes making a good living and eager to keep it that way. Do they really need to be motivated by something another player may (or may not) have said in the build-up to the game? Well, we’re going to find out come Sunday when the Cleveland Browns take on the New Orleans Saints, as defensive end Carl Granderson is a bit out of joint over comments from Cleveland quarterback Shedeur Sanders. #Saints EDGE Carl Granderson says the defense will play with a chip on its shoulder Sunday against the #Browns : "They've been chirping a little bit. We see what the quarterback said. […] It's going to be a good game for sure." pic.twitter.com/FRs0qxBzWe — NOF (@nofnetwork) November 6, 2026 In a clip from the NOF Network, Granderson said the Saints will be ready for Sanders come Sunday: “We have a chip on our shoulde for sure. They’ve been chirping a little bit. We see what the quarterback done said. So we going to come in hot and ready to play. It’s going to be a good game for sure. One would think the Saints would be “hot and ready to play” even without some pretty tame comments from a player who is going to make one start before heading back to the bench. On Friday, Cleveland […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns roster continues to be in flux heading into Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints. On Wednesday, the Browns signed TE Carsen Ryan to the active roster, but then waived him the following day, which caused some speculation and confusion about why those decisions were made as they were. On Friday, Cleveland signed DT Sam Kamara to their active roster in Ryan’s place. Kamara’s addition is likely due to the injury to DT Maliek Collins that has kept him from practicing this week . Since Kamara has already been elevated the maximum of three times this season, the Browns must have him on their active roster if they want him to play in Week 9. The team has not made the Kamara move official at the time of this writing, but has been reported by his agent: The #Browns are signing DL Sam Kamara to their active roster, per his agents Zac Hiller and Matt Leist of LAA Sports. Kamara has 1 sack, 3 TFLs, and 10 tackles in 3 games this season. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 6, 2026 Kamara has been with the Browns since 2022, playing in 21 games, including two starts. In his three games this season, Kamara has 10 tackles, one sack, and one tackle for loss.

title: 5 quick hitters with Canal Street Chronicles: Browns can take advantage of Saints’ run defense
summary: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns are on the road as they take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 9. To help preview a few topics from the Saints’ perspective, we reached out to Nic Jennings from Canal Street Chronicles and exchanged five questions with him. Chris: “It must be frustrating that Jordyn Tyson hasn’t […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - APRIL 23: Jordyn Tyson of Arizona State poses for a photo after being selected eighth overall by the New Orleans Saints during Round One of the 2026 NFL Draft at Acrisure Stadium on April 23, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns are on the road as they take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 9. To help preview a few topics from the Saints’ perspective, we reached out to Nic Jennings from Canal Street Chronicles and exchanged five questions with him. Chris: “It must be frustrating that Jordyn Tyson hasn’t been able to play this season yet, but tell us about Tyler Shough — are fans behind him as the team’s long-term future QB?” Nic : “It certainly has been frustrating that we haven’t seen Jordyn Tyson on the field yet, but this was the timeline that made the most sense given his hamstring issue and injury history. Some fans will argue that the Saints should have pursued more immediate help by selecting someone like Caleb Downs or an offensive lineman, but Tyson will bring a different dynamic to this offense once he is able to make his season debut. Hopefully, that comes this week against Cleveland. Get ready for game day with SB Nation’s new app! SB Nation’s NEW game chat feature in the app is perfect for keeping the latest Browns game-day conversations and updates at your fingertips. Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . As for Tyler Shough, absolutely. Shough is the real deal and his teammates rally behind him. He’s been one of the three consistent bright spots for the Saints this season, along with Chris Olave and Chase Young. Shough showed a lot of promise in his limited starts as a rookie, then attacked the offseason and blew expectations out of the water. He’s carried that same momentum into this season. His ball placement, ability to stretch the field with his arm, poise in the pocket and ability to extend plays with his legs give the Saints a dimension offensively that they haven’t really had. And most importantly, he has that clutch gene. He’s shown he can make plays when the Saints need them most. I do think there are still things he can improve on. The offense has developed a habit of starting slowly, and while I’d put more of that on Kellen Moore, Shough still plays a role in getting the offense into a rhythm. Though to Shough’s credit the Saints have a putrid rushing attack, which hasn’t eased the pressure on Shough and the passing game one bit. But overall, I’ve seen more than enough to believe he can be the long-term answer in New Orleans.” Chris: “What do you view as the Saints’ biggest weakness on defense right now?” Nic : “The Saints’ biggest weakness on defense has to be the interior of the defensive front, which has led to an inability to consistently stop the run. New Orleans is tied for fourth in yards per carry allowed at 4.8, while allowing the second-most rushing touchdowns in the league with 11. They’ve also allowed the second-most rushing first downs with 62, while having the highest rushing first-down percentage allowed in the league at 30.5%. Outside of that, stopping vertical threats at tight end continues to be the Saints’ kryptonite like it has in years past, so expect Harold Fannin Jr. to be licking his chops at the opportunity to face the New Orleans defense.” Chris: “Which of the Saints’ draft picks has the best chance of making an impact in Week 9?” Nic : “Well, if Tyson is able to suit up, I’d bank on him being the guy to stand out. Like I previously mentioned, the dude is a game changer who will add a different dimension to the Saints’ passing game. If not Tyson, I’d put my money on sixth-rounder Barion Brown making a difference. He’s started to heat up recently in the return game and showed New Orleans throughout the offseason that he can be a receiving threat as well. He’s already had some standout moments in the passing game during the regular season and has even been effective as a ball carrier. He’s a playmaker that opposing defenses have to account for whenever he’s on the field, and he’s been getting involved more and more by the week. I don’t expect that to slow down anytime soon.” Chris: “Tell us about one player who Browns fans may not have heard of, but who could have an impact on this Sunday’s game.” Nic : “On offense, it has to be Devaughn Vele. After the Saints invested a fourth-round pick in him last year to pry him away from Denver, Vele has come in and become the contested-catch slot receiver the Saints have been searching for since Michael Thomas. He’s quickly become one of Tyler Shough’s favorite targets and has become the go-to guy on third-and-long situations. He and Juwan Johnson have also been quite lethal in the red zone. Vele is a guy I expect to keep garnering more and more attention as the season progresses. For a six-foot-foot receiver to be able to move the way he does and have that type of body control, it’s truly remarkable. On defense, keep an eye on second-year defensive back Jonas Sanker. He consistently finds his way to the football and has been impressive in his first year starting in the slot. He returned a fumble for a touchdown against the Vikings and had another return for a touchdown in Week 1 against the Lions that was called back after Jared Goff apparently “intended” to throw the football forward. Expect Sanker to be flying all over the field on Sunday.” Chris: “The Browns are underdogs against the Saints on Sunday (Browns +3 as of this question, per FanDuel). Who would you pick to win the game?” Nic : “This is a must-win game for New Orleans if it wants any hope of turning its season around. Coming off their bye week, the Saints have had time to put their issues under the microscope and address them. Kellen Moore’s seat has never been hotter, so I expect the Black and Gold to come out prepared and ready to show their home crowd that there is still reason to believe in this football team. I’ll take the Saints, 23-12.” Thanks again to Nic for taking the time to answer my questions.

title: College football draft targets for the Cowboys: Week 10
summary: We are taking a quick peek ahead to the upcoming offseason to scout out a few potential draft picks in the college ranks. Miami vs. Notre Dame Miami takes the highest-scoring offense in the country to South Bend, but the Hurricanes will be without explosive receiver Malachi Toney following ankle surgery. That increases the pressure […]
full_text: Photo by Aaron Baker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We are taking a quick peek ahead to the upcoming offseason to scout out a few potential draft picks in the college ranks. Miami vs. Notre Dame Miami takes the highest-scoring offense in the country to South Bend, but the Hurricanes will be without explosive receiver Malachi Toney following ankle surgery. That increases the pressure on Miami’s defense and gives Notre Dame receiver Jordan Faison an even more important role. In the middle of that battle will be Hurricanes defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr, one of the better interior defenders expected to enter the 2027 draft. Miami: Ahmad Moten Sr, defensive tackle Moten is the prototypical sized defensive tackle who wins with his first step. He fires off the ball before offensive linemen can settle into their stance and forces the blocking scheme to react immediately. That burst allows him to create pressure from the three-technique position and disrupt running plays before the back reaches the line of scrimmage. He became a full-time starter in 2025 and produced 4.5 sacks and nine tackles for loss. His 12.9% pressure rate showed that the production was not based only on a handful of big plays. Moten repeatedly found his way into the backfield while playing beside first-round talents Rueben Bain Jr. and Akheem Mesidor. With those players now in the NFL, he has taken on a larger role as the experienced leader of Miami’s defensive front. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas needs to add young legs to their veteran rotation on the inside and prepare for the future adding another interior disruptor would help protect the investment Dallas has already made in Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark. Moten could begin as a rotational three-technique and a pass-rushing option on obvious throwing downs. His ability to penetrate would complement the power of Williams and Clark, while Christian Parker could move him across different alignments in the pressure package. He currently carries a second-round projection, placing him in the exact area of the draft Dallas must maximise. The Cowboys would need to improve his pad level and consistency against double teams, but his explosive first step is a trait that cannot easily be taught. Notre Dame: Jordan Faison, wide receiver Faison has developed from a walk-on and two-sport athlete into Notre Dame’s leading receiver. He enters this game with 38 catches for 497 yards and four touchdowns. He led the Irish in both receptions and receiving yards last season, recording 49 catches for 640 yards and four scores, while also contributing as a punt returner. His route running is the foundation of his game. Faison changes speed during the route to create separation without relying on elite size. He is especially effective from the slot. Why The Cowboys Care We say it every week when bringing g up wide receiver, this is all about George Pickens’ future. His long-term contract and possible trade value will remain major offseason questions, and although Ryan Flournoy has provided useful depth, the Cowboys still need another receiver who can separate quickly and keep the offense on schedule. Faison could compete for the third-receiver role, work from the slot and give Dak Prescott a reliable answer when the defense sends pressure. His punt-return experience adds another route onto the active roster. He is currently viewed as a third-round prospect, which makes him a realistic Dallas target rather than a player the Cowboys would need to chase at the top of the draft. BYU vs. Utah The Holy War will feature two top-10 teams for the first time. Utah enters at 8-0, while BYU is 7-1 and attempting to hand its rival a second consecutive defeat in the series. BYU running back L.J. Martin is doubtful, placing more responsibility on the Cougars’ defense. That makes linebacker Isaiah Glasker a key figure against a Utah offense protected by rising left tackle Zereoue Williams. BYU: Isaiah Glasker, linebacker Glasker looks like an NFL linebacker in every way. A former high school receiver and safety, he has the athletic background to turn and run in coverage and match tight ends without immediately creating a size disadvantage. That versatility has been central to his role at BYU. The Cougars can align him as an off-ball linebacker, walk him onto the edge or send him through an interior gap. He recorded 67 tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss and two interceptions in 2025 after a 2024 season in which he produced 70 tackles, 14.5 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks and three interceptions. Those numbers reflect a defender capable of making plays in several areas rather than simply collecting tackles in the box. Why The Cowboys Care DeMarvion Overshown’s injury history remains a concern, while Dee Winters may or may not be part of a future roster. Glasker could give this defense a long, athletic defender who can play in space, blitz from different angles and contribute on special teams. His current draft stock has fallen into the late-round, which makes the rest of the season important. Dallas would not need to spend a premium selection to bet on his physical tools. A strong performance against unbeaten Utah could move him back into full Day 3 consideration. The Cowboys would be drafting the coverage range and versatility while trusting their coaches to improve his processing and ability to defeat blocks. Utah: Zereoue Williams, offensive tackle Williams is one of the fastest-rising offensive tackles in this draft class. The 6-foot-8, 305-pound senior spent most of his college career as a reserve before earning Utah’s starting left-tackle job this season. His size immediately creates problems for edge rushers. Williams has the length to make first contact and guide speed rushers beyond the quarterback. He moves well for a player of his height and has enough balance to stay connected rather than lunging at defenders. His basketball background appears in the way he mirrors movement and uses his reach without losing control of his base. Why The Cowboys Care Offensive tackle remains one of the most important positions for Dallas to evaluate. Williams has the physical tools to compete on the left side, or he can play on the right and potentially take over for Terence Steele. His draft range is wide because of the small sample, but most projections place him around the second or third round, but it really does range with him. That makes him especially relevant to a Cowboys team with limited draft capital. Dallas could allow him to develop behind its starters before asking him to take over a full-time job, or he could win it straight away.

title: Cowboys key matchup: Quinnen Williams vs the Colts interior OL
summary: We have been saying the same thing for almost a month now, but the Dallas Cowboys are heading into a must win game in week nine with the Indianapolis Colts. This is a unique matchup for the Cowboys due to the Colts practically punting on their season and moving on to 2027. In recent weeks, […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images We have been saying the same thing for almost a month now, but the Dallas Cowboys are heading into a must win game in week nine with the Indianapolis Colts. This is a unique matchup for the Cowboys due to the Colts practically punting on their season and moving on to 2027. In recent weeks, the Colts have traded away two of the best players on their roster in DeForest Buckner and Queneton Nelson, and their star running back Jonathan Taylor has dominated trade rumors over the last two weeks. With the Colts not focusing on winning football games right now, and the Cowboys desperately needing a win, one of the biggest matchups in this game should be a massive mismatch favoring the Cowboys. Early on in the season, it was fair to say Quinnen Williams was a bit disappointing. But over the last month or so, Williams has really turned it on and has been showing the dominant player we all expected to see in 2026. Since week five, Williams has recorded four sacks, three run stuffs, and 14 tackles. Williams has an intriguing matchup coming up in week nine against a depleted Colts offensive line. The interior of the Colts offensive line took a big blow when Quenton Nelson was traded to the Seattle Seahawks. Taking his place at left guard was rookie fourth-round pick Jalen Farmer, who struggled mightily in his first start of the season in week eight. Farmer allowed three pressures, one hurry, and two QB hits against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Colts center has struggled this season too. Tanor Bortolini has allowed multiple pressures in every game this season except for two and has drawn six flags in the last four games. The Colts right guard, Matt Goncalves, has had a solid season so far for the Colts, but he is also a player Williams should be able to take advantage of as well in the running and passing game. Goncalves has allowed multiple pressures in the last two weeks. This is an ideal matchup for Quinnen Williams who has been heating up here lately. Williams has registered 15 pressures and four sacks in the last three weeks, and this matchup should be one of the more favorable matchups he will see this season. Williams will need help from Kenny Clark and Otito Ogbonnia to keep some of the focus off of him, but this should be a matchup the Cowboys should win, and can be one of the biggest factors in them winning a much needed football game on Sunday.

title: Cowboys news: Jerry Jones tries to walk back ‘paying coaches’ comments

full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images Jerry Jones has been criticized for not being willing to write a huge check for a championship type of coach, but he doesn’t feel that it’s an issue whatsoever. The NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching. If Dallas was to indulge, there’s one area that’s likely to get the most attention. The Cowboys have a talented offense that more than capable of being productive, but hiccups at the wrong times have caused some confusion. Cowboys’ Jerry Jones says paying coaches has never been an issue – Todd Archer, ESPN Jerry Jones got ridiculed after he mentioned that there was no connection between the highest-paid coaches to winning championships. Now, he’s saying spend top dollar for a coach hasn’t been a problem in Dallas. “The facts are I have been out there, and I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on and knew full well that I was going to pay them for their success,” he said. “So that has been done. No one knows that, but I do. And so it is absolutely ridiculous. And I actually grin when somebody says, ‘Jerry’s not willing to pay the money for what it would take to get the right kind of coach out there.'” Cowboys to be without two starters, four more questionable vs. Colts – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The Cowboys are facing a huge game against the Colts as they try to stay within striking distance in the NFC East. They’ll have to do so with multiple starters out. On Friday, the Cowboys hit the practice field for the last time before boarding the flight to Indianapolis on Saturday, and they did so without two starters. Wide receiver and kick returner KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and rookie outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence (ankle) did not practice this week and have been ruled out for Sunday’s game. Which position group could Cowboys add to at trade deadline? Stephen Jones answers – SportsDay Staff, Dallas Morning News The NFL deadline is next Tuesday, and the Cowboys have been talked about as a team that could make a move. The specific position that they could make a play for was revealed. Q: Which position or positions do you think could help the team the most right now? Jones: “Yeah I think it’s one everybody talks [about], obviously a pressure player could help us. After that, we took care of business earlier in the year with [Joey Porter Jr.]. It’s unfortunate he’s been missing some time. No excuses, because everybody has injuries, but no question it hurt us not having him or Caleb [Downs] in the game there in that quarter as well.” Download the SB Nation app today! Here We Goooo: Cowboys defense must turn pressure into turnovers vs. Colts -Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Dallas is starting to pick up defensively when it comes to getting to the quarterback. However, taking the ball away needs to improve more also. Pressure is nice, but it doesn’t mean anything if the defense not affecting the quarterback. Bringing quarterbacks down more recently has helped, but Dallas needs to be able to throw Colts QB Daniel Jones off his game with their pressure on Sunday, as it’s affected him throughout the season. Quinnen Williams has been the best defender in terms of getting into the backfield and affecting the quarterback this season, so expect him to be let loose again in this game. Cowboys disconnect grows as CeeDee Lamb unloads on underachieving offense – Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat The Cowboys look pedestrian offensively in situational football last week against the Cardinals. It’s caused tensions to boil over. Lamb is a veteran. He may wear his emotions on his sleeve on the field, but he’s not the type to publicly throw his head coach under the bus. His comments could just as easily be interpreted as criticism of the players’ execution, but it’s hard to imagine Schottenheimer’s conservative play-calling and predictable offense aren’t at least part of the equation.

full_text: Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys, for just a moment, looked like they had righted their season after beating the Philadelphia Eagles and were on their way to taking out the Arizona Cardinals. title: Brandon Aubrey has confidence in everything around him
summary: When it comes to kickers, the Dallas Cowboys are quite fortunate. This season has been a little bit rough in some moments, but ultimately the Cowboys still employ one of the best around in Brandon Aubrey. It is unbelievable to consider that 2026 is already year number four for Aubrey. Aubrey has been around the […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images When it comes to kickers, the Dallas Cowboys are quite fortunate. This season has been a little bit rough in some moments, but ultimately the Cowboys still employ one of the best around in Brandon Aubrey. It is unbelievable to consider that 2026 is already year number four for Aubrey. Aubrey has been around the Cowboys so long that he has the proper marks to prove it. He was with the team when they last made the playoffs, a group that is starting to dwindle, and he even has a second contract with the club which means he has really walked through fire. Aubrey is someone who takes care of himself and recently he has begun to do so by partnering with Invisalign and their “SHIFT Happens” mindset, something that he is considering both on and off the field. This week I had a chance to talk to him thanks to Invisalign, and you can watch our entire conversation below. It was a treat to talk to Aubrey about some of the specific natures of kicking in today’s NFL. We spent a good bit of time talking about his preparation and also how he has handled the new kickoff in terms of trying to pin opponents in specific circumstances. One thing I was curious about was whether or not he believes his own success has played a part in how the Cowboys operate things on offense. My point was that some believe that Aubrey’s range from downtown leads to Brian Schottenheimer becoming dependent on that when the Cowboys do get into field goal range. Obviously right now there is a bit of a feeling from fans that Schottenheimer is operating conservatively so take all of this with a grain of salt, but I found Brandon’s answer on that specific question to be very interesting. Has Brandon Aubrey’s success from deep changed how the Cowboys approach getting into or handling field goal range? I was curious so I asked Brandon. pic.twitter.com/cTudDo2Hc8 — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) November 6, 2026 “I don’t think when you’re looking at, I don’t I can’t speak for play callers or coaching staff’s mindsets, but for me if I were in that position I think I would have a couple of different ideas based on where I am on the field. And field goal range wherever that is for your kicker is one mindset, one play style especially if it’s like a one score game.” “I’ll say we’ve been in a lot of high scoring games so you can’t necessarily think that way I guess. You’d always wanna score a touchdown if you can. But yeah, I think when you’re in field goal range, you tend to not want to turn the ball over just because at that point you’re very obviously giving up points. So yeah I can see possibly being a little more conservative when you’re in field goal range. I don’t know what our play calling mindset is. I’m not involved in any of those decisions. I just try to be ready to kick it when when my name’s called.” This was a fair answer from Aubrey. He was specific in saying that he was only speaking for himself in a hypothetical world where he made those types of decisions, and he noted that you want to protect your opportunity to score points. That is fair and rational. But the feel and reality of our current moment is hard to ignore. Consider that the Cowboys entered Week 9 with the lowest amount of attempted fourth down conversions (on 4th and 5 or shorter) when already inside of field goal range. A Brian Schottenheimer chart that’s also a fantasy football kicker chart You want kickers that are in good offenses with coaches who kick a lot pic.twitter.com/vMPPoP7jud — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) November 5, 2026 Again, this information really kind of tells you what you want it to. On one hand it suggests that the Cowboys try to secure points when it feels like they have them. On the other it opens the door of conversation as to whether or not they are perhaps too reliant upon that, which is why I asked Aubrey the question in the first place. What do you think? Is the way that Dallas is going about things the right way, or should they adjust things in some way? Our thanks to Brandon Aubrey and to Invisalign for the time.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: What the numbers say about a winner in Cowboys vs Colts
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 3-5 Dallas Cowboys take on the 2-6 Indianapolis Colts. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak […]
full_text: Photo by Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 3-5 Dallas Cowboys take on the 2-6 Indianapolis Colts. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 195 yards, one touchdown and finished with a passer rating of 96.2 . He’d also score once with his legs. Prescott was sacked four times as the offensive line again struggled throughout the day in both run blocking and pass protection. Javonte Williams was again the primary focus on the day. The results were quite poor as compared to the previous week. He finished with just 56 yards on 24 carries – good for an atrocious 2.3 yards per carry. This was especially concerning when considering the Cardinals inability to stop the run throughout the season. The big three receivers, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Ryan Flournoy totaled a combined 144 yards on 19 targets. Just one touchdown on the day went to a Flournoy on a nifty one-handed catch. Colts key stats from last week The Colts finished last week with only one score on the day, losing 42-7 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. They were down 28-0 at halftime and never stood a chance in their fourth straight loss. Daniel Jones was sat down in the fourth quarter after throwing for just 144 yards and two interceptions. He was sacked three times on the day. Jonathan Taylor carried the ball eight times for 23 yards, by far his lowest output on the season. Trade rumors continue to swirl around the Colts’ most valuable piece. Indianapolis finished the day with 243 total yards on offense, one touchdown, and three turnovers. The defense surrendered 366 yards and six touchdowns, including a pick-six. This is certainly a team that’s given up on the season, exporting key pieces to jumpstart their rebuild and it shows. Get the Javon-train back on the tracks The last two weeks we’ve implored coach Brian Schottenheimer to stick with the run. He listened maybe a little too well to our requests. Last week, the Cowboys ran the ball into a brick wall throughout the entire day. And at times, it’s necessary to do so to keep the defense honest. If they want to present a light box, this offensive line and running back should be able to take advantage. But that just wasn’t the case last week. The Cowboys were stuffed at the line of scrimmage the second most across the NFL last week, according the SumerSports. The insistence on running between the tackles play after play (65.7% of the time) on a day where the interior three offensive linemen struggled was a certainly a decision that did not work. On the season, Dallas ranks third in inside run percentage while they rank 29th in outside run rate. With 53 yards to work with sideline to sideline, the Cowboys insist on utilizing just the seven yards between the tackles. If Dallas is to get Javonte Williams and this run game back on track, they either need to utilize more of the boundary to make the linebackers defend sideline to sideline, or they need to snag explosive plays downfield to back these teams off the line of scrimmage. Against a bad Colts run defense and a team that has thrown in the towel, this would be a great week to do so. What do the numbers mean? The Colts aren’t good, but neither are the Cowboys. On paper, Dallas possesses superior talent at the most important positions on the field. They were also more talented than the Buccaneers and the Cardinals but that didn’t mean much when the game moved from the paper to the field. The Colts struggle mightily on defense, both through the ground and the air. If the good Cowboys offense decides to show up this week, they should be able to move the ball and score at will. But if they allow the Colts team to stick around throughout the day, just as Dallas did against the Cardinals, this could be a game where Indianapolis finds an opportunity to regain some pride. We should expect Dallas to once again try and establish the run this week, and rightfully so. The Colts have traded key defensive lineman DeForest Buckner back to the 49ers, and were struggling to stop the run even before then. Indianapolis is the second worst defense in EPA/rush attempt across the league. If Dallas can’t get right on the ground this week, it’ll be difficult to expect a successful rushing attack for the remainder of the season. On defense, the Cowboys will face off against old “rival” in quarterback Daniel Jones and a formidable running back in Jonathan Taylor. Jones continues to prove he’s mistake prone when trying to keep up with an offense on the other side. If Dallas can jump out to an early lead, this quarterback will certainly provide opportunities to make plays on the ball. The most important factor for the defense will be to limit Jonathan Taylor – a task that’s proven difficult for them against lesser competition. If the Colts are allowed to slowly and methodically march down the field behind a balanced attack, the Cowboys defense will once again be in for a difficult day. Dallas should win this game, favored by 5.5 points. But nobody in the fan base trusts them right now, and rightfully so. Hopefully this will be a week where we see the Cowboys put the other side away early, as the paper matchup indicates they should. But this team has not earned the right for us the believe that will be the case. And for most of us, regardless of the score, we’ll be holding our breath through the final whistle.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys vs. Colts recent history puts spotlight on coaching
summary: The Dallas Cowboys visit the Indianapolis Colts for the first time since 2018 this Sunday, and have played their way into a corner where this is an unfortunate bad versus bad game. Brian Schottenheimer’s Cowboys are yet again continuing their pattern of mostly alternating wins and losses, and only having losing streaks compared to winning […]
full_text: Photo by Greg Nelson /Sports Illustrated via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys visit the Indianapolis Colts for the first time since 2018 this Sunday, and have played their way into a corner where this is an unfortunate bad versus bad game. Brian Schottenheimer’s Cowboys are yet again continuing their pattern of mostly alternating wins and losses, and only having losing streaks compared to winning streaks, into November. They go to Indy with a 3-5 record, off a 33-30 overtime loss at home to the Cardinals. The Colts are off yet another loss at the Jaguars, but it marked their fourth straight to sit at 2-6 right now. The Colts have already accepted this 2026 campaign as a lost season, trading away players like Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner for future assets, with more personnel and coaching changes expected for a season that’s failed to match even mild-ish expectations. The Cowboys have done no such thing, teasing the possibility of actually being buyers in the trade market still with the awfulness of the NFC East adding fuel to this fire. There’s also been nothing but votes of confidence in the coaching staff, which again may be a two-fold result of still having a “winnable” division, as well as not having an obvious answer to who would replace Schottenheimer in-season if a change was made, nor Klayton Adams or Christian Parker. If the Cowboys want to continue selling any semblance of hope for this season, beating a team that’s already punted on that hope is obviously a must. Yes, we mostly said the same about the Cardinals game that was one of the worst collapses in recent memory, but at bare minimum that wasn’t an opponent that has given up. Getting in the win column in their third to last game before Thanksgiving, with another one of these also coming against a bad AFC South opponent the Titans, is the best the Cowboys can do this Sunday. Their absolute most recent game against the Colts came in Week 13 of 2022. The Cowboys had a second-year head coach just like they do now, but it was Mike McCarthy who beat the Colts 54-19 in Dallas. It was the third straight win of four in a row, all four in response to an overtime loss at the Packers. The Cowboys also beat the Vikings 40-3 in this stretch. The most recent away game in the series for Dallas came in 2018. The Cowboys were coming off of missing the playoffs in 2017 after Dak Prescott’s amazing rookie campaign of 2016, and patience was wearing thin for head man Jason Garrett, but more so offensive coordinator Scott Linehan. Presently, the Cowboys have these responsibilities both on Schotty’s shoulders as he is the play-calling head coach. These 2018 Cowboys were in the same position, 3-5, as the 2026 team. They won five straight to reach 8-5 by Week 15, but then were shutout for the first time since 2003 in a 23-0 loss at the Colts. The Cowboys got into Colts territory on the opening drive of the game but had a field goal blocked, got it into the red zone the next possession but turned it over on downs, then proceeded to punt twice, turn it over on downs two more times, and end the game with an interception. Blake Jarwin had the longest catch of the game for Dallas for 18 yards. The Colts defensive coordinator responsible for keeping the Cowboys off the scoreboard in this game? None other than Matt Eberflus, who had spent the last seven seasons as the Cowboys linebackers coach, and the 2016-17 seasons also taking on passing game coordinator duties. Cowboys fans worst nightmares about the predictability of Linehan’s offense were realized with the harshest reality check possible, a coach that worked in the same building as Linehan the year before having all of the answers to the test and shoving the Cowboys offense in a locker for four quarters. It is pretty wild to also consider the fact Eberflus parlayed this defensive coordinator job with the Colts into his first head coaching job with the Bears, and that was his final stop before returning to Dallas as DC to work with Schottenheimer last year. Eberflus is also now with the San Francisco 49ers, who are tied with the Vikings and Bills for having the best record in the NFL. If the Cowboys get this weekend’s win against the Colts, that elusive winning streak will be in play only by beating Eberflus and the 49ers back at home the following week. Today’s Cowboys almost assuredly don’t have the same luxury of being able to lose this game to the Colts and still make the playoffs as a 3-5 team that would fall to 3-6, but whether or not they’re even playoff worthy will have to remain a discussion even with a blowout win. It is an awkward spot to be in, and the hollowness of this game feels like a direct result of coaching malpractice – the seeds of which were planted as early as the last time the Cowboys were in Indianapolis, or possibly even earlier. It may not be far fetched at all to say both of these organizations coming into week nine have more to look forward to when they’ll be in Lucas Oil Stadium for the Combine this offseason, searching for the prospects that can turn fortunes around. The Colts have already positioned themselves to be ahead of the Cowboys (not a hard thing to do) in the offseason coaching search if they choose to do so though, as the realization of how much that matters has yet to hit Jerry Jones.
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys at Colts: Offensive, defensive impact players in Week 9
summary: Whether it’s due to talent or circumstances, certain players impact the game more than others week in and week out. The Dallas Cowboys have several such players who can help turn the tide at any moment in any given game. To hopefully get their season back on track and start stacking some wins together, they […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Whether it’s due to talent or circumstances, certain players impact the game more than others week in and week out. The Dallas Cowboys have several such players who can help turn the tide at any moment in any given game. To hopefully get their season back on track and start stacking some wins together, they need these players to step up now more than ever. In the Week 9 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts we believe the Cowboys have a player on each side of the ball who will impact the game in a big way in this week, and we discuss why these two individuals should help sway the game in the Cowboys favor. Offense – RB Javonte Williams The offensive game plan and play-calling for Brian Schottenheimer should be an easy one this week, run the ball early and often. The Indianapolis Colts currently ranked 27 th in the league in run defense, allowing 131.8 rushing yards per game. That should equate to a big game for Javonte Williams, and possibly Tyler Goodson as well. These two combined for nearly 200 total rushing yards a couple weeks ago against the Eagles and could duplicate that success in this Week 9 matchup with the Colts. We expect No. 33 to have a huge impact on the outcome of the game and predict he’ll have his second 100+ rushing yard performance of the season. This, of course, all hinges on how the offensive line performs. They’ve been a little hit and miss all season, but are at their best when run blocking. If everything comes together and plays out as we expect, Dallas’ run game should propel them to victory this week. Defense – DT Quinnen Williams Quinnen Williams got off to somewhat of a slow start to the 2026 season, but has recently been playing at an elite level. He completely dominated in what was unfortunately a losing effort last week against the Arizona Cardinals, collecting a couple of QB sacks. He dominate once again in this Week 9 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts, whose offensive line has been struggling, especially along the interior. Williams should be licking his chops for this matchup. We fully expect him to test the Colts rookie LG Jalen Farmer, a fourth-round pick this year, early and often. He replaced All-Pro Quenton Nelson after he was traded to the Seattle Seahawks a few weeks ago. This is a battle No. 92 should be able to easily exploit to his advantage, and in so doing, help secure the “W” for the Cowboys.

title: Broncos checked in on TE Trey McBride, but the Cardinals refused to trade him
summary: Well, that would have been fun. According to ESPN’s NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the Denver Broncos have been checking in around the league for tight end help, and even checked in on Cardinals star tight end Trey McBride. The Cardinals made it clear to the Broncos that they have zero intention of […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Trey McBride #85 of the Arizona Cardinals reacts to Brandon Jones #22 of the Denver Broncos during the third quarter of the game at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that would have been fun. According to ESPN’s NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the Denver Broncos have been checking in around the league for tight end help, and even checked in on Cardinals star tight end Trey McBride . The Cardinals made it clear to the Broncos that they have zero intention of trading the face of their franchise, and the Broncos have turned their attention elsewhere. The Denver Broncos have checked in around the league on tight ends, going so far as to ambitiously — and some would say outrageously — check on Cardinals star Trey McBride, who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. The Cardinals made it very clear they… https://t.co/fz5M8XuzSF pic.twitter.com/7M5uZb4uKo — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 7, 2026 Schefter and Rapoport added that the Broncos have checked in around the league for tight ends, including Cardinals star tight end Trey McBride, who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. Unfortunately for the Broncos, the Cardinals made it known they have no intention of trading away the face of their franchise. The Denver Broncos have checked in around the league on tight ends, going so far as to ambitiously — and some would say outrageously — check on Arizona Cardinals star Trey McBride, who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. The Cardinals made it very clear they have zero intention of trading McBride, and Denver turned its attention elsewhere. This has been a move many Broncos fans have been wanting them to make, and despite being in the basement of the NFC West once again, the Cardinals do not seem keen on the idea of trading away their star tight end. Still, it appears the Broncos are big fish hunting ahead of the trade deadline and would like to add a playmaker to their offense prior to the deadline this coming Tuesday. As we know, they have been connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, but their level of interest seems to have lowered recently, with the New York Giants being the main interested team there. McBride would have been a huge and unexpected splash, so now we have to ask: what do GM George Paton and HC Sean Payton have cooking? It’s clear they want to add a weapon to their offense and are willing to make a big splash if they can. The Colts are seeking a pricey package for Jonathan Taylor, and Trey McBride would have cost at least multiple 1st-round picks. So, what other running backs, tight ends, or, hell, even wide receivers are they looking to acquire? One tight end to potentially keep an eye on is Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert. The pass-catching tight end market is not very good, but Goedert does seem like a player who could be available. With that said, he was a free agent this past offseason, and the Broncos did not show much interest at all; he ended up re-signing with the Eagles on a one-year deal. A move at running back or tight end would make sense for the Broncos. The emergence of Jonah Coleman helps the Broncos’ backfield, but they still need more. Veteran JK Dobbins has really taken a step back this season and has struggled badly. Also, second-year back RJ Harvey and reserve/third down specialist Tyler Badie are currently on the IR. So, you could make a case that they need to add some depth to their running back room, even with Jonah Coleman playing well. As for tight end, they have veteran tight end Evan Engram who simply isn’t really used. He gets snaps but isn’t really targeted and feels like an afterthought in the offense. Adam Trautman is your blocking specialist and reserve/blocking tight end Nate Adkins leads the team in touchdown receptions (3), but only has 6 total receptions on the year. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos appear to be a team that will be very active ahead of the Deadline.

title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Denver Broncos latest news and rumors
summary: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline, but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way. As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far. We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It’s supposed to be an active deadline, so we’ll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days. Some notable trade Candidates Colts RB Jonathan Taylor Colts WR Josh Downs Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. Titans RB Tony Pollard Eagles TE Dallas Goedert Chargers EDGE Khalil Mack Cardinals EDGE Josh Sweat Jets RB Breece Hall Colts DT Grover Stewart Jets EDGE Will McDonald IV Eagles G Landon Dickerson Eagles CB Riq Woolen Titans WR Calvin Ridley Broncos news and rumors Broncos may explore adding a “weapon or two” prior to the deadline, per 9NEW Denver’s Mike Klis – Source Broncos are reportedly doing everything in their power to trade for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, per DNVR’s Zac Stevens – Source The Broncos might be a little less inclined to trade for Taylor now, according to SI’s Albert Breer – Source Veteran RB JK Dobbins name came up in trade talks, but that could be less likely now that RJ Harvey is on IR, per SI’s Albert Breer – Source Broncos have been calling around the league for tight end help, and even attempted to trade for Cardinals star TE Trey McBride, but the Cardinals were not interested – Source
