title: 6-2 Jaguars Facing Difficult Brian Thomas Balancing Act
summary: With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, few Jacksonville Jaguars storylines carry as much league-wide attention as the future of wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. His diminished role since Week 4 has fueled a steady stream of speculation about what it means for his long-term place in Jacksonville, and the answer is slightly more complicated […]
full_text: Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. runs onto the pitch ahead of the NFL London Games match at Wembley Stadium, London. Picture date: Sunday October 18, 2026. (Photo by Bradley Collyer/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, few Jacksonville Jaguars storylines carry as much league-wide attention as the future of wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. His diminished role since Week 4 has fueled a steady stream of speculation about what it means for his long-term place in Jacksonville, and the answer is slightly more complicated than simple usage charts suggest. New Layers to the Conversation In a recent report , NFL Network’s Cam Wolfe added some important context to the recent BTJ buzz. According to Wolfe, Thomas and Travis Hunter are close friends. Thomas is also well liked in the Jaguars’ locker room, and his speed remains an asset even without the production to match. Wolfe also reported that the Jaguars have wondered whether last year’s Tyson Campbell trade hurt their immediate locker room energy, and that the organization has “learned from it.” That last point deserves attention. After the Campbell trade to Cleveland in Week 6 of 2025, some players were reportedly unhappy with the move, and Jacksonville followed it with back-to-back tough losses to the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams. As is often the case in the NFL, winning will always cure the discomfort, however. The Jaguars closed out 2025 by going 9-1, and the locker room appeared no worse for wear. Still, it’s easy to see how that experience could shape the team’s approach to dealing with the third-year receiver this time around. However, it’s hard to argue that the team made the wrong 2025 decision, based on the on-field outcomes, and their defensive scheme not matching the player. That’s the key piece that makes this such a fascinating conversation. Where is the line between doing whatever is necessary to win versus doing what is needed for the locker room to be together? Usage Speaks Volumes The numbers, on the surface, show a player whose role has shrunk considerably. Thomas currently ranks fourth on the team in targets (21), fifth on the team in receptions through eight games played (10), and seventh in yards (117) behind rookie Josh Cameron who has 123. Over his last four games combined, he has just one catch, a 12-yard touchdown against the Indianapolis Colts. On Thursday, he logged only 19 snaps against the Baltimore Ravens, a game in which he was relegated to the fourth receiver spot. However, that trend didn’t start in Week 8. Thomas played a career-low 15 snaps against the Houston Texans in Week 6, before the Bye Week. After that game, head coach Liam Coen described the team’s confidence in Thomas as a week-to-week matter and said simply, “Guys have to step up and make plays.” Ahead of the Colts game, Coen expressed faith that Thomas would continue helping the offense make plays. He quickly supported that faith, securing the opening-drive touchdown, his lone catch of the game. Brian Thomas Jr. starts the scoring in Jacksonville! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TSkI5R33VG — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Meanwhile, around the league, interest is as real as ever. ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported that opposing teams are asking about Jacksonville’s plans for Thomas and are expected to continue reaching out before the November 10 deadline. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that several executives believe Thomas’s days in Jacksonville are numbered, and noted that a change of scenery could bring out the best in him. For a former 2024 Rookie of the Year finalist who topped 1,200 receiving yards as a rookie, that kind of interest is not surprising. What would be surprising is the team trading that caliber of player away for less than a first-round pick. Reduced Role a New Normal? Thomas is not publicly asking to be traded. By all accounts, he’s a hard worker and has embraced the team-first approach being built. But within Liam Coen’s offense, his role appears to be that of the sacrificial X, stretching the defense vertically to open space underneath for the middle-of-the-field throws that drive the scheme. With Trevor Lawrence at his best working inside the hashes, that job rarely comes paired with a major statistical output. Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington, Josh Cameron, and the Jacksonville tight end group all share that strength. Thomas doesn’t, and that’s okay. Thomas’ role can be valuable to the offense without ever showing up in his stat line, which is an extremely difficult reality for a player of his pedigree. Trevor Lawrence: Over the Middle ( @PFF ) – 90 / 116 (77.6%) – 1178 Yards – 12 TD / 2 INT – 136.3 RTG pic.twitter.com/y6Lag7EiFZ — Daniel Griffis (@DanDGriffis) November 6, 2026 Take the Baltimore matchup as an example: while Thomas was only on the field for 19 total snaps, he ran a route on 11 of Trevor Lawrence’s 26 pass attempts (42.3%). Meanwhile, the team built up a 20-point third quarter lead in the rainy Baltimore night. On those 11 dropbacks, Lawrence was 6/11 (54.5%) for 109 yards, with four of the team’s 11 passing first downs (36.4%), and the only passing touchdown – a 50 yarder to Parker Washington. The argument that BTJ pulls the primary coverage or opens up space could be supported. The BTJ Trade Deadline Question This is a delicate situation. The Jaguars have spent two years shaping a finely tuned locker room, and they’re looking to mold this roster into a legitimate Super Bowl contender. Trading away a well-liked player who is also a close friend of Hunter’s carries risks that don’t clearly show up on a stats sheet. For that reason, I expect Jacksonville to be buyers only at Tuesday’s deadline. Coen touched on the locker room impacts of prospective trades in his Friday media availability: “How does it affect things moving forward, cap, future, other players, how we can resign or not, other guys, there’s so much that goes into this time of the year. Also, being cognizant of the group that you have in the locker room and making sure that the guys all know in the building we’re trying to do everything we can as an organization to make the best decisions for the group and for our team, because those guys are so important to what we’re doing. It’s a fine line. It’s definitely a balancing act for sure, and everything that comes across your desk, you’ve got to make sure that you’re looking at it through that lens; at least we are.” The one exception I could see would be a trading partner offering a corresponding move that makes sense for both sides, such as a deal that returns defensive tackle or safety talent, which effectively forces the team’s hand in moving Thomas. With injuries already thinning the safety room, that kind of return is the only scenario where moving Thomas feels justified for a team with the roster Jacksonville has built.

title: Kingdom Keys: 3 Keys to a Chiefs victory over the Jets in Week 9
summary: After opening the season with five consecutive victories, the Kansas City Chiefs return to Arrowhead Stadium riding a two-game losing streak. The 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks was a poor performance in all three phases. Kansas City’s offense responded with 399 total yards and 24 points against the Denver Broncos, but the defense surrendered […]
full_text: East Rutherford, NJ October 1, 2023 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co After opening the season with five consecutive victories, the Kansas City Chiefs return to Arrowhead Stadium riding a two-game losing streak. The 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks was a poor performance in all three phases. Kansas City’s offense responded with 399 total yards and 24 points against the Denver Broncos , but the defense surrendered a late touchdown in a 28-24 loss. The Chiefs remain in the AFC West race and in contention for the AFC’s No. 1 seed, but they can no longer afford to lose games they are expected to win. The New York Jets are only 2-6 and have lost three consecutive games, but they have remained competitive. Quarterback Geno Smith is coming off a 290-yard, two-touchdown performance in which the Jets scored a season-high 33 points. Kansas City should win this game. To do so convincingly, it must accomplish these three things. Offensive key: Restore the vertical passing game Kansas City’s declining rushing production over the past two weeks has drawn plenty of discussion. After averaging 6.3 yards per carry and rushing for 665 yards over his first five games, Kenneth Walker III has been held to 105 rushing yards on 35 carries over the last two. That is an average of only 3.0 yards per attempt. Some of that decline can be attributed to offensive-line execution and opposing defenses adjusting to Kansas City’s running concepts. However, wide receiver Tyquan Thornton’s absence has also changed how defenses can play the Chiefs. Thornton was Kansas City’s primary field-stretching receiver. Before dislocating his ankle against the Las Vegas Raiders , he caught 11 passes for 219 yards — nearly 20 yards per reception. His final catch was a 55-yard gain against Cover 0 that demonstrated exactly what he provided: a receiver capable of making defenses pay for crowding the line of scrimmage. Walker still rushed for 128 yards against the Los Angeles Chargers after Thornton’s injury, so the receiver’s absence is not the only explanation for the recent struggles. But as teams have gained more film of the Thornton-less offense, they have become increasingly comfortable bringing safeties closer to the line and challenging Kansas City’s remaining receivers to win downfield. Through seven games, approximately 90% of Patrick Mahomes’ throws have traveled fewer than 20 yards beyond the line of scrimmage. Only 24 of his 232 attempts were directed 20 or more yards downfield, per statchasers.com . Kansas City does not need to throw deep on every possession. It must, however, prove that the threat exists. Head coach Andy Reid should create opportunities through play-action, max protection and pre-snap motion. Xavier Worthy is the most obvious candidate to assume more of that vertical responsibility, but Rashee Rice, Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen must also contribute. The objective is not simply to complete one long pass. Kansas City needs to make New York’s safeties respect the possibility. If the Chiefs can connect on multiple passes of at least 20 yards, the Jets will be forced to defend more of the field. That should create additional running room for Walker and restore the balance that powered Kansas City’s 5-0 start. Defensive key: Sack Nation must return Kansas City’s pass rush has not lived up to its nickname. The Chiefs enter Week 9 with nine sacks, ranking 30th in the NFL. Their 3.6% defensive sack rate is among the league’s worst. No player better represents those struggles than defensive tackle Chris Jones. The self-proclaimed CEO of “Sack Nation” has recorded only half a sack, three quarterback hits and one tackle for loss through seven games. During the losses to Seattle and Denver, Jones failed to register a tackle, quarterback hit or pass breakup across 87 combined snaps. Jones continues to command double teams, and his presence can create opportunities for teammates. But those opportunities only matter if someone capitalizes on them. Defensive end George Karlaftis has been Kansas City’s most consistent pass rusher, but Felix Anudike-Uzomah, Ashton Gillotte, R. Mason Thomas, and the rest of the defensive front must win more one-on-one matchups. Against Denver, the Chiefs pressured Bo Nix on only two of his 34 dropbacks—a 6% pressure rate, the lowest recorded by any NFL defense in a game this season. The Jets present an ideal opportunity for the pass rush to get healthy. Smith has already been sacked 23 times, and New York ranks 26th in sack rate allowed at 9.62%. Smith has otherwise played well, throwing 12 touchdowns against only three interceptions with a 104.5 passer rating. Kansas City cannot let him operate comfortably and push the ball downfield. The defensive benchmark should be at least three sacks, with Jones directly contributing to one of them —either by recording it himself or forcing Smith into another defender. This is the matchup in which Sack Nation needs to reappear. X-factor: Win on third down Third down will connect everything Kansas City wants to accomplish on Sunday. Offensively, the Chiefs have converted 34 of their 85 third downs, exactly 40%. The Jets’ defense has allowed opponents to convert 41 of 100 attempts. That presents Kansas City with an opportunity to extend drives and wear down an injury-affected New York defensive front. Mahomes cannot be asked to repeatedly rescue the offense on third-and-long. The Chiefs must use early-down runs, play-action passes, and quick completions to create manageable situations. The goal should be to convert at least 45% of their third downs. Defensively, Kansas City must get off the field. The season-long numbers are respectable, with opponents converting 39.2% of their third-down attempts. But Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs, including five situations requiring at least 9 yards. Those conversions let the Seahawks control the ball for nearly 36 minutes and limit Kansas City to only eight possessions. New York’s offense has converted 37.6% of its third downs this season. That is below the league’s better offenses, but Smith’s experience and willingness to push the football vertically make him dangerous if Kansas City cannot generate pressure. Third down is where Jones and the defensive line can change the game. A sack ends a possession, improves field position, and gives Mahomes another opportunity to attack a Jets defense allowing 23.5 points per game. Kansas City needs to win third down on both sides by extending its own possessions and quickly ending New York’s. The bottom line The Chiefs should not need Patrick Mahomes to carry them through another four-quarter fight against a 2-6 opponent. Kansas City must restore the deep-ball threat and force New York’s safeties away from the line of scrimmage. That will create more space for Kenneth Walker and prevent the offense from becoming predictable. Defensively, Chris Jones and Sack Nation must take advantage of an offensive line that has already allowed 23 sacks. On third down, the Chiefs must sustain their own drives while refusing to let the Jets control the clock. If Kansas City can produce multiple explosive passes, record at least three sacks and win the third-down battle, it should not merely end its losing streak — it should do so convincingly.

title: In Week 9’s ‘Reacts’ poll, Chiefs fans are worried about the offense
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week, we send out questions to the most plugged-in Kansas City Chiefs fans. You can see all of the recent survey results here. And be sure to check out FanDuel Sportsbook, the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation. Chiefs fans’ confidence What a difference […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts , a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week, we send out questions to the most plugged-in Kansas City Chiefs fans. You can see all of the recent survey results here . And be sure to check out FanDuel Sportsbook , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation. Chiefs fans’ confidence What a difference a few weeks makes. Last month, we ran the same poll, and 92% of Chiefs fans were confident the franchise was heading in the right direction. That was before back-to-back losses, one in the closing seconds to a division rival after a fourth-quarter collapse by all three phases. It was also back when Kenneth Walker III looked completely otherworldly, not just really, really, really good. It also doesn’t help that the Chiefs are coming off one of the worst statistical pass-rushing performances in recent memory. With the trade deadline around the corner, there is a feeling amongst some Chiefs fans that Kansas City needs to make a big move to keep from wasting a second straight year of quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ prime. So this could also be where the low confidence in the direction of the franchise. There is also the fringe group of fans whose faith in Andy Reid is starting to waver as well, as some of his past game management warts are starting to creep back up again on a roster that is not talented enough to cover up the blemishes. Whatever the reason is, there is only one way to raise confidence, and that’s by winning football games. They have a chance to start rebuilding the fans’ faith in them this week against the New York Jets . Where to worry It’s a little surprising to me that Chiefs Kingdom voted that 46% of you believe that Kansas City’s offense is their most worrisome unit right now. Especially coming off a game where the offense moved the ball relatively well against a really good defense. Now, obviously, late-game coaching decisions and the ability to punch the ball into the end zone on the final play into the decision, but given the special teams unit’s gaffes in recent weeks, I was sure that they would be selected as the unit causing the most hand-wringing. What this tells me is that Chiefs fans are worried that the offense’s issues are deeper and harder to fix than getting a new return man or kicker. Chiefs Kingdom is worried that our offensive tackles are subpar and we are in desperate need of more top-end talent at the wide receiver position. These things are harder to fix in season, and your votes reflect that. Click here to see other recent survey results.

full_text: (Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When Kansas City Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson flew downfield to finish off a 73-yard touchdown against the Denver Broncos , it was one of the season’s most exciting plays. Johnson’s first-career touchdown was memorable and worthy of a big celebration after the play, but thanks to quarterback Patrick Mahomes, the ball used on the play wasn’t lost in the hubbub. Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Patrick Mahomes showed again why he’s a great teammate after Emmett Johnson’s TD | The Kansas City Star This is something Mahomes has done frequently in the past, and it shows again why he’s such a great teammate. Mahomes did it in Super Bowl LVII so Skyy Moore got the ball after his first career touchdown reception. Xavier Worthy has the ball from his first NFL touchdown thanks to Mahomes. Ditto for former KC running back Isiah Pacheco. “I remember I got my first ball,” Mahomes said after getting Pacheco’s keepsake. “I can’t remember who gave me my first touchdown ball, but I remember getting that. That’s something I will keep it my entire life, and so I always think about when those guys (score) the first touchdown either for the Chiefs or for their first touchdown of their career, I always get that football to them.” Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy, lists Chiefs Super Bowl ring as collateral | The Athletic Among his assets, Rice included a 2023 Mercedes-Benz car estimated at $53,800, along with $5,000 in “NFL Jerseys & Hats,” $7,500 in clothing and apparel and a combined $13,600 in three separate checking accounts. He also listed $421,825 in expected deferred compensation. The document showed that Rice owes attorney Thomas McMurray $185,226.45. Of that, Rice’s Super Bowl LVIII ring is being kept for $160,000 in collateral. Other debts include $207,104.40 to First National Bank of Middle Tennessee for “business debt-personal guarantee” and $140,150 to First National Bank in Killeen, Texas, for an “unsecured” loan. NFL Week 9 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more | ESPN Chiefs’ Justin Fields will run a QB sneak The Chiefs continue to never run QB sneaks, and the yearly scrutiny over that decision has arrived this week following their late short-yardage failures against the Broncos. Kansas City has a big QB2 in Fields and loves to use funky packages featuring nose tackle Khyiris Tonga. Why not put the backup QB sneak on film … just to set up an inevitable fourth-down outside run that hits for an explosive play in six weeks? Struggling players at midseason: Is Justin Herbert broken beyond repair? Can DK Metcalf get right? | NFL.com Kingsley Suamataia KC | OG Will he bounce back in 2026? Suamataia always has a chance to improve in practice and perform better when he gets another opportunity to crack the starting lineup. However, the third-year pro’s résumé and reel suggest his struggles will continue because his talent hasn’t meshed with the Chiefs’ prescribed techniques. On the plus side, he’s still just 23 years old. Perhaps he can become a serviceable starter in time who holds his own when protected by a strong supporting cast. But the 2026 Chiefs’ O-line woes are so severe that it is hard to envision the third-year pro returning to prominence this season. Kansas City Chiefs to face New York Jets without three top draft picks | Chiefs Wire 2025 second-rounder Omarr Norman-Lott has also been ruled out for the AFC showdown. Delane is said to be dealing with a shoulder injury, Woods has what is being described as a “neck stinger,” and Norman-Lott is working his way back from a stint on injured reserve caused by his knee. While Delane and Norman-Lott were able to practice in a limited capacity over the past three days, Woods was the only Chiefs player who was held out of all of Kansas City’s workouts in Week 9. Around the NF L What I’m hearing about Derrick Henry, Jonathan Taylor, Garrett Wilson rumors at the NFL trade deadline | The Athletic The Jets have no desire or intention to trade wide receiver Garrett Wilson or running back Breece Hall, according to multiple sources. If you think I’m hedging, it’s only because I don’t think a right-minded Darren Mougey would turn down a huge haul for either player. But I don’t see one coming, either. “It is very unlikely to happen,” one team source says. Wilson, the 2022 Offensive Rookie of the Year, is on track for another 1,000-yard receiving season despite currently being in concussion protocol. Hall, who is expected to return this week from a Week 3 quad injury, is coming off his first 1,000-yard rushing season and was rewarded in the offseason with a three-year, $45.75 million contract extension. Colts in Daniel Jones trade talks as multiple teams call about QB, sources say | ESPN The Baltimore Ravens were one team to check in on Jones before they opted to trade for former Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. But the Ravens are hardly the only team to call the Colts about him, according to league sources. Speculation has also included the Minnesota Vikings, a team Jones has history with and a team with a Super Bowl-caliber defense that shouldn’t be ruled out. Rams’ Myles Garrett (knee) set to return this week vs. Commanders | Yahoo! Sports After back-to-back days of being limited in practice, Garrett is set to play Sunday when the Rams face the Washington Commanders barring any setbacks. The team opened his 21-day practice window this week. “He’s looking good, looking fast,” said Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald of Garrett. “[We’re] getting to work with him in full pads and playing off each other. It looked pretty good today, so I’m excited about having him here, having him back, and seeing what we do Sunday.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride What the Chiefs are saying about the Jets “Allen has had four really good games, and it feels like they want to feature the running back no matter who’s back there,” Spagnuolo pointed out. “I think they’re a little bit different, and yet I think they both run the scheme really well.” I think he looks Derrick Henry-ish to me sometimes,” Spags described Allen. ”He’s a big guy. So, we’ve got to be on point tackling. “It will all start with run defense, where Kansas City ranks eighth in rushing yards allowed per game (96) and third in yards per rushing attempt (3.5). The Seahawks ran for 153 yards a couple of weeks ago, but no other opponent has hit 120 or more yards against the Chiefs on the ground this season. title: Chiefs Market Movers: Who’s Trending at Midseason?
summary: Week 9 marks the halfway point of the 2026 NFL regular season. The Kansas City Chiefs will take on the New York Jets, but before we get to that game, let’s look at who’s trending up (the Bulls) and down (the Bears) for the Chiefs through eight weeks: Bulls Running back Emmett Johnson: The absolute […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 9 marks the halfway point of the 2026 NFL regular season. The Kansas City Chiefs will take on the New York Jets , but before we get to that game, let’s look at who’s trending up (the Bulls) and down (the Bears) for the Chiefs through eight weeks: Bulls Running back Emmett Johnson: The absolute star of the loss to the Denver Broncos , Emmett introduced himself to the NFL as a complementary back and as a kick returner. He’s elusive, explosive, and high energy. He can catch the football and break big plays. From here forward, he should be sharing touches with Ken Walker (maybe put them both on the field at the same time)— and could be that dude at kick returns if they let him. Wide receiver Rashee Rice: Rashee needs some good news this week. I’m sure that making this list will make up for what he’s got going on. Anyway, I do think the arrow is pointing back up for the current #1 wide receiver on the roster. The Broncos defended him pretty well (in both games), but this is still a 1,000-yard-type guy if he’s ever on the field for a full season again. Patrick Mahomes needs a reliable target who can get YAC—Rice is still perfect for that role, and he’s likely as hungry as he’s ever been. I wouldn’t be shocked if Rice has over 100 yds this week and/or next. Edge rusher R Mason Thomas: I am going to keep buying R Mason Thomas stock, because you just get the feeling it’s about to take off. The rookie leads the team in pressure rate and is second in sacks (yes, with one …). His snap share has declined the last two games— and the pass rush struggled in both (losses). RMT might be a guy who gets QB sacks in bunches, and the team needs him. Watch to see if he’s back to a bigger role this weekend. Others trending in the right direction: Mansoor Delane, George Karlaftis, Kahlil Benson, Cyrus Allen, Nohl Williams, Felix Anudike-Uzomah, Ashton Gillotte, Andrew Armstrong, Chris Roland-Wallace Bears Wide receiver Xavier Worthy: I still believe in this guy, but my hope for a breakout season is dwindling. He has elite ability, but execution and awareness have been… suboptimal. The fact that the Chiefs are (allegedly) aggressive in the wide receiver market isn’t a good sign for how they think of their recent 1st-round pick. At what point do they give up and make him a jet-sweep/tunnel-screen gadget guy only? Kicker Harrison Butker: It’s hard to pinpoint why a historically great (and clutch) kicker is suddenly costing his team every week. But it’s easy to see that it’s happening. Butker has missed more kicks than any other active kicker—and he’s been paid more than most. His contract makes it tough to cut him, but bringing in other kickers (however controversial) might lead to a change at some point. Offensive line coach Andy Heck: Along with head coach Andy Reid, the other Andy bears some responsibility for the struggles up front. Not only have they struggled to build enough depth to get through a season, but they also have fielded a group that gets penalized far more than is reasonable. On top of that, there are these mysterious issues that have led to a benching and a winding path to the Reserve/Injured list. Not to mention the best center in the NFL having a bad snap or two nearly every game. Oh, and apparently, protection was also to blame for the short-yardage failures and even the missed field goal (according to Andy). The big uglies continue to be a problem that seems beyond the Chiefs’ ability to solve— even after it has cost them dearly in multiple Super Bowls. Others trending in the wrong direction: Jaylon Moore, Jack Cochrane, Harrison Butker, Nikko Remigio, Creed Humphrey, Kingsley Suamataia, Chris Jones Value (sleeper) picks: Jacob De Jesus : Chiefs Twitter thought it was funny that he was signed in the midst of wide receiver trade talks. He’s not the answer at wide receiver, but he could be an elite punt returner if given a chance… Ben VanSumeren : Given the short-yardage struggles, it’s time to get behind a fullback. Justin Fields : Given the goal-line struggles, it’s past time to get Fields behind Trey Smith and Creed as needed for a push.

title: Chiefs-Jets Madden Simulation Week 9: Get Right Week
summary: On Sunday, the (5-2) Kansas City Chiefs are back at Arrowhead taking on the (2-6) New York Jets. Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 27. Note: Madden simulation is 6-1 this season, predicting the outcome. First quarter The Kansas City Chiefs received the opening kickoff and wasted no time getting the […]
full_text: On Sunday, the (5-2) Kansas City Chiefs are back at Arrowhead taking on the (2-6) New York Jets . Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. Note: Madden simulation is 6-1 this season, predicting the outcome. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here . First quarter The Kansas City Chiefs received the opening kickoff and wasted no time getting the offense going. At midfield, Patrick Mahomes lobbed a pass down the left sideline to Kenneth Walker, who was running a wheel route. Walker hauled it in and took it all the way to the Jets’ four-yard line. The New York Jets defense attempted to stand tall, but on third-and-four, Mahomes found Travis Kelce on a slant route in the end zone for a touchdown. The Jets could potentially welcome back running back Breece Hall after his quad injury. On their first five plays, Hall had his hands on the football. His biggest play came on a 16-yard run straight up the middle. Felix Anudike-Uzomah got to Geno Smith for a sack, forcing the Jets to punt. End of first quarter: Chiefs 7, Jets 0 Second quarter The Chiefs picked up one first down but couldn’t get past midfield. Matt Araiza came on to punt the ball back to the Jets. The Chiefs defense quickly got the ball back as Chris Jones and George Karlaftis teamed up to sack Geno Smith on third down, forcing a three-and-out. Mahomes connected with Kelce twice for 37 yards, moving the Chiefs inside the five-yard line. After a play that resulted in a 10-yard loss, Mahomes went right back to Kelce in the end zone for his second touchdown of the game. At their own 24-yard line, Hall took a handoff straight up the middle, broke a tackle, and made several defenders miss on his way to the end zone. A 76-yard touchdown run brought the Jets back into the game. Rashee Rice picked up a first down on a drag route to midfield. On the very next play, Mahomes delivered a strike to Xavier Worthy, who ran a corner route before cutting upfield and racing into the end zone for a 50-yard touchdown. Jadon Canady intercepted Smith with 49 seconds remaining at the Jets’ 44-yard line. The Chiefs failed to capitalize on the opportunity before halftime. End of second quarter: Chiefs 21, Jets 7 Third quarter The Jets quickly went three-and-out. During the drive, Mansoor Delane came screaming off the edge on a blitz and brought down Smith for a sack. The Chiefs controlled the majority of the quarter, putting together a lengthy drive deep into Jets territory. At the 10-yard line, Mahomes kept the ball on a read option and took a massive hit before being brought down at the two-yard line. On third-and-goal from the two, Walker caught a screen pass from Mahomes and reached the end zone for a touchdown, giving the Chiefs a three-score lead. Karlaftis got to Smith for another sack, forcing the Jets to punt once again. End of third quarter: Chiefs 28, Jets 7 Fourth quarter On the first play of the quarter, Walker broke free and reached the Jets’ 16-yard line. Worthy followed it up by catching a touchdown pass in the end zone, giving the Chiefs a four-possession lead. The Jets managed to put together a 12-play scoring drive, capped off by an Adonai Mitchell touchdown. New York attempted an onside kick, but Jalen Royals had other plans. Royals recovered the football and returned it all the way to the four-yard line. However, Mahomes threw an interception, giving the Jets possession once again. Facing fourth-and-goal from the nine-yard line, Smith lobbed a pass toward the corner of the end zone, where Tim Patrick hauled it in for a touchdown. Final score: Chiefs 35, Jets 21 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 26 for 30 passing, 320 yards, 5 touchdowns, 1 interception, 5 rushes, 21 yards. Kenneth Walker: 9 rushing attempts, 78 yards, 8 receptions, 88 yards, 1 touchdown. Travis Kelce: 6 receptions, 87 yards, 2 touchdowns. Rashee Rice: 5 receptions, 51 yards. Xavier Worthy: 4 receptions, 71 yards, 2 touchdowns. Khyiris Tonga: 1 sack Mansoor Delane: 1 sack Felix Anudike-Uzomah: 1 sack George Karlaftis: 1 sack Chris Jones: 1 sack Drue Tranquill: 1 sack Jadon Canady: 1 interception. Geno Smith: 15 for 23 passing, 175 yards, 2 touchdowns, 1 interception. Breece Hall: 12 rushing attempts, 119 yards, 1 touchdown, 4 receptions, 30 yards Adonai Mitchell: 4 receptions, 53 yards, 1 touchdown Next week, the Chiefs are back on the road heading to Hotlanta to visit the Atlanta Falcons . Until then, we will see how it is played out inside the EA Universe.

title: Chiefs-Jets Week 9 Final Injury Report: Mansoor Delane ruled out
summary: Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 9, the Chiefs play the New York Jets on Sunday afternoon. Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website: Chiefs “Both those two… are making progress, […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 9, the Chiefs play the New York Jets on Sunday afternoon. Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website : Chiefs Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) was ruled out after missing practice all week. He suffered the injury early in the Week 8 loss; he walked gingerly to the sideline without stopping the game after taking on an open-field block. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) was ruled out after limited participation in practice all week. He has been dealing on and off with the same shoulder injury since training camp and missed last week’s game against the Denver Broncos . “Both those two… are making progress, and that’s a positive thing, but they’re going to be out this game,” Reid said during his Friday press conference. “It’s just a matter of getting back and making sure they’re strong; both of them, it’s a strength thing right now,” Reid said before alluding to the fact that both could be fine over the next week or so. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was ruled out after limited practice for the two weeks since being designated to return from the Reserve/Injured list; next week is the final week before he must be activated on the 53-man roster. Returner Nikko Remigio (hip) was listed as questionable after upgrading to full participation in practice Friday and Thursday from being limited Wednesday. The team signed undrafted rookie wideout Jacob De Jesus to the practice squad this week, who has preseason reps as a returner for the Chiefs. Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was a full participant in practice on Friday and Thursday after being marked as limited on Wednesday. He has no game designation heading into Week 9. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was a full participant in practice on Friday and Thursday after being marked as limited on Wednesday. He has no game designation heading into Week 9. The following Chiefs players were full participants in practice all week and have no game designation: Linebacker Nick Bolton (neck) Linebacker Drue Tranquill (pectoral) Quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) Jets No. 1 wide receiver Garrett Wilson entered concussion protocol on Monday after a helmet-to-helmet hit in Week 8 and was ruled out for this week. He has racked up 527 yards and three touchdowns over 43 receptions this season. Starting defensive tackle Harrison Phillips (ankle) was listed as questionable after he did not participate in Wednesday or Thursday practice, but was a full participant on Friday. He has 24 tackles, three quarterback hits, and a fumble recovered while playing 57% of the defensive snaps for New York this season. The Jets placed defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat (knee) on the Reserve/Injured list last week. Rookie phenom edge rusher David Bailey (groin) has no game designation after he was upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice after being limited Wednesday and missing Week 8. He has 5.5 sacks and seven tackles for loss while playing 81% of the Jets’ defensive snaps. Tight end Mason Taylor (back) has no game designation and was a full participant in Thursday’s and Friday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday; he missed time earlier in the season due to a thumb injury. Starting running back Breece Hall (knee) has been on the IR since Week 3 but will return this week after fully particpating in practice on Thursday and Friday.He has 265 total yards and a touchdown this season. His backup, Braelon Allen, has 565 rushing yards and three touchdowns in relief. Rookie safety VJ Payne of Kansas State saw his practice window open for the first time this season after suffering an injury in the preseason; he was listed as questionable to play.

title: Chiefs-Jets Week 9 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
summary: It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the New York Jets — in their first matchup since 2023 — our writers predicted the final score and result. The 206 Jets are likely more focused on evaluating head coach Aaron Glenn — and […]
full_text: (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the New York Jets — in their first matchup since 2023 — our writers predicted the final score and result. The 206 Jets are likely more focused on evaluating head coach Aaron Glenn — and the likelihood of having a trio of top ten selections in April’s NFL Draft — than what happens the rest of the season. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 9.5-point home favorites. Although the Jets lost to the Las Vegas Raiders 38-33 in Week 8, Gang Green did rack up 439 yards of offense, including 166 rushing yards. New York should not be considered a pushover opponent. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) It’s been a hard fortnight to be a Chiefs fan. I am still of a mindset to see how this team looks at the end of the season, but losing any of the next three games would be catastrophic for the season. Earlier on, I was worried about the Chiefs sleeping on a team like the Jets. But after losing two straight games, I think the Chiefs will come out and play one of their best games of the season. The concern will remain of what happens against good teams, but I don’t think you will see a play with their food performance at Arrowhead following a tough two-game road trip. Chiefs 31, Jets 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) After consecutive losses, the Chiefs badly need a win to get back on track. The Jets are a far cry from as bad as they have been in recent memory, but the Chiefs should win this game with minimal issues. The Jets are more talented offensively than they have been in some time, but running back Breece Hall has missed time this season with injury, and wide recieve Garret Wilson has shown up on the injury report. With a quality defense ranked near the top in several categories, the Chiefs will need to bring their A-game. Kansas City played a solid game offensively, but this week all eyes will be on the short-yardage and red zone situations where the team failed to convert in critical spots last week. Defensively, a turnaround game for the pass rush would be a big boost.I would continue to watch the emergence of Emmet Johnson alongside Kenneth Walker in creating a two-headed monster in the KC backfield. Chiefs 26, Jets 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I think the Chiefs are gonna handle the Jets at Arrowhead this week. If Garrett Wilson can’t go, the Jets lose their best threat in the passing game, and Spags can load up on the run and make them beat Kansas City through the air. If Mahomes gets the Chiefs up two scores early, I don’t see how the Jets keep up. I think this one gets out of hand in the second half. Chiefs 31, Jets 17 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The Chiefs enter a three-game stretch that feels critical to keeping their AFC West title and No. 1 seed hopes within reach. After starting 5-0, Kansas City has dropped two straight, and the losing streak needs to stop Sunday against the Jets. New York has remained competitive, but this is a team the Chiefs should beat, especially back at Arrowhead in front of a crowd eager for something to celebrate. Garrett Wilson’s uncertain availability could hurt the Jets, although Braelon Allen has proven their running game deserves respect regardless of Breece Hall’s status. For Kansas City, getting Kenneth Walker III going starts with making defenses respect the passing game again. To me, his recent struggles go beyond the running back and offensive line. Tyquan Thornton’s absence has taken away a deep threat, allowing defenses to crowd the line of scrimmage. The Chiefs must find ways to stretch the field without him, create room for Walker and get back to building off play-action. I expect Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid to find those answers this week, with Kansas City settling down and delivering a convincing win. Chiefs 27, Jets 13 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) The New York Jets come to town at a pretty good time for the Chiefs. Having lost the past two games, they’ll be hungry to get back in the win column. Andy Reid has rightfully been blamed for the team’s failures over the last couple of weeks, so I’d expect at least a “B” game plan on Sunday. He should let Kingsley come back as the left guard, and Rashee Rice is getting healthier— these two developments alone could get the offense moving enough to beat the Jets. But the Chiefs also have developing weapons in Emmett Johnson and Cyrus Allen. Both rookies should continue to see increased touches every week from here to the postseason (in my humble opinion). I’m of the opinion that the Chiefs are still in pretty good shape overall— the Denver loss hurt, but KC looked like the better squad. The Jets aren’t as bad as their record either, so this won’t be a cakewalk, but I expect the home crowd will have plenty to cheer about. Chiefs 28, Jets 13 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) I hope the Chiefs are as angry as the fan base after that last game. Because they need to play angry, even against the Jets, if they’re going to turn this season around. Now in a fight for the division, the Chiefs must take advantage of these next three games against what seems like inferior opponents. While I have serious concerns about this football team, I believe they get back in the win column this weekend. The offense should be able to get in a rhythm and right some of their wrongs from the past two weeks. And for the Jets, if Garrett Wilson can’t go, then I think the Chiefs’ defense should hold their own and focus on shutting down their running game. Chiefs win fairly comfortably in this one. Chiefs 28, Jets 17 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) It’s been a rough couple of weeks. The Chiefs have lost back-to-back games. But they played well enough in Denver that they should have won that game. Some poor coaching decisions and a few mental lapses are all it takes in the NFL to lose to a division rival. That being said, this should be a get-right game for the Chiefs. The New York Jets are having a very Jets-like year and have struggled to move the ball and score points. They are also averaging 123.6 yards allowed per game on the ground. The Chiefs should plan on dealing a healthy dose of Kenneth Walker III and Emmett Johnson to them. This could be the perfect get-right game for Kansas City. Chiefs 24, Jets 10 Nate Christensen The Jets have been a better team this year. Their offense has dramatically improved with Geno Smith at quarterback and an impressive set of weapons. Braelon Allen has broken out at running back. Adonai Mitchell, Garrett Wilson, and Omar Cooper have formed a good trio. They have good young tight ends and two top-10 draft picks at tackle. Their offense can score and keep them in games The issue has been their defense, which is bad. They don’t have a lot of talent, particularly in the secondary. I think the Chiefs should easily be able to throw the ball this week, and I expect Kenneth Walker to bounce back with a big game. Chiefs 34, Jets 23 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) Welcome to Game 1 of three that the Chiefs are fully expected to win, similar to the first five games of the season. The Jets are talented on offense and competitive on defense; they have too many recent first-round picks not to be, but there’s nothing Aaron Glenn and company can do about Kansas City needing a confidence-building win after two straight losses. Look for the Chiefs’ run game to come alive again and marry it to a passing attack that found answers against the Broncos last week until the final play. Whether the wide receivers are a big part of the game plan, I see Kansas City lighting up the scoreboard and putting this game out of reach in the second half. full_text: (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images In our “Let’s Argue” series, Mark Gunnels considers the hot takes, wacky predictions and unpopular opinions of Kansas City Chiefs fans from all over the world. We need to tear it down and build back up: I’m with you on the holes, especially in the trenches and at receiver, but I don’t think the Chiefs need to tear it all down. Give Mahomes a legit No. 1 receiver, get better up front on both sides of the ball, and I think we’re right back in the Super Bowl mix. I’d rather see them make those moves now than spend a year of Mahomes’ prime digging out of dead money. Jets agree to trade Garrett Wilson to KC: On Friday morning, the Jets announced that Garrett Wilson (concussion) would be ruled out for this game. Man, I’d love this. Garrett Wilson would be a home run for the Chiefs and give Mahomes a legit No. 1 receiver. The catch is that with the dead money the Jets would have to eat, I could see them asking for two first-round picks, and that might be too rich for Brett Veach’s blood. Wouldn’t shock me if the Chiefs miss the playoffs: I think this is a massive overreaction, Casey. I’d bet the seven AFC teams in playoff position right now are the same seven that get in, and the odds Justis Mosqueda shared from The Athletic’s simulator show why: the Chiefs are at 84%, all seven are at 78% or higher, and Cleveland is the closest team on the outside at 43%. I’m way more worried about where the Chiefs are seeded than whether they get in.

title: What the Chiefs are saying about the Jets
summary: In Week 9, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the New York Jets near the midpoint of the 2026 regular season. The game at Arrowhead Stadium will feature a coaching matchup of second-year head coach Aaron Glenn and Chiefs head coach Andy Reid in his 28th season. At the podium Wednesday, Reid looked forward to […]
full_text: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 9, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the New York Jets near the midpoint of the 2026 regular season. The game at Arrowhead Stadium will feature a coaching matchup of second-year head coach Aaron Glenn and Chiefs head coach Andy Reid in his 28th season. At the podium Wednesday, Reid looked forward to the matchup with New York by describing the team Kansas City hasn’t faced in three years. The Chiefs won a road game on “Sunday Night Football” 23-20 in Week 4 of the 2023 season. “They’re very physical on both sides of the ball,” Reid said. “Scoring a lot of points on the offensive side, and their defense – they’ve got a lot of different looks that they’re going to present. Solid veteran players that do a nice job for them.” Glenn, a former NFL cornerback and Detroit Lions defensive coordinator, is organizing a unit that just allowed 38 points to the Las Vegas Raiders at home last week. However, this season, New York ranks 11th in total yards allowed per game (318) and allows the fifth-lowest rate of passing yards per game (194). “They’ve got some good veteran guys, whether it’s the safeties, the linebackers. You’re not going to have things that are botched up,” Reid shared. “They do a good job of making sure they can adjust to most things and do it accurately. Then they’ve got some guys on the front that are good football players, big guys. They’re good players. They’ve got some good speed on the outside.” Whether it’s linebacker Demario Davis or safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, the Jets made sure to bring in veterans to lead Glenn’s group this season. Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy pointed out the style of defense Glenn has instilled. “They play extremely hard,” Bieniemy pointed out. “They play fast and A.G.,obviously, they haven’t had the best of luck, but when you turn that tape on, they get your attention.” On the flip side, the Chiefs’ defense will face a hot Jets offense. They have scored 58 points over the last two weeks, and first-round rookies in wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. and tight end Kenyon Sadiq have had big games around No. 1 wide receiver Garrett Wilson. With Wilson in concussion protocol this week, Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is still ready to defend downfield passes from veteran quarterback Geno Smith, who was once his quarterback when he was defensive coordinator and interim head coach of the New York Giants in 2017. Smith was also the quarterback for the Raiders when Kansas City pitched a 31-0 shutout with just four first downs allowed in Week 7 last year. “I’ve always had a lot of respect for Geno,” Spags said. “I’ve always had a great deal of respect for how smart he is and his rocket arm; he has a really strong arm. I put like three clips on yesterday of him from one side of the field throwing all the way [to the other], an out cut, deep to a number of different receivers. You know how talented and young they are, and they can all run that route. So we’re alerted to what kind of quarterback we’re dealing with.” Jets have had six players with 100+ receiving/rushing yard games so far this season – Garrett Wilson – AD Mitchell – Omar Cooper Jr. – Kenyon Sadiq – Braelon Allen – Breece Hall More than any team in the NFL… pic.twitter.com/8O7TWfprxo — BetMGM 🦁 (@BetMGM) November 4, 2026 Spagnuolo then alluded to the Jets’ league-leading six players with 100-yard games this season, including running back Braelon Allen, who has stepped in since a groin injury to starter Breece Hall; Hall is expected to play on Sunday afternoon, but both backs look like threats to the coach. “Allen has had four really good games, and it feels like they want to feature the running back no matter who’s back there,” Spagnuolo pointed out. “I think they’re a little bit different, and yet I think they both run the scheme really well.” I think he looks Derrick Henry-ish to me sometimes,” Spags described Allen. ”He’s a big guy. So, we’ve got to be on point tackling.” It will all start with run defense, where Kansas City ranks eighth in rushing yards allowed per game (96) and third in yards per rushing attempt (3.5). The Seahawks ran for 153 yards a couple of weeks ago, but no other opponent has hit 120 or more yards against the Chiefs on the ground this season.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Chiefs-Jets: 5 Things to Watch in Week 9 matchup
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) will take on the (2-6) New York Jets Sunday afternoon in an AFC showdown. The game kicks off at 12:00 PM Arrowhead time and will be broadcast on CBS. The Chiefs, losers of two straight, lost a heartbreaker last week, 28-24 to the Denver Broncos. The Chiefs controlled most of […]
full_text: (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) will take on the (2-6) New York Jets Sunday afternoon in an AFC showdown. The game kicks off at 12:00 PM Arrowhead time and will be broadcast on CBS . The Chiefs, losers of two straight, lost a heartbreaker last week, 28-24 to the Denver Broncos . The Chiefs controlled most of the game, but a fourth-quarter offensive meltdown and major defensive breakdowns let the Broncos snatch a late victory. The Jets also lost last week, falling to the Las Vegas Raiders 38-33. With three straight losses, the Jets are among the bottom dwellers in the AFC, despite having a roster with quality talent in multiple critical positions. The Chiefs need a win to keep pace in the AFC standings, while the Jets are seeking a signature win for second-year head coach Aaron Glenn: Here are five things to watch 1. Emmett Johnson ’s usage This season, Johnson has shown flashes of the player he can become, but this week against Denver, he exploded onto the scene with a massive game. With 145 all-purpose yards and a touchdown, he was voted NFL Rookie of the Week. Johnson had been quiet up to this point in terms of production, but his ability to break tackles had drawn attention and was on full display as he ran all over the Denver defense. Had them on the ropes. Look how excited 15 was. pic.twitter.com/mjIekz1G7p — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 3, 2026 Johnson is the Chiefs’ third-leading receiver behind only Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice, ahead of players like Xavier Worthy and Noah Gray. The Chiefs offense needs help not only finding explosive playmakers, but also finding consistent playmakers. Johnson can be both, and the Chiefs should get him the ball more often. Emmett Johnson is HUMAN ELECTRICITY ⚡ pic.twitter.com/wxUiYBG70p — PFF (@PFF) November 5, 2026 2. Stuffing Braelon Allen Jets star running back Breece Hall was a full participant in Thursday’s practice after being on the Reserve/Injured list since Week 3. The Jets’ run game didn’t skip a step, and his backup Braelon Allen has stepped in and stepped up. Allen has rushed for over 100 yards in three of his last four games and has been the driving force in New York’s offense. Braelon Allen just put together the best rushing performance of his NFL career. 21 CAR, 147 RUSH YDS, 1 TD, 2 REC, 6 REC YDS With Breece Hall sidelined, Allen has now surpassed 100 scrimmage yards in each of his first 7 career starts. pic.twitter.com/aqcqSZbVkY — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 1, 2026 Allen is poised for a bright career, but Kansas City should be able to stop him. The Chiefs’ defense currently ranks 8th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game at 96.3. Linebacker Nick Bolton is tied for 10th in the NFL this season with 68 total tackles and will play arguably the biggest role in stopping Allen on Sunday. Allen may be young, but Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo made sure to give him his due in Thursday’s media availability. I think he looks (Ravens RB) Derrick Henry-ish to me sometimes,“ Spags described Allen. ”He’s a big guy. So, we’ve got to be on point tackling.” If Hall does indeed return, it will be interesting to see how the Jets divide their touches against the Chiefs. 3. Rookie edge rushers This week will feature two of the NFL’s premier rookie pass rushers. The Jets defense will feature No. 2 overall draft pick David Bailey coming off the edge, while the Chiefs more so rotate in second-round pick R Mason Thomas. Bailey was the cream of the crop for pass rushers in this past year’s draft and is already the Jets’ best pass rusher, with 5.5 sacks so far this season. Bailey (groin) missed last week with an injury, but he practiced in full on Thursday and is trending toward playing Sunday. “David Bailey with his 3rd sack of the day no celly at all… this guy has no social media he's a different type of cat all he does is go home and study pass rush” pic.twitter.com/PjNpDOuclK — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) October 11, 2026 Bailey will draw most of the headlines, but the Chiefs have their own young, budding pass rusher. . @ByNateTaylor cooking on @ChiefsHMA “R Mason Thomas in 81 plays as a pass rusher has 20 wins. Ranks 13th in pass rush win rate when giving true chances to rush the passer in dropback settings.” — SleeperChiefs (@SleeperChiefsKC) November 3, 2026 While Thomas has been a rotational player for the Chiefs so far this season, he has been productive and disruptive on the snaps he has seen. On the interception, R Mason Thomas got the pressure that forced the bad throw. Good hand swipe and a nice power move to push the LT into the pocket. pic.twitter.com/GvoTEFRtw2 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) October 27, 2026 The Chiefs only have nine sacks as a team so far this season, and defensive end George Karlaftis is the only player with more than one. Thomas has seen a slight dip in snaps the last two weeks, but the Chiefs should look to up his pass-rush looks, especially on obvious passing downs. Both offensive lines will have their work cut out, and each rookie rusher can change the game for their team. 4. Field Goal unit At this point in the season, it is not a matter of whether Harrison Butker will miss a kick; it is a matter of when, and that thought should linger in the Chiefs’ minds when they get into fourth-down situations across midfield. Butker missed a critical kick late in the game in Denver, allowing the Broncos to turn around and quickly take the late lead. Many suspected it could be the end of Butker in Kansas City, but this week the Chiefs coaching staff stood behind their long-time kicker. “You exhaust every possibility to get this guy right, Toub told reporters on Thursday. ”And that’s what we’re doing right now. We’re not just going to pull the plug.” “Butker’s our kicker,” Toub continued. ‘He’s on our team, and we’re paying Butker. And Butker has won a lot of football games for us. Butker is a champion. And he deserves the right to be exhausted on this thing, and we’re going to exhaust every possibility with him.” Regardless of the confidence, fourth-down situations will get even more interesting once the Chiefs get past midfield. I would expect to see the Chiefs punt in fourth-and-long situations this week if they do get into what was once Butker’s range. The team ranks 17th in the league with a 53.85% conversion rate on fourth down, and it will be interesting if they decide to attack these situations moving forward. 5. A potential quarterback sneak? Short-yardage ineptitude led to disaster for the Chiefs’ offense last week, and this week speculation rose about an ongoing issue. Mahomes has not run a quarterback sneak since a freak injury in October 2019, and while the team has run it with other players taking the snap, they haven’t shown the look in quite some time. In Denver, the Chiefs failed on three straight snaps from the one-yard line, and this week both Mahomes and Reid were questioned about the willingness to run a quarterback sneak. Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes were asked about the QB sneak. Mahomes says, "It's not like we're scared to call the quarterback sneak. It's just something that we haven't done. We've been able to execute with other things… If we can't execute with the other things, I'm sure… pic.twitter.com/dExgaQ44zK — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) November 4, 2026 The Chiefs brass did their best to dispel the notion that they were afraid to let Mahomes sneak the ball in short-yardage situations, but their actions say otherwise. An early November matchup against the Jets might not be the time for Mahomes to reintroduce the quarterback sneak, but it will be worth watching how the Chiefs handle short-yardage situations.

title: Chargers-Texans Game Preview: Can 2 returning starters on offense make the difference?
summary: The Chargers are back inside SoFi Stadium to face the Texans (2-5) this Sunday. It’s been hell for Justin Herbert and the offense all year, but it’s been just as rough when they’ve played the Texans each of the past two seasons. Houston has picked off Herbert five times and chances are they’ll add to […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (83) limps off the field during the NFL game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chargers are back inside SoFi Stadium to face the Texans (2-5) this Sunday. It’s been hell for Justin Herbert and the offense all year, but it’s been just as rough when they’ve played the Texans each of the past two seasons. Houston has picked off Herbert five times and chances are they’ll add to that total this weekend given how things have gone for two months of the season now. Can they FINALLY shock the fan base and dig out their first win? Will the woes continue against Houston? I guess we have to tune in to find out. Here are the three things I’ll be watching the closest when these two teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) How will the Chargers offense look with reinforcements en route? The Chargers offense will hopefully look a bit different this week with a pair starters returning to the fold. Tight end David Njoku had his activation window opened this week and has logged a pair of limited practices this week. He was one of Justin Herbert’s top targets through the team’s first two games and I’ll be interested to see if that continues once he’s back. Kayode Awosika, the team’s starting left guard to begin the season, also looks to be making his way back to the field after a pair of limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Awosika was one of the offensive line’s best performance before going down with a fibula injury and I wouldn’t be shocked if his presence next to Joe Alt on the left side moves the needle — in some way at least — on offense this week. Njoky being a pass-catching tight end first and forement could help the passing game while Awosika’s return could potentially open up things on the ground. Now of course one player in each facet likely isn’t enough to be a true fix, but that unit needs anything at all and two former starters returning to the field is a good start. 2.)Will the nightmare continue for Justin Herbert against the Texans? The last two times Justin Herbert and the Chargers have faced the Texans have been a nightmare. In last year’s matchup on December 25th, the Chargers lost 20-16 in a game Herbert threw one touchdown to one interception. The prior game against Houston was the wild card matchup in January of ‘25 where Herbert threw four interceptions in one of his worst outings as a pro. As much as I wish I could say this is a real opportunity to exorcise the demons from those two games, I simply cannot. Herbert and the Chargers have never looked like a worse, less-cohesive unit and even with the Houston defense not its usual elite self, they still have numerous players who can make a splash play at a moment’s notice. Even the return of a healthy Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Tre’ Harris did next to nothing for the offense’s production in Week Eight. Coming out of the bye, the Chargers scored just nine points, all of which came in the first half. They were then completely blanked in the second as Herbert threw his second interception on top of nearly losing a fumble that was luckily knocked out of bounds. At this rate, nothing is going to come to save the Chargers from themselves. If they want the nightmare to end, they’ve gotta wake up and do it themselves. 3.) Chargers pass defense will have another tough task vs. WR Nico Collins and a rejuvenated C.J. Stroud Stroud did not have to play at an All-Pro or Pro Bowl level the past two seasons while the Texans defense was arguably the best in the league from 2024-2025. This year, with the defense taking some steps back, he’s had to carry the load a bit more and that’s somewhat worked out after a rough start. The Texans are the NFL’s 7th-ranked passing offense and that is mainly due to an abysmal run game averaging only 84.7 yards per game (29th). After throwing for at least 260 yards in Weeks Four through Six (including two games of over 300), Stroud only threw for 153 in their loss to the Giants just before their bye. With two weeks of preparation, you have to think they’ll be ready to roll. On the flip side, the Chargers pass defense currently ranks 7th in the league, as well (198.4). That rank has mostly been maintained without All-Pro safety Derwin James or veteran cornerback Donte Jackson in the lineup. If that’s not the far-and-away strength of the Bolts defense, then I don’t know what is. Just a bunch of names putting together a top-10 unit under a first-year defensive coordinator. Will that be enough this week?

full_text: Aaron Donald almost recovered a fumble in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and had Donald actually recovered that ball, he may have scored a touchdown. Instead, Donald botched the recovery and he was left with nothing. "If anybody knew how hard it is at our age to go down there and get a ball." Matthew Stafford felt for Aaron Donald after he missed the mark on the fumble recovery 😭 @insidethenfl Week 8 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/vOfSbC7kj4 — NFL (@NFL) November 2, 2026 If you watch Donald talk about it, underneath the laugher for this blunder, he knows he needs to be better. He talks about the reality that if the Rams didn’t win, or if they were trailing, not recovering the ball wouldn’t have been such a laughing matter. Donald wants to be better for the Rams, and the Rams will need him and everyone to play at their best to recover from their 4-4 start. Rams’ Aaron Donald Breaks Down Viral Muffed Fumble Opportunity (sports.yahoo) “Donald explained that he may have gotten a bit too excited about the chances of scoring his first-ever defensive touchdown, which led to his missing out completely on the fumble recovery. “Boom. I seen the ball. First thing came to my head. ‘Touchdown. I’m going to get this ball.’ I should have slowed down, but I felt people behind me like I want to get hit in my back. That’s going to hurt. So, I tried to go full speed and scoop it. The ball was going I thought the ball was going to bounce this way, but it bounced that way. And it just looked all damn silly,” Donald said. “ Aaron Donald gets brutally honest about Rams return (nypost) “The 35-year-old three-time Defensive Player of the Year made a candid admission about his return to The Sporting Tribune’s Eric Lambkins II. “No, it’s not what I expected, but we here,” Donald said of his return. He then added, “And I’m going to enjoy it though, you know. I’m enjoying the process. I’m enjoying myself week in and week out getting better. I’m enjoying being out there with the guys.” “Ain’t what I expected, but I’m enjoying it,” he added. Donald also spoke about getting Myles Garrett back healthy in Los Angeles’ upcoming game against the Washington Commanders, as Garrett has been sidelined since the Rams’ Week 1 game.“ Myles Garrett expected to play vs. Commanders (ramswire) “The returns of Garrett and Ferguson will both be huge for the Rams, who have missed them over the last month-plus. Josaiah Stewart will now take on a more limited role in the pass-rush rotation, while Ferguson steps in immediately and becomes the Rams’ top pass-catching tight end. With Davante Adams out, the Rams badly need another receiving threat, and Ferguson provides just that. Garrett, meanwhile, is the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and the record-holder for the most sacks in a season (23).“ NFL predictions: Washington Commanders vs Los Angeles Rams (sports.yahoo) “Brown is a former playoff hero with the Commanders who lit up the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Detroit Lions during 2025’s playoff run, before wilting with 42 yards in the NFC Title Game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Brown has played in seven games this season and has contributed, albiet at a reduced rate, with nine receptions for 94 yards and no touchdowns. He has been dealing with a calf injury. Burks has been ramping up his production this season with 12 catches for 233 yards and two touchdowns, including 81 yards against the Eagles on November 1. He is dealing with a left foot injury.“ Myles Garrett Set to Make Return vs. Commanders, But What Should Rams Expect? (si.com) “The Rams traded for Garrett in what was their biggest acquisition of the offseason . However, shortly into training camp, Garrett began missing practices with what was described as knee soreness and then was placed on injured reserve that week as he underwent arthroscopic surgery. “There were just things I was dealing with mechanically that only continued to worsen as I played more throughout that game,” said Garrett on Friday. “It was rough and I was trying to avoid it, but you learn and you grow. Now it’s just a lesson that I had to learn from and I took the necessary steps to come back.” With Jaylen Watson heading on injured reserve earlier this week, the Rams won’t get a look at what their defense could have been with Garrett, Watson, Trent McDuffie, and Aaron Donald. However, the Rams will get a look at what their defense can do with Donald and Garrett on the field together for the first time.“ Myles Garrett’s Expected Return Gives Los Angeles Rams a Pass-Rush Boost (athlonsports) “Locked On Rams Squad Show host Gavin Carlson said Garrett can help compensate for Watson’s absence by shortening the time Daniels has to diagnose coverage. Carlson’s central point was not that one pass rusher erases the loss of a productive cornerback; it is that Garrett can force quicker decisions, creating more manageable coverage situations for the defensive backs who remain.” Rams safety Quentin Lake apologizes to Justin Herbert for ‘deli meat’ comment, even though he has a point (sports.yahoo) “According to The Los Angeles Times, Lake sent an apology to Herbert over text message, but had not heard back. “I don’t know if he read it,” Lake said. “He probably says, ‘I don’t care about it anymore. I’m not trying to see this. It doesn’t matter. You said what you said.’ But at the same time I … felt like it was right for me to at least say, ‘Hey, man, I didn’t mean it in any disrespectful way.'” Come on, Justin: He meant you were throwing deli meat in the most respectful way imaginable!“ Rams listed Matthew Stafford with elbow injury because reporters asked about ice on it (sports.yahoo) “Really, it’s because you guys asked me about it earlier in the week,” McVay told reporters on Friday regarding the decision to disclose an elbow injury for Stafford. “It’s more semantical than anything else. It’s normal, like what he told you guys, but because you guys asked me about him having ice on his elbow. . . . He’s been full, hasn’t missed any sort of reps so normal management stuff that he’s been doing over the last few years.” It conjures memories of the Patriots’ one-time habit of listing former quarterback Tom Brady as “probable” with a “right shoulder” injury. That all started because he had ice on his shoulder in the locker room, reporters inquired, and the team decided to just put him on the injury report every week.“ Los Angeles Rams Announce Bad News About Former Top Draft Pick (heavy.com) “Grant Stuard will be limited with his hamstring. He’ll be questionable for the game. Jordan Whittington will be limited with his back. He’ll be questionable for the game. We’ll end up putting Jaylen Watson on IR, but he’s listed as out on this injury report. Joe Cardona will be doubtful. Trent McDuffie , Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl , they’ll be listed as questionable for the game. Trent will be a DNP. Everybody else has no injury designation.” Rams & Commanders set for a crucial NFC showdown in Week 9 | Game Preview (therams.com) “Key contributors continue to peel off to the injured list, sapping what should be some nice momentum for the Rams. When you think back to how this roster was constructed, it’s deflating to come to grips with the fact that we’ll see zero snaps of Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson , Myles Garrett , and Aaron Donald playing football together in 2026. “I think you’ll miss the production, the toughness, some of the different things that we’re able to do with him,” Sean McVay remarked this week as Watson accepted season-ending surgery on his twice-injured shoulder. “A couple of weeks ago, he’s cramping at the Raiders game and he says when he’s getting an IV, ‘Give me half a bag. I need to get back out there.’ He’s been awesome. He’s been playing through some different stuff, but he’s been really productive, and it’s unfortunate that that happened.” Comment of the day: Feed post of the day:

full_text: In pursuit of a third consecutive win, the Los Angeles Rams travel cross-country to take on the Washington Commanders. Kickoff is set for 10 a.m. PST from Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland. The nation’s capitol eleven currently stands at 2-4-1 and are coming off a 27-10 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Washington’s offense is ranked in the bottom third of NFL teams for the season, but have trended upward slightly over the last three games with the return from injury of quarterback Jayden Daniels. The Rams have had their struggles defending athletic quarterbacks who can extend drives with their running ability and Daniels is adept at that. While injuries have detoured his and the team’s success since his Rookie of the Year performance in 2024, he is still dangerous and has yet to throw an interception in 2026. Daniels does good work spreading out the receiving targets, veteran Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams being the primaries. Both should get a lot of work Sunday, secondary receivers Dyami Brown (calf) and Treylon Burks (foot) have been ruled out of the game with injury. The Commanders run game has struggled, Rachaad White and Jacory McCrosky-Merritt have combined for a paltry 439 yards. The big news for the Rams is the expected return of edge Myles Garrett off the Injured Reserve List. It will be his first action since Week 1. Tight end Terrance Ferguson was also anticipated to play after missing five weeks, but has been downgraded to out for the game. Here’s how to follow the game! full_text: Sean McVay gave a press conference on Friday stating that Terrance Ferguson was looking likely to play in Week 9 for the Los Angeles Rams against the Washington Commanders. McVay stated he expected both Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson to suit up on Sunday. “Do expect Myes (Garrett) and Terrance (Ferguson) to play barring any sorta setbacks” There must have been a setback in practice because later on in the day, the Rams announced that Ferguson will be out against the Commanders as the second-year tight end is reportedly dealing with a new hamstring injury. Rams now say TE Terrance Ferguson is out for Sunday’s game against the Commanders. https://t.co/3UIdOeJZcb — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 6, 2026 Ferguson was looking like a potential breakout candidate for the Rams in Week 2 against the New York Giants when he grabbed six balls for 54 yards and one score. In Week 3 against the Denver Broncos, Ferguson injured his ankle and couldn’t stay in the game. Finally, in Week 9, it was looking like Ferguson would be back just in time to go along with Garrett, and while Davante Adams is still on IR. Ferguson may have had a great chance to reestablish himself as an offensive weapon, but instead, Ferguson is hurt again, with no clear timeline on when he’ll return. On his career, Ferguson has 18 receptions for 290+ yards and four touchdowns. The talent is there, but the health has not been for the young player in 2026. He may get another chance to suit up in Week 10, barring any setbacks.

title: Rams Reacts: Do fans think McVay is part of the problem?
