full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 20: Brandon Aiyuk #11 of the San Francisco 49ers gets injured after making a catch during the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Levi's Stadium on October 20, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. The Chiefs defeated the 49ers 28-18. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brett Favre never got this kind of coverage. Today is the day soon-to-be-former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk reports to the team facility in order to begin his reinstatement to the NFL. As of this writing, several things are being discussed; the main hurdle is the $13 million the NFL informed Aiyuk that he owes the 49ers. You know it’s obnoxious when you have local news choppers providing footage not of Aiyuk, but of his new agent Drew Rosenhaus getting out of a van…less than a mile away from the facility. Let me remind you, this isn’t someone signing with a new team. This is someone going to a meeting where a team wants their money back and a resolution to get him off their team. Chopper footage of Brandon Aiyuk's agent Drew Rosenhaus getting out of a large van and entering a Starbucks less than a mile away from Levi's Stadium. pic.twitter.com/l8MUNAF8Ux — Matt Lively (@mattblively) November 6, 2026 And then, on the ground, we have that same van arriving at 49ers HQ. Aiyuk hopped out of the van and gave a statement: Brandon Aiyuk’s arrival at 49ers HQ and statement pic.twitter.com/nSWy3nsMV4 — David Lombardi (@LombardiHimself) November 6, 2026 Let’s not think this statement is something bigger than it is. Aiyuk wants back into the “National Football League.” There might be speculation that he could come back to the 49ers, but that’s nonsense . While the opposite has happened in declarations made by this team (see Jimmy Garoppolo leaving in 2022), there’s little evidence outside of some recent ambiguous answers by Kyle Shanahan to suggest he’s welcome back to the 49ers. Aiyuk was placed on the reserve/left squad list in 2025, and aside from going on Instagram, he made no attempt to get off it . The drama continued with him firing his previous agent and declaring he’d never do business with the 49ers again. We’ll update you when this circus is over, but it’s almost inevitable on what the ending to this story is. At this point, Daejon Love has a better chance of suiting up in 2026 than Brandon Aiyuk does. But you have to hand it to Aiyuk; he’s got everyone talking about what’s going to be a meeting that ends with him off the 49ers. title: 49ers-Raiders predictions: All eyes on Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are coming off their bye week with some added reinforcements, as they look to start the second half of the season on the right track against the Las Vegas Raiders this weekend. The Niners are 9.5-point favorites on FanDuel Sportsbook, with the game total set at 51.5. While the 49ers will […]
full_text: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are coming off their bye week with some added reinforcements, as they look to start the second half of the season on the right track against the Las Vegas Raiders this weekend. The Niners are 9.5-point favorites on FanDuel Sportsbook , with the game total set at 51.5. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . While the 49ers will not have wide receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, or Christian Kirk, Demarcus Robinson is trending toward playing, while cornerbacks Upton Stout and Nate Hobbs are looking in that direction as well. Additionally, San Francisco will have Nick Bosa back, so he and DeForest Buckner should be on the field on Sunday as the 49ers debut their new-look defensive line. Heading into the weekend, the 49ers are massive 10-point favorites over the Raiders after opening as 8.5-point favorites, with the total skyrocketing to 51.5 points. While the 49ers are tied for the league’s best record at 6-1, the Raiders have been on a bit of a slide after their hot 3-0 start. They suffered four straight losses to the Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots, Buffalo Bills, and Los Angeles Rams before their come-from-behind win over the New York Jets last weekend. So, let’s look at our three predictions for Sunday’s game, which is set to kick off at 1:25 p.m. on FOX. Demarcus Robinson returns with a big play The 49ers have missed that vertical field-stretcher since Demarcus Robinson went out weeks ago. Initially, that was set to be De’Zhaun Stribling, but he suffered the ankle injury back in Week 1. So, that went to Demarcus Robinson, who played in just a game and a half before suffering a high ankle sprain. Robinson has been out since Week 2, but he was involved in both of the games he played to start the year. He had the long 39-yard touchdown against the Rams in Week 1, finishing with two catches for 50 yards. Then, in Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins, he had three catches for 34 yards, with the longest going for 19. The 49ers wide receiver core is still beaten up, and the group has struggled with separation at times. That’s where Robinson comes in, and it feels like Kyle Shanahan will look his way for a couple of vertical plays. I think one hits on Sunday. Nick Bosa, DeForest Buckner return with a sack Kirk Cousins has taken 11 sacks this season, as Klint Kubiak and the Raiders have done a great job getting the ball out of his hands. Cousins has averaged a 2.70-second time to throw, and he’s been even quicker against the blitz. All 11 of his sacks have come when teams have rushed four or fewer, and I think the 49ers will find their way to at least one courtesy of returners Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner this weekend. Las Vegas’s run game has not been great. That should leave the Raiders in some tough late-down situations, and the 49ers suddenly have a pretty impressive veteran pass-rushing group with Bosa, Buckner, and Osa Odighizuwa. Now, others might get home for even more sacks, but I think the stars are aligning for Bosa or Buckner to get to the quarterback at least once on Sunday. Fred Warner has the battle to watch One way the Raiders’ passing game has been thriving this season is by throwing to Ashton Jeanty, one of the most targeted running backs in the NFL this season. Now, Jeanty may have gotten a soft benching last week, as his snap share dipped significantly in favor of rookie Mike Washington, but he’s still a very talented pass catcher, and that leaves Fred Warner with the top assignment this weekend. Not only will Warner likely carry star Brock Bowers for a few routes, but he’ll also work in coverage against the running backs, the two spots Las Vegas has looked to target. Jeanty is second on the Raiders with 37 receptions for 376 yards and three touchdowns. The 49ers will have to mitigate that on Sunday.

title: How the 49ers plan to use DeForest Buckner with new look DL room
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are hitting the field on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, coming off a bye week, and they’ll have their new addition on the defensive line with them. Recently traded defensive tackle DeForest Buckner is set to make his 49ers return, marking his first game in San Francisco uniform since the […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 20: DeForest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts sacks Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the second quarter of an NFL football game on September 20, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are hitting the field on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, coming off a bye week, and they’ll have their new addition on the defensive line with them. Recently traded defensive tackle DeForest Buckner is set to make his 49ers return, marking his first game in San Francisco uniform since the 2019 Super Bowl. Buckner, 32, has long been known as a quality pass rusher with a unique size-length profile at 6’7, and will hope to add some of that to a young defensive tackle room that also includes Osa Odighizuwa. Now, the 49ers have their two veterans, along with rookie Gracen Halton and former undrafted free agent Sebastian Valdez as their top depth. With the Indianapolis Colts, Buckner had a top five snap count among defensive tackles this season. With the 49ers, that’ll hopefully drop as the 49ers rotate their linemen more. But, with Buckner and Odighizuwa both having familiarity playing as three-techniques, how will the 49ers use Buckner in his return? “We’ve done so many different things, moved people around,” defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said. “They have the ability to play three-technique. They have the ability to play nose. They have the ability to play four-eye, the ability to play on the edge. You’ve kind of seen these guys kind of move around all over the place, so I wouldn’t really put them in a bucket. “You’re talking about a guy with supreme talent. Those guys kind of can do whatever you ask them to do. Traditionally he’s been a three-technique around here, playing a huge role and doing some really good things. He’ll do a lot of the same thing. I’m a big believer in doing what people do really well and we’ll try to find out what he does really well again, implement them to what the guys have been doing and put those guys together and put them out there playing fast.” The 49ers have regularly been moving players around, kicking some of their bigger edges inside, while also creating different ways to rush the passer. The creativity should increase with Nick Bosa also trending to play, but it doesn’t seem like Morris is concerned with the usage. San Francisco has been without Bosa for a few weeks now, and their pass rush has struggled a bit as a result. Now, with him and Buckner both likely in the fold this week, what will that do for the defense? “I don’t know when it would be a bad time to get a guy like Buck,” Morris added. “It’s been a lot of fun to meet him the last couple of days and be around him and watch him practice and put him a part of it. Really feel like I’m further away from it than he is because of how long he spent here and the time that he spent here and how much he means to this organization and the people around him. “So, it’s been a lot of fun being around that guy and to have that whole unit being able to come back relatively healthy. To see these guys (Buckner and Bosa) probably for the first time altogether, I think altogether, for the first time this year, I think it’d be a lot of fun.” Now, the 49ers have two veterans in their defensive tackle room, which should only help in the development of younger guys like Mykel Williams, Halton, Valdez, Romello Height, and the rest of the room. “Buck’s done it at a very high level for such a long time,” Morris continued. “I don’t know if there’s anybody in this building that can’t pick something up from him. I just know how much, let’s just go with the ultimate leader in Fred [Warner] and [Dre] Greenlaw, how much respect those guys have for him. So when you’re talking about guys that have done a lot of really cool things at different positions that can learn from him, you can only imagine what the guys up front can get from him, just those guys being together. “Having Osa being a vet and then having Buck come in with some different perspective, different realities of what he’s been through and what he’s done. To be able to come back into the fold and really pick it back up and fit right back in with the guy that’s coached him, guys that he’s familiar with, whether it be the head coach or his position coach, I think is always a really good thing.” The Niners will kick things off against the Raiders this weekend as they look to start the second half of the season hot. We’ll get to see how Buckner looks returning to the 49ers, and whether the team still needs to make another move ahead of the deadline.

title: A tale of the 2 best tight ends in the NFL: George Kittle vs. Brock Bowers
summary: The San Francisco 49ers will do battle with their former local rivals on Sunday at Levi’s Stadium as the Las Vegas Raiders come to town. The 6-1 49ers will likely be shorthanded on offense, with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel expected to miss the game, but they’ll get Demarcus Robinson back, along with DeForest Buckner […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers will do battle with their former local rivals on Sunday at Levi’s Stadium as the Las Vegas Raiders come to town. The 6-1 49ers will likely be shorthanded on offense, with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel expected to miss the game, but they’ll get Demarcus Robinson back, along with DeForest Buckner and Nick Bosa. The storylines can begin with the rivalry, or we can continue with the Kirk Cousins/Kyle Shanahan narrative. Also, the Kubiak/Shanahan connection is worthy of a mention. The real highlight will be the two superstar tight ends for the Raiders and the 49ers. Let’s start with George Kittle. His recovery from a torn Achilles in the playoffs last season is as close to a modern miracle as there is. It’s a testament to the freak athlete he is and how hard he works. As Kittle prepares to wear a gold jacket, the tight end is close to rarefied air for any tight end. This season, Kittle has 425 receiving yards and, with 75 more, will join Rob Gronkowski as the only tight ends with 500-plus receiving yards in their first ten seasons, per NFL Communications. There is an argument that Travis Kelce has achieved this feat, but he played in a single game in his rookie season without recording a catch, and the NFL doesn’t recognize the achievement. Yes, I think it’s silly as well, but on Sunday, Kittle can join Gronk and make his Hall of Fame case stronger. Either way, Kelce will join both Kittle and Gronk as Hall of Famers. On the flip side, Brock Bowers is on his way to the same distinction with over 500 yards in each of his three seasons. His rookie season was sensational with 112 receptions and 1,194 yards. Last season was an injury-riddled season, but he still managed to put up 680 yards and, with Kirk Cousins, has recorded 547 yards, despite missing games due to injury. Now, the beauty of the two tight ends is how effective and impactful both are, but in very different ways. Kittle plays inline much more and is widely known as the best blocking tight end in the NFL, while Bowers is split out wide and beats cornerbacks. While Kittle is supposedly “winding down” his career, Bowers is just getting started. Trey McBride is another top tight end, but Sunday will be a matchup of the old guard vs. the new guard. We have to truly appreciate Kittle while he’s still playing. Bowers will be a joy to watch for the rest of his career. Sunday isn’t National Tight End Day, but it should be.

full_text: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Once the clocks get set back, the San Francisco 49ers turn into juggernauts. That’s been the case since 2022, save for a disastrous 2024 season. The Niners are 23-8 in November and December regular-season games since ’22. Here’s a breakdown by year: 2022: 9-0 2023: 7-2 2024: 2-7 2025: 7-2 The only way to beat that 2022 team was by having a defender ensure that then-rookie Brock Purdy couldn’t throw a forward pass. There’s an asterisk next to 2023, since one of those losses was a meaningless Week 18 game. The other one came when Purdy was in a giving mood on Christmas. I remember traveling to Lambeau Field in 2024 around Thanksgiving. Brandon Allen started that game. That sums up the second half. In ‘25, the schedule all but guaranteed the 49ers a postseason berth. Post-bye performances If we look at how San Francisco has performed after their bye, it’s been just as impressive. The last time the 49ers lost after a bye was Week 7 of 2021. Jimmy Garoppolo threw two interceptions and lost a fumble, as did Deebo Samuel. Carson Wentz found Michael Pittman to ice the game in the fourth quarter, making it 30-18. Garoppolo was still under center for the 49ers game after their 2022 bye. At home against the Chargers, the Niners trailed 13-3 before shutting Los Angeles down and holding them scoreless in the second half. Up 22-16 with 49 seconds remaining, Talanoa Hufanga picked off Justin Herbert to end the game. Week 10 in 2023 might’ve been the most dominant performance we’ve seen from Shanahan coming out of a bye. On a rainy day in Jacksonville, the 49ers squeezed the life out of the Jags, holding them to 221 yards and only three points. George Kittle outran the defense to open the half for a 66-yard touchdown to make it 20-3. Hufanga picked off Trevor Lawrence, sealing the deal and cementing the Niners as contenders. Both teams left the game 6-3, but one team was for real. In 2024, the 49ers beat Tampa Bay and were 5-4 after their bye. Despite a 23-20 win, the signs were there. Jake Moody missed three field goals. The offense couldn’t run the ball. There were glimpses of excellence from Ricky Pearsall, but that would be the last of the successes that season. Getting the Titans in Week 15 off a bye was a gift from the 2025 schedule makers. Purdy had three touchdowns and seven incompletions. His QBR was nearly triple Cam Ward’s. A 37-24 score looks closer than the game actually was, thanks to a pair of fourth-quarter touchdowns by Tennessee. We have seen a second-half surge under Shanahan’s teams. Their post-bye excellence should continue with a home game against a Raiders team that was outgained by the Jets. Depending on how you feel about the rest of the schedule, the No. 1 seed is the Niners to lose, even with a couple of slip-ups along the way. It won’t be easy, especially if Mike Evans misses multiple weeks. But reinforcements on the other side of the ball take pressure off the offense from needing to score 30 points a game until Evans returns.

title: 2 reasons why the Raiders might give the 49ers fits
summary: The San Francisco 49ers used their bye week wisely, shoring up the defensive line by adding DeForest Buckner. The 49ers have one final game before the trade deadline, hosting their former neighbors, the Las Vegas Raiders. With San Francisco getting a bye week following its first loss of the season, the Raiders ended a four-game […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers used their bye week wisely, shoring up the defensive line by adding DeForest Buckner . The 49ers have one final game before the trade deadline, hosting their former neighbors, the Las Vegas Raiders. With San Francisco getting a bye week following its first loss of the season, the Raiders ended a four-game skid with a win over the Jets. Las Vegas started hot with a 3-0 start, but that quickly turned to 3-4 before the Week 8 win. The 49ers look to return the Raiders to their losing ways on Sunday. Here are three numbers to know going into the former Battle of the Bay: 1 Team. The Raiders are the only team in the league to be in the bottom three in yards allowed and points allowed. Simply put: the Raiders’ defense is bad. It’s 381.9 yards allowed per game, the third-most allowed (only the Titans and Cowboys are worse), and the 28.8 points allowed per game is second-worst (only Arizona has allowed more, and the Colts are slightly better). And the scary thing for Vegas is the defense is only getting worse. In each of its last five games, the Raiders have allowed 30 or more points after allowing just 27 points combined in the first two games of the season. Part of the reason the points have gone up is the Raiders just can’t stop the ball. Las Vegas has allowed more than its average of 382 yards in four of the last five games, with the offense only able to keep up last week, going 1-4 in those five games. The New York Jets scored 30 points for the first time since Week 8 of last season. It’s easy to see a 49ers offense even without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel putting up points against this Raiders defense. 13 Turnovers. The Raiders defense has forced 13 turnovers, fifth-most in the league. Not a good one, but a defense that can take the ball away if you aren’t careful, and the 49ers haven’t been protective of the ball recently. Hopefully the bye week fixed that issue. The Raiders have been plenty opportunistic (and maybe a little lucky) with only five interceptions, placing them in the middle of the league in picking the ball off. Where the Raiders shine is when the ball is loose, with seven fumble recoveries. The bad news: the 49ers average a fumble per game, with five of the six that were lost coming in San Francisco’s last three games. Turnovers have been a recent plague for the 49ers. After turning the ball over two times in the first four games, San Francisco has eight turnovers in the last three games, with four of those coming against an Atlanta team that entered Week 7 with just six turnovers. The Raiders defense can be beat, but the 49ers must shake this recent turnover issue to fully take advantage. 265.1 Passing yards per game. The Raiders offense averages 265.1 passing yards per game, third-best in the league. While the Raiders defense isn’t great, its offense is explosive, which puts them in the category of “not a great team, but a fun team” that has the ability to get into a shootout. In four of the Raiders’ eight games this season, both teams have scored more than 24 points, with the Raiders splitting those games. The spark for the Las Vegas offense has been giving second-year tight end Brock Bowers a competent quarterback in veteran Kirk Cousins. Cousins has turned the clock back with Las Vegas under Klint Kubiak, throwing for 19 touchdowns and five interceptions through the first half of the season. His 6.7 touchdown percentage is his highest since 2020, while his 1.8 interception rate is his lowest since 2023. But Bowers has been the key to Cousins’ resurgence. Despite missing the first two games of the season, the tight end leads the Raiders in targets by 14, receptions by four, receiving yards by 73, and touchdowns by one. The Las Vegas offense looked fine in the two games without Bowers but has taken a step up with him, scoring 30 points in three of the six games the tight end has played in. How the 49ers choose to cover Bowers will be something to watch. They could use a safety (maybe Ji’Ayir Brown?) or maybe a corner (but the 49ers’ corners might have a tough time with the size of Bowers). I’m curious to see if the 49ers even throw Fred Warner at Bowers a few times just to see how he handles it.

title: Jordan Watkins has clear chance to continue coming out party
summary: Jordan Watkins was the major bright spot of the 49ers’ defeat to the Atlanta Falcons before their Week 8 bye, as the second-year wide receiver took advantage of the extra opportunities afforded to him by San Francisco’s injuries at the position. Watkins enjoyed a career day in the Niners’ 29-20 loss in Atlanta, catching three […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 25: San Francisco wide receiver Jordan Watkins (17) attempts to catch a touchdown pass during the NFL game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Atlanta Falcons on October 25th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jordan Watkins was the major bright spot of the 49ers’ defeat to the Atlanta Falcons before their Week 8 bye, as the second-year wide receiver took advantage of the extra opportunities afforded to him by San Francisco’s injuries at the position. Watkins enjoyed a career day in the Niners’ 29-20 loss in Atlanta, catching three passes for 56 yards as he was targeted six times by Brock Purdy. One of Watkins’ targets looked to have gone for a touchdown when he appeared to have made a sensational diving leaping grab over a defender in the corner of the endzone in the fourth quarter, only to have that score wiped away following a replay review Watkins did not survive the ground having spectacularly managed to get both feet in bounds. Still, his performance in Atlanta is likely to have increased the faith Brock Purdy has in the former fourth-round pick. And Watkins is likely to have a chance to continue his coming out party as the 49ers return from their bye to face the Las Vegas Raiders, with top receiver Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel looking likely to miss another week. The 49ers look primed to get Demarcus Robinson back from injury, but there appears to be some doubt around Christian Kirk after he missed Thursday’s practice having only made his season debut against Atlanta. As such, the prospective absences of Evans, Samuel and perhaps Kirk give Watkins another chance to serve as one of Purdy’s top pass-catching weapons in Week 9. And the numbers suggest that opportunity is coming against an ideal opportunity. The Raiders have one of the worst pass defenses in the NFL, ranking 30th in the league by dropback success rate (47.4%) allowed and 25th in the league by dropback EPA per play. In other words, the Raiders allowing a little under half of the dropbacks against them to turn into successful plays, while they consistently struggle to prevent explosive passing plays. For a player with Watkins’ speed, the chance to go up against a defense so vulnerable to the big play represents an enticing matchup. Given the rapport he seemingly has with Purdy, he should view it as a game in which he could put together an even more impressive career day. With the continuation of the injury problems they are having at receiver, the 49ers would substantially benefit from having Watkins emerge as bonafide dynamic and reliable weapon in the offense. The Las Vegas defense is one that figures to be accommodating to the 49er passing game despite its injuries and, though San Francisco is in a desperate position in terms of options at wideout, for Watkins the conditions are perfect for a fully fledged breakout game.

(Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buccaneers kicker Chase McLaughlin received recognition for his perfect kicking in October, as he earned NFC Special Teams Player of the Month honors. McLaughlin not only stayed perfect throughout October (7-for-7 on field goals, 11-for-11 on extra points), but he’s been 100% accurate throughout the entire season thus far. In 8 games, the 30-year-old veteran has successfully converted all 19 of his attempts in 2026, as well as all 17 of his extra point attempts. Chase McLaughlin says that his special teams player of the month award is as much about the rest of the special teams unit as it is about him: pic.twitter.com/17PI1x3aPO — River Wells (@riverhwells) November 5, 2026 The Tampa Bay placekicker, in his fourth season with the team, is the first to earn the honor in nearly two decades for the Bucs. He joins Matt Bryant, who garnered it in December 2007. Missing October by one day, McLaughlin arguably produced his best outing of the year with a 3-for-3 day against the Atlanta Falcons last Sunday in the midst of a deluge. McLaughlin is tied for most makes in the entire league with Arizona’s Chad Ryland and Indianapolis’s Spencer Shrader, but both of them have multiple misses on their ledger. He’s easily the frontrunner for first-team All-Pro halfway through the year. McLaughlin has been nothing short of elite since joining the Bucs in 2023, as he’s been the most accurate kicker from 50+ yards and one of the most accurate kickers overall. He etched his name in the record books last season with the longest outdoor field goal in NFL history, nailing a kick from 65 yards against the Philadelphia Eagles at home. In the final year of his contract, “Money” McLaughlin has earned his new pay day, and the Bucs will need to soon prioritize paying one of their most reliable players.

Head coach Robert Saleh and staff must reflect over the bye week on necessary changes, starting with the Jacksonville […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Gunnar Helm #84 of the Tennessee Titans looks on prior to Week 2 of the preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans are taking a strong offensive performance in Week 8 against the Cincinnati Bengals into a Week 9 bye. Quarterback Cam Ward played the best game of his career , his first-ever 300 yard showing. Head coach Robert Saleh and staff must reflect over the bye week on necessary changes, starting with the Jacksonville Jaguars game in Week 10. We’ve particularly identified three Titans players who need to be more involved following this weekend’s bye-week. TE Gunnar Helm Offensive coordinator Brian Daboll finally involved sophomore tight end Gunnar Helm in the passing attack in Week 8 and it paid dividends. Helm posted a career-high 76 receiving yards via five catches. Ward looked so comfortable targeting his reliable tight end. It was a sophomore breakout performance, and Daboll needs to ensure his momentum continues moving forward. WR Chimere Dike Speaking of sophomore breakouts in the passing game, Chimere Dike enjoyed one of his own versus the Bengals. The speedy special teams ace reminded the coaching staff that he’s also very useful on offense. Dike recorded five receptions for a season-high 71 yards and a touchdown. Daboll needs to continue getting him snaps on offense, even at the expense of Wan’Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley. CB Alontae Taylor After benching Alontae Taylor in Week 5, his name has been mentioned in various trade-rumor articles. Trading him would be pretty complicated given they just signed him to a three-year, $58 million contract earlier this offseason. Anything is possible, but his contract isn’t exactly trade-friendly given its newness. Taylor played well at nickel corner against the Bengals after Marcus Harris got hurt. The Titans probably have to keep him in that position versus the Jaguars in Week 10.

title: Commanders win-loss projections for next 5 games – survey results
summary: Looking one month into the past A month ago, at the beginning of October, Washington had a record of 1-3, and things were looking decidedly grim for a team that had just lost both its starting and backup quarterbacks — and then lost to an inferior Colts team in London with Commanders rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, […]
full_text: Looking one month into the past A month ago, at the beginning of October, Washington had a record of 1-3, and things were looking decidedly grim for a team that had just lost both its starting and backup quarterbacks — and then lost to an inferior Colts team in London with Commanders rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, formerly of Rutgers, being pressed into service when Marcus Mariota was knocked out of the game in the first quarter. Dark times, indeed. Back then, as the Commanders headed into mid-October, we asked Hogs Haven members to predict, in the Reacts survey , how many wins Washington would rack up in the 3 games scheduled in the then-upcoming month, which would see the burgundy & gold go against the Giants and Eagles at home, as well as the 49ers on the road, with a bye week thrown in to boot. It’s interesting to look back on the results of that October survey in which about 1/3 of respondents predicted a 1-2 record; another 1/3 predicted a 2-1 record, and over a quarter of respondents predicted that Washington would get completely shut out, going 0-3. The predicted number of wins in that poll, calculated as a mathematical average, was 1.17. As we all know, the team actually ended up going 1-1-1, approximating the predicted number of wins in our survey, and out-performing the number of wins projected by 62% of respondents in that October survey. Fast forward to the present As dismal as the season may seem at the moment, if you can cast your mind back to that time early October — when fans were unsure who was going to take snaps at quarterback in Week 5 against the Giants, and nearly 30% of the fan base was expecting an 0-3 record for the upcoming month — you may come to the same conclusion that I have; that is, that the actual on-field results have improved (.250 in the first 4 weeks; .500 in the next 4 weeks), and the outlook for the 2026 season appears a little bit brighter than it did back then. After all, Jayden Daniels has started and finished 3 complete games since that survey was conducted. And, in the 6 quarters of football played since halftime at San Francisco in Week 6, the Commanders were highly competitive vs the 49ers, outscoring them 14-3 to make a game out of that prime time contest, and they actually beat the Eagles 27-10 this past Sunday. Sure, a lot of fans and media personalities are calling for Dan Quinn’s head one-third of the way through Season 3 of the rebuild recalibration, but the team still has every opportunity to meet or exceed preseason expectations by finishing strong, compiling 8 or 9 wins, and — given the current state of the NFC East — potentially winning the division and earning a home playoff game. While that still seems like a big ask with the team having just 2 wins in November, Hogs Haven readers who completed the Reacts survey this week seem to think that the Commanders can win more games than they lose over the next 5 weeks, and that — with respect to winning the division — no game will be more important than the road trip to New York five days from now to play the Giants. The upcoming five weeks — and especially Thursday’s Week 10 prime time game against the Giants — are critical to the Commanders 2026 season, and have the capacity, if Washington can beat New York and at least 2 other opponents in that slate of games, to set the team up for an exciting stretch run in the final weeks of the season. This Week’s Reacts Survey In this week’s Hogs Haven Reacts survey , we asked readers two questions to measure community sentiment entering the ninth week of the season. The first question was our weekly staple, asking whether you are confident in the overall direction of the team. This week, 43% of respondents answered “Yes,” while 57% voted “No.” The 21-point jump from last week’s mark was predictable; nothing lifts the collective mood around Washington quite like beating the Philadelphia Eagles. After struggling through a mistake-filled first quarter on Sunday night, Washington played nearly three full quarters of (fairly) disciplined, competitive football to overcome the early 10-point deficit and put away a division rival in a game that was critical to any hope the Commanders have of reaching the playoffs in 2026. Of course, a 57% negative vote is still a clear reminder of the frustration built up from a rocky first two months, but putting an NFC East win in the bank goes some way toward soothing the unease of the fanbase. Looking at November (and a little beyond) Our second question turned the focus forward: What record will the Commanders compile in the next 5 games? The upcoming slate features the Los Angeles Rams (4-4) at home before a quick turnaround trip to New York to take on the division-leading Giants (4-2-1) on Thursday Night Football. There is a mini-bye of sorts ahead of a home date against the Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) on Monday Night Football, which is followed by road trips to play the Arizona Cardinals (3-5) and Tennessee Titans (1-7). Sizing Up the Next Five Games When the votes were tallied for this second survey question, 10% of respondents had predicted a 5-0 sweep; 25% predicted 4 wins; 39% projected 3 wins; 17% expected 2 wins; 8% voted for 1 win, and just 1% foresaw a 0-5 collapse. Visit our partners at FanDuel My takeaway from those numbers is that nearly three-quarters of our community—74% of respondents, to be exact—expect Washington to put together a winning record over this upcoming five-game stretch. The single largest group, representing a 39% plurality, landed squarely on a 3-2 outcome. Only about a quarter of Hogs Haven voters anticipate a losing record over this stretch, and just 9% foresee complete disaster with fewer than two victories. That represents a dramatic shift in tone from where things stood just a few weeks ago. Mathematically, Hogs Haven readers responding to this week’s survey projected an average win total of 3.09 — strongly suggesting that our in-house prognosticators, who projected the win total so closely last time around, have a strong collective belief that the Commanders will go 3-2 in the coming five weeks, putting together the first multi-game stretch of the season above .500. When you consider the sheer amount of deep concern that accompanied the team’s sluggish start, seeing roughly three out of every four voters project winning football between now and early December shows that most of the fan base still believes this roster has life in it – at least enough life to get some wins against the relatively lightweight set of opponents that Washington will face in the next several weeks. What a winning record in the next 5 games would mean The strategic significance of that projected 3-2 run is notable. If the Commanders manage to win three of the next five, they would enter Week 14 with a 5-6-1 record. With five games left on the schedule at that juncture, an 8-win or 9-win season would morph from an offseason daydream into an attainable mathematical reality. In a division that has shown plenty of vulnerability from top to bottom, being within striking distance of a .500 record by early-to-mid-December should keep Washington in position to compete for the NFC East division title. Alex Rowsey said it in as many words in the comments: “In this division, if they win 3 of those games (with 1 coming against NYG), they’ll be sitting in pretty good shape at 5-6-1 after Week 13.” Playoffs?? Playoffs??!! The thought process behind the projection of 3 victories doesn’t seem too mysterious. Most survey respondents who forecast a winning stretch seem to view the road games against the Cardinals and the Titans as ones in which Washington should be able to take care of business. Arizona has struggled to string together consistent four-quarter efforts, having logged wins over the Rams, Cowboys, and winless Chargers (3 teams with a combined 7-16 record), while Tennessee sits at 1-7, their lone victory coming in Week 6 against the lowly Indianapolis Colts (yes, I remember…

title: NFL predictions: Washington Commanders vs Los Angeles Rams
summary: The Washington Commanders are coming off a much-needed win over the Philadelphia Eagles. They’ve got another big game this weekend as they attempt to dig themselves out of the NFC East’s basement and catch up to the division-leading Giants in a down year. The Los Angeles Rams are coming to town, and they’re bringing a […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders are coming off a much-needed win over the Philadelphia Eagles. They’ve got another big game this weekend as they attempt to dig themselves out of the NFC East’s basement and catch up to the division-leading Giants in a down year. The Los Angeles Rams are coming to town, and they’re bringing a freshly-activated Myles Garrett with them. It’s been a disappointing 4-4 start for a team that was on a lot of people’s predictions to win the Super Bowl. Washington is 2-4-1 for the season, and this is another critical game for a team that’s two games behind in the division. The Rams have been disappointing to preseason expectations, but they are still a good team that opened as 5.5-point road favorites. Matthew Stafford was the NFL’s MVP last season, but he’s been throwing interceptions at a higher rate this year. Davante Adams is out, but Puka Nacua will be on the field testing a secondary that looked better against the lowly Eagles. The Washington Commanders will be missing two more weapons on Sunday afternoon with Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf) ruled out on Friday. There are only two healthy receivers who have caught passes from Jayden Daniels this season in Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams. Players like Luke McCaffrey, Van Jefferson, and possibly Jaden Bradley could see their number called more this week. TE Chig Okonkwo has been a big factor since returning from injury, and he will be a top-2 receiving option vs the Rams. The Commanders running backs room continues to change due to injury. Jeremy McNichols returned from IR, but quickly went back on the reserve due to a new foot injury. That led to the Commanders claiming rookie Robert Henry Jr off waivers, a return after the Seahawks did the same a month ago. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the only other healthy backs on the 53-man roster. Washington continues to look for a run game that hasn’t materialized this season. Will Ekeler get more snaps this week or can the new blood pump some life into the ground game this week? This game’s 47.5 O/U lines up with our predictions this week, but hopefully the scores are switched and the Commanders pull off the upset. The team has options with Luke McCaffrey waiting for his first catch of the season. They also signed veteran Van Jefferson from the practice squad after Terry McLaurin’s season-ending knee injury. Quinn was said undrafted rookie Jaden Bradley, who will likely be elevated Sunday, leads the team’s scout team and he’s shown growth this year. The Rams are likely getting future Hall of Fame DE Myles Garrett back this week after he was placed on IR after surgery from a Week 1 knee injury. Quinn said the Rams defense can get pressure with four linemen, and Garrett’s return helps them. He called him a complete player who’s long, and bigger than you think. title: Commanders news: Why Jayden Daniels is next-level protecting the ball
summary: The Daily Slop – 6 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Post (paywall) […]
full_text: The Daily Slop – 6 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Post (paywall) How Jayden Daniels turned protecting the football into his ‘superpower’ Through all of the Commanders’ struggles, the quarterback has remained one of the NFL’s most efficient passers. Ahead of his freshman year of college in 2019, Jayden Daniels sat down with then-Arizona State coach Herm Edwards. The quarterback had been an excellent decision-maker in high school, but the former NFL coach wanted to drill home that the margin for error was about to shrink. He figured that Daniels had a future playing on Sundays and wanted to prepare him for what would come next. “He always told me, ‘No matter what, you give yourself a chance to win the game if the possession always ends with a kick,’” Daniels told The Washington Post. “Whether that’s a punt or a field goal, you always want to end it with a kick.” That was ingrained in Daniels throughout his five years of college football, and it hasn’t changed in the slightest through his third season with the Washington Commanders. Among the 33 NFL quarterbacks who’ve attempted at least 100 passes this season, he’s the only one who hasn’t committed a turnover. Few quarterbacks have been better than Daniels at protecting the football since he entered the NFL in 2024. He has an interception rate of just 1.5 percent (the fourth lowest among quarterbacks who attempted at least 500 passes during that span). Overall, he’s committed just 14 turnovers (tied for the fewest). “You just got to be locked in for six seconds each play,” Daniels said. “It kind of just goes with the flow of the game. And then, also, just having that discipline of like, ‘Okay, if it’s not there, don’t force it.’” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders Mailbag: Is Luke McCaffrey Being Overlooked? Did Dan Quinn Win Back Trust? With Terry McLaurin out for the year, McCaffrey’s limited role on offense is harder to overlook. Plus, what the Eagles win did—and didn’t—change for Dan Quinn. Luke McCaffrey looked good on that long kickoff return, but he barely played on offense. With Terry out for the year, is there a reason he still isn’t getting more opportunities at receiver? Question from Nigel F. via email That’s a great question that I’ve written about here before . From what I can tell, the staff likes McCaffrey, or he wouldn’t be on the roster, but he somehow keeps falling outside of the group that gets the main share of the offensive snaps at receiver. Against Philadelphia, McCaffrey played just three offensive snaps. Antonio Williams played 50, Treylon Burks 40, and Stefon Diggs 39. The team loaded up at receiver this offseason, giving the staff options even after McLaurin went down. The receiver room may not be big on names outside of McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, but rookie Antonio Williams is emerging fast , and whenever Treylon Burks can stay healthy, he routinely produces. Add in the attention tight end Chig Okonkwo gets, and there’s not much left for McCaffrey, Dyami Brown, or Van Jefferson. On film, McCaffrey gets open, so offensive coordinator David Blough has to make the scheme work with the talent they have. With injuries playing a factor, McCaffrey will likely get his shot to show what he brings to the field before the end of the season. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Commanders’ grand offensive transformation remains a work in progress The Washington Commanders didn’t start over completely after their 2025 season ended with only a handful of wins. A month after the team moved on from its previous coordinators, coach Dan Quinn reintroduced David Blough, previously the assistant quarterbacks coach, as his new play caller and they laid out their basic vision of the offense. Blough’s would be “an aggressive, balanced attack,” Quinn said, with more under-center formations and a departure from the no-huddle system Jayden Daniels had grown accustomed to over the past two years. It would require the young quarterback to get comfortable with relaying play calls — some of them lengthy — then quickly reading the defense to make any checks at the line of scrimmage. Among the more noticeable changes: Daniels would work under center more and no longer operate almost exclusively from the shotgun formation. “I think it opens up some different schemes in the run game, some things that I believe in,” Blough explained in February. “It opens up different play actions and keepers and getting him on the perimeter in different ways. I think there’s a level of communication that happens under center. … I think a lot of teams that you saw even playing deep into the playoffs, it was something that was a foundation of what they did.” The goal, both Quinn and Blough said, was to create a more explosive system that would take advantage of Daniels’ accuracy and running without asking him to do everything for the offense. Throughout the offseason, Blough, a first-time play caller, collaborated with his assistants and sought the input of his players as they built a system they said would be exclusively theirs. The foundation was an amalgamation of the offenses Blough ran during his years as a quarterback, and drawing from the offenses run by Washington’s previous play caller, Kliff Kingsbury, as well as Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell and even Louisville coach Jeff Brohm, whom Blough played for at Purdue. The crux of the Commanders’ offense, however, would draw from Ben Johnson, Blough’s former coordinator in Detroit who has since transformed the Chicago Bears’ offense with his heavy use of play action, multiple tight end sets, outside zone run concepts and pre-snap motion. To read more of this story, click here Last Man Standig (paywall) OFF SCRIPT: Austin Ekeler wasn’t sure he’d play again. He was OK with that. The Commanders running back opens up about nearly retiring after tearing his Achilles, AI’s upside and scary possibilities, growing up in rural Colorado and the NFL statistic he treasures most. ASHBURN, Va. — Austin Ekeler thought he had reached the finish line of his playing career. Not necessarily while lying on the Lambeau Field grass in pain after tearing his right Achilles. But soon after the non-contact injury in Week 2 that ended his 2025 season, any quiet time became a mental battle. “I’m probably done,” Ekeler thought. “Probably retiring.” The entire picture of his work and life put the injury into perspective. The running back was a workhorse for much of his seven-year stint with the Chargers. He helped the Washington Commanders reach the NFC Championship Game in season 8. Then Ekeler tore his Achilles in Year 9. He would be 31 if he returned. 2025 was also the first year he became a father. Ekeler and his wife, Melanie, welcomed a baby boy into the world that May. The guy who grew up on a farm in rural Northern Colorado was already busy “ripping projects,” from coding to creating apps to business and real estate investing. He loves football, but it’s not his life. And yet… “I told myself, ‘Look, let’s focus on the rehab. Don’t focus on whether I’m done or not. Don’t make that decision while I’m emotional. Continue to rehab, and then once that’s done, let’s get back in shape.” Ekeler is a gym guy, so he would get back into shape regardless. “Then, if I start to feel good and people are calling about me, I’ll do a workout. If they want to have me in, great. If not, let’s go rip some more code and build some more projects. That’s what it was for me.” The calls did come. The Carolina Panthers checked in and were set to add Ekeler to their practice squad when Washington raised the stakes with a spot on the active roster. title: Commanders GM Adam Peters discusses Jayden Daniels, NFL trade deadline
summary: General manager Adam Peters conducted his weekly interview with the Junkies on 106.7-FM The Fan in Washington on Friday morning, providing updates on quarterback Jayden Daniels, defensive line depth, Antonio Williams, while skating out of a discussion of a certain 49ers receiver that shall not be named.   The Commanders suffered more star power injuries, […]
full_text: General manager Adam Peters conducted his weekly interview with the Junkies on 106.7-FM The Fan in Washington on Friday morning, providing updates on quarterback Jayden Daniels, defensive line depth, Antonio Williams, while skating out of a discussion of a certain 49ers receiver that shall not be named. The Commanders suffered more star power injuries, with Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne out for the season . Terry McLaurin had successful surgery to repair a torn patellar and has been around the facility lifting others up, Peters said. Peters also said there’s concern about Dyami Brown after he suffered a calf injury in Thursday’s practice, but the team is hoping Johnny Newton can return for Sunday’s home game and that Bill Croskey-Merritt will be able to play the Bengals when he’s eligible to come off injured reserve . Let’s get to some interesting Peters quotes from that interview, which you can hear in its entirely below: Jayden Daniels and tight window throws “I believe in him and how great he is and he can be. The more repetitions he gets in this offense, the better he’s going to get. You’re seeing that. There are things we’re seeing for the first time that he’ll know for next time. He’s going to get more comfortable in this offense as we go. That’s what should happen. … I’d put Jayden being able to throw in a tight window with anybody. He’s a great passer and he trusts his arm and he trusts his accuracy and he trusts his receivers. I don’t have any issues not throwing it in tight windows. I don’t see that. What I do see is a guy who is taking care of the football. That’s really the most important thing and not turning the ball over. Even though our record doesn’t reflect it, we’ve been really good about taking care of the football and taking it away. If we continue to do that, that will reflect in our record.” On DL depth “Hopefully we’ll be getting Johnny Newtown back this week. He did a really good job rehabbing. He was here night and day, 24 hours it feels like, rehabbing that pec. He beat the timeline for that. He has been practicing the last two weeks. He’ll be back. The guys behind those guys – Tim Settle has really started to come on. Quietly, Shy Tuttle has been a really good part of our rotation and will have a bigger role with that now. We have Deatrich Wise, who also did a good job rehabbing back off a big injury he suffered last year in Green Bay. He’s going to help us in the run game. And then (Charles) Omenihu, who had his best game for us coming off injury. I think he’s going to take off for us.“ Antonio Williams’ growth “Every time we look his way, he comes through for us. And, whether he gets the ball or not, I feel like he’s always open. He has been coached really well here and was coached really well at Clemson. He also has this innate ability to find spots and be a friendly target for the quarterback. He has earned the right to get more targets. … We won’t force it to him, but he obviously makes it easy when he gets open all the time. We’re excited and pleased with his progress throughout the year. He’s going to keep getting more targets.“ On the NFL trade deadline “As we get closer, they always want to get through the week. …Anything that happens will happen early next week, if it does. There are a lot of calls. Our guys are fielding calls on other teams. I don’t see anything heating up today or tomorrow. We’ll see what happens on Monday. …The results of the game aren’t going to dictate what we do. It’s a matter of whether we think it’s a move that’s right for our team. If it’s a good value, we’ll do it, whether its buying or selling as they say. But what happens on Sunday doesn’t really dictate what we’re going to be doing.“

title: NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Jacoby Brissett, Jeffery Simmons, more
summary: Wise move for the Ravens to add Jacoby Brissett? Did the Bears give up too much to go all-in with Jeffery Simmons? Let's evaluate eight trades before the deadline.
full_text:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline , which is Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET.

 When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

 Here are our evaluations for eight deals of trading season, including two quarterback moves ( Jacoby Brissett and J.J. McCarthy ) and the massive blockbuster sending  Jeffery Simmons to Chicago. Check back through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

 

 
 Jump to a trade: 
 Brissett |  Simmons |  Buckner |  Nelson 
 Harrison  |  Jurgens  |  Porter | McCarthy 

 
 

 

 Cardinals trade QB Brissett to Ravens 
 Ravens get: QB Jacoby Brissett , 2027 fifth-round pick 
 Cardinals get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 seventh-round pick

 Ravens grade: B+ 
 Cardinals grade: B

 With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both hurt , the Ravens are throwing a Hail Mary to save their season. Baltimore is trading for veteran Brissett, shortly after the Cardinals benched him in favor of Gardner Minshew II .

 Brissett is a respected bridge quarterback and has played around expectations this season in Arizona. He has a 48.9 QBR, which ranks 23rd out of 30 qualifying starters. That number alone is probably selling Brissett's performance short this season, though, considering he was playing behind the O-line unit that ranked 31st in pass block win rate and was able to use play-action just 18% of the time (27th most). He has posted a plus-5% completion percentage over expectation, per NFL Next Gen Stats (fifth) along with an average 15% off-target rate. And he has been sacked 5.7% of the time (roughly average but notable, given the lack of pass protection). He did throw seven interceptions in eight games, but because he hasn't fumbled yet this season, his turnover rate is roughly average, too.

 

 We can zoom out on Brissett's performance and see a similar picture. Since 2021, he has a 51.1 QBR and a plus-3% completion percentage over expectation (along with a 16% off-target rate), though his QBR was worse than that the past two years. All of this is to say, Brissett is rightfully a fringe starter in the NFL, but that also makes him a substantial upgrade over undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano .

 The Ravens lost 33-10 to the Jaguars on Thursday night with Fagnano (and also some Derrick Henry in the Wildcat) at quarterback. In all likelihood, Baltimore's season is over with Jackson currently on injured reserve and the team at 4-5. Ravens coach Jesse Minter has said Jackson's injury is "potentially" season-ending. But Brissett gives the team at least a sliver of hope of staying afloat long enough to hand the reins back to Jackson with a shot at the playoffs.

 But make no mistake, those chances are extremely slim. Even knowing Brissett is about to take over at QB (and assuming Jackson has, say, a 30% chance of coming back in games starting in Week 14, ESPN's Football Power Index  gives Baltimore only a 3% chance of reaching the playoffs. If Jackson is indeed able to come back, that number goes up, but it's still a long shot. The cost here is low. By ESPN's draft pick valuations, the swap works out to the equivalent of an early sixth-round pick. Considering the team's upside if it does get Jackson back, I think that is easily worth it for Baltimore.

 As for Arizona? Brissett's role with the Cardinals always had an expiration date. The team decided to have two bridge quarterbacks on its roster heading into this season and recently turned to the second one in Minshew, while demoting Brissett to third-string. Eventually, the Cards will likely turn from Minshew to Carson Beck , too. So trading Brissett before the deadline was an easy choice; they can recoup some draft value for him and save a few million along the way (Brissett had a $9.7 million base salary this year, and if the contract is untouched, the Ravens will take on the remaining portion of that).

 

 I actually thought Arizona might get a little more for Brissett, because I could have imagined the Vikings -- and maybe the Eagles or Browns -- being interested, as well. But it certainly made sense to deal him, and the Cardinals almost had to make sure they did so before the deadline. -- Walder 

 
 

 Titans trade DT Simmons to Bears 
 Bears get:  DT Jeffery Simmons , 2028 fifth-round pick 
 Titans get: 2027 first-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 first-round pick

 Bears grade: C 
 Titans grade: A

This trade is extremely fun. The Bears were already an enjoyable and fascinating team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. And now they've added one of the game's truly elite defensive players. They also gave up a lot to do so.
 The Bears enter Week 8 as ESPN Football Power Index 's seventh-best team, with an 80% chance to reach the playoffs and a 13% chance to reach the Super Bowl. When quarterback Caleb Williams has played this season, their offense has produced 0.14 EPA per play, which would be fourth-best in the NFL. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has also been working miracles -- without major turnover luck this time -- but there was a clear need for reinforcements on the defensive depth chart. And now the Bears have landed the best defensive tackle in the league, period.

 Simmons has four sacks this season, despite having his pass rush opportunities limited by being on a bad team. He leads all interior linemen in pass rush win rate and ranks fifth in pressure rate. His run stop win rate is above average. And it is hardly a fluke: Simmons ranked second in pass rush win rate (and above average in run stop win rate) while recording 11 sacks last year in a season in which he might have merited Defensive Player of the Year consideration if not for Myles Garrett  setting the single-season sacks record.

 Simmons is a force and a massive upgrade at an area of weakness. The Bears had been playing 33-year-old Grady Jarrett (who has zero sacks but a solid pass rush win rate) alongside veteran journeymen Kentavius Street , Neville Gallimore and James Lynch . Simmons is an entirely different level of player.

 So, Simmons absolutely makes sense for the Bears, and in general, I am strongly in favor of Chicago making deadline additions this season. But there is a compensation limit where a trade ceases to make sense, and I think the Bears ran past it.

 

 Simmons joins a small fraternity of non-quarterbacks to be traded for multiple first-round picks in recent years: edge rushers Micah Parsons and Khalil Mack , offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil , safety Jamal Adams and cornerback Sauce Gardner . The results have been mixed at best for the acquiring team and Simmons, at 29 years old, is the oldest of these players at the time of the deal (Mack was the previous oldest, as the Bears acquired him as a 27-year-old in 2018).

 Simmons is under contract through 2030. Assuming that contract is untouched, he will cost $27 million in 2027 and $29.8 million in 2028, with the 2028 base salary becoming fully guaranteed the year prior. That is below what Simmons would make on the open market, but it's still a decent-sized contract for Chicago to take on.

 The money saved on Simmons' contract compared to what he would make as a free agent will not reach the expected surplus value of a first-round pick. Even accounting for the high levels of uncertainty in the NFL draft, first-round selections can deliver massive value for NFL teams -- stars on very affordable contracts. The 2027 pick will likely be toward the end of this year's draft, and it seems hard to imagine that 2028 won't be a late first-rounder, too. But I…

full_text:

Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder give us final score picks for every game.

 What we're hearing on the Bengals: The numbers say quarterback  Joe Burrow is in the midst of a career year. After he tallied six touchdowns (five passing, one rushing) last week, that's what Falcons DC Jeff Ulbrich believes, too. Said Ulbrich: "He's playing his best football that he's ever played in his career, in my opinion, right now." Burrow leads the NFL in passing TDs (20) and ranks fourth in passing yards (2,115). -- Ben Baby 

 What we're hearing on the Falcons:  Atlanta will need to disrupt Burrow to give itself the best chance to win. The Falcons have the personnel and scheme to do it, too -- Brandon Dorlus and Gervon Dexter Sr . rank first and second, respectively, in the NFL among DTs in pressure rate. They are the first teammates to be first and second in that category through eight weeks since 2018. -- Marc Raimondi

Atlanta can pressure QBs, but Burrow gets the ball out quickly enough to make that tough. If the rush doesn't get there, the Falcons allow almost a 75% completion percentage. With WRs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins , Cincinnati has the guys to turn those clean pockets into TD drives. Read more . -- Maldonado

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Proposing deals for Tony Pollard, Riq Woolen, others
summary: Our NFL experts pitched trade offers they'd love to see get done before Tuesday's deadline, including moves for Tony Pollard, Riq Woolen, Jonathan Taylor and Jessie Bates III.
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is three days away, and we've already seen a handful of major moves from teams. The Colts traded away cornerstones on both sides of the ball, with guard Quenton Nelson  to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner  to the 49ers. And the Bears dealt a package that included two first-round picks to land Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . Two quarterbacks have also switched teams, with J.J. McCarthy going to the Giants and Jacoby Brissett joining the Ravens.

 But what other big deals could be on the horizon? Ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline , we asked eight experts from ESPN and NFL Network to pitch realistic trade offers that they would love to see get done. They laid out the compensation for each team and then explained why the deals would make sense for both parties involved.

 Here are the trades they are proposing, starting with the running back on everyone's mind ahead of the deadline.

 

 
 Jump to a deal for a player: 
 Bates | Brown | Downs |  Ojomo 
 Pollard  |  Suamataia | Taylor | Woolen 

 
 

 Judy Battista's offer 
 

 Minnesota Vikings get: RB Jonathan Taylor 
 Indianapolis Colts get: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 third-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick ( acquired from NYG )

 Why this deal makes sense for both sides: It's a haul (similar to one that sent RB  Christian McCaffrey  to the 49ers in 2022), but the Vikings need Taylor's home run threat to pair with QB  Kyler Murray 's explosive rushing ability. Up until this point of the season, their offense has been largely stagnant despite the presence of receivers Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison .

 The Vikings have arguably the best defense in the league, but they'll need to score points for a deep playoff run. The Colts, engaged in a fire sale and potentially  hoping to get a first-rounder for Taylor, get plenty of draft picks to help kickstart what looks like a total rebuild.

 

 
 

 Matt Bowen's offer 
 

 Chicago Bears get: CB Riq Woolen 
 Philadelphia Eagles get: 2027 fifth-round pick

 Why this deal makes sense for both sides: The Bears already made an aggressive trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons -- a game changer in the front -- but they still need more top-end speed in the back end. Woolen brings the physical traits and boundary speed to play man coverage with his 6-foot-4 frame, plus he fits in coordinator Dennis Allen's split-safety schemes as a ball disruptor (12 interceptions and 59 pass breakups in his career).

 For the Eagles, they get a Day 3 return on Woolen, who is set to be a free agent in 2027 after signing a one-year deal with Philly.

 

 
 Jeremy Fowler's offer 
 

 Kansas City Chiefs get: WR  Josh Downs 
 Indianapolis Colts get: 2027 fourth-round pick

 Why this deal makes sense for both sides: Kansas City has been looking for receiver help, and Indianapolis is weighing trade options for Downs, who wants out . The Colts would love a third-round pick for him but might need to settle for a fourth. The Chiefs would get a much-needed additional playmaker, and the Colts would strengthen their rebuild, though Downs' absence would badly hurt an already struggling offense.

 

 

 
 Aaron Schatz's offer 
 

 Los Angeles Rams get: WR Dyami Brown , 2027 seventh-round pick 
 Washington Commanders get: 2027 sixth-round pick

 Why this deal makes sense for both sides: Don't be fooled by Brown's low average of 10.4 yards per reception; he's primarily a deep threat who stretches the field. And though it feels like he has been around for years, he's still only 27 years old.

 For the Rams, Brown would probably be a better receiving option than Tutu Atwell . And more importantly for coach Sean McVay's offense, Brown is a better run blocker with 30 pounds on Atwell. Brown shouldn't demand much of a return, and the Rams don't have a 2027 seventh-round pick (it was flipped to the Ravens in 2024 as part of a deal involving CB  Tre'Davious White ).

 

 
 Ben Solak's offer 
 

 Green Bay Packers get: RB Tony Pollard 
 Tennessee Titans get: 2027 fourth-round pick

 Why this deal makes sense for both sides: Even if the Packers trust they'll have running back  Josh Jacobs for the rest of the season after his six-game stint on the commissioner exempt list , his lack of explosive runs is disqualifying from consistent 15-plus-carry games. Jacobs' longest run of the season is 10 yards, and he is 26th out of 35 running backs in 10-plus-yard rush rate since the start of last season. Meanwhile, Pollard is 11th and has the necessary pass-catching chops to play all three downs in Green Bay's offense.

 The Packers have an extra fourth-round pick, thanks to the Rashan Gary trade with Dallas in March, and could easily flip it to introduce more balance to their playoff-contending team.

 

 
 Seth Walder's offer 
 

 Buffalo Bills get: S Jessie Bates III 
 Atlanta Falcons get: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 sixth-round pick

 Note: Atlanta would convert all but the minimum of Bates' remaining 2026 base salary into a signing bonus prior to this proposed trade. 

 Why this deal makes sense for both sides: The  release of C.J. Gardner-Johnson means there is a perfect opening for Bates -- one of the game's best safeties -- in Buffalo's secondary. But the sneaky reason why this could happen? The Falcons have over $109 million of 2027 cap space (most in the NFL), per OverTheCap.com. So they're almost guaranteed to be active in free agency, which in turn means there's a chance they wouldn't get a compensatory pick for Bates (because signings cancel out departures when compensatory picks are distributed). If the Falcons keep Bates through the deadline, the risk they lose him for nothing is high.

 Buffalo is in the opposite cap situation, so this would be like a short-term signing. But Bates probably would net them something like a fourth-round compensatory pick in 2028 if he signed elsewhere next offseason, significantly softening how much draft capital Buffalo is giving up in this scenario.

 

 
 Cameron Wolfe's offer 
 

 Jacksonville Jaguars get: DT Moro Ojomo 
 Philadelphia Eagles get: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fourth-round pick

 Why this deal makes sense for both sides: The Jaguars were already looking heavy into interior defensive line upgrades before their elite run-stopping nose tackle  DaVon Hamilton  suffered a season-ending quad injury Sunday. Now an addition feels mandatory for this Super Bowl-contending team. Ojomo looks like the best option available, and he would be an excellent fit as a three-down disruptor next to Arik Armstead .

 At times, Ojomo has looked like the Eagles' best defensive lineman on tape this season. And though they value him a lot, he is a free agent after this season on a team that already granted big deals to DTs  Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis . This move would allow the 2-6 Eagles to load up on more draft capital, locking in two middle-round picks instead of one potential compensatory pick if Ojomo left in free agency.

 

 
 
 

 Field Yates' offer 
 

 Green Bay Packers get: OL Kingsley Suamataia 
 Kansas City Chiefs get: 2027 fourth-round pick

 Why this deal makes sense for both sides:  After starting all of last season for the Chiefs, Suamataia has been benched twice this season  despite backup options yielding less than optimal results in his stead. However, he could still be a valuable asset to another team given he's just 23, has positional versatility and is under contract through next season. The Packers must continue to hurl resources at an offensive line that has battled injuries and ineffectiveness through eight weeks, so giving up a fourth-round pick is worth it.

title: Bengals face Falcons S Jessie Bates III, evoking mixed emotions
summary: Cincinnati hasn't been to the playoffs since Bates' departure, but Atlanta also hasn't reached the postseason since his arrival.
full_text:
MADRID -- When the Cincinnati Bengals step on the field at the Santiago Bernabeu in Madrid on Sunday to face the Atlanta Falcons , the Bengals will be posed with a question it once forced other teams to ask.

 How does one account for safety Jessie Bates III ? 

 From 2018 to 2022, Bates emerged as one of Cincinnati's best playmakers in the team's run to the Super Bowl at the end of the 2021 season. But after Bates left Cincinnati in free agency, he has spent the past four seasons with the Falcons, with whom he has maintained his perch as one of the best in the NFL.

 And ahead of Sunday's game, Bates was asked how much he thinks about the events that led him to leave the team that drafted him.

 "Coming here to Atlanta has changed my life, my family's trajectory, what that looks like moving forward," Bates told ESPN. "But at the same time, it's like, damn, you want to play in meaningful football games. I haven't played in the playoffs since I left there. And I don't think they've been in the playoffs, either, since I left."

 Bates is correct. The Falcons (3-5) could use a win to jump-start their season and break a nine-year postseason drought. Cincinnati (5-2) is looking to secure its first playoff berth since 2022.

 That was Bates' last season with Cincinnati, which drafted him in 2018 with a second-round pick. Bengals coach Zac Taylor, who arrived a year after Bates was drafted, recalled how the former Wake Forest standout went from a young player adjusting to a new scheme to an ascending star.

 "He was really just a perfect example of a guy that just shows growth from every year, from years one through five, and proud of the way he attacked it," said Taylor, who continued to extoll everything from Bates' reputation in the locker room and community to how he received coaching. "I don't usually spend this much time praising the other team, but Jessie's one that I've always really liked."

 But that growth clashed with a couple of the NFL's realities. In a league with a salary cap, decisions must be made on which players are considered most essential. And after quarterback Joe Burrow and the passing attack proved to be one of the best in the NFL, that's what the Bengals spent their resources on.

 In hindsight, even just looking at the financial aspect of the decision, one could argue it cost the Bengals more to let Bates leave.

 Bates signed with the Falcons on a four-year deal worth just over $64 million. The contract included guaranteed money in the second year, which is something Cincinnati only just started doing for non-quarterbacks.

 Since then, Cincinnati has tried four players in Bates' former role. The combined value of those contracts is $77.9 million, according to OverTheCap.com. That includes the rookie deal for current Bengals cornerback Dax Hill , a 2022 first-round pick who has never settled into a full-time position after initially being drafted to replace Bates.

 This offseason, the Bengals took their biggest swing at correcting the decision. They signed former  Bryan Cook , who was on two Super Bowl-winning teams with the Chiefs, to a three-year deal worth just over $40 million.

 And though the secondary has still had its ups and downs, defensive coordinator Al Golden has been very pleased with how the team's current safeties stack up.

 " Jordan [Battle ] can stand on his own," Golden said. "Obviously, [ Kyle] Dugger  has been in the league seven years. He can stand on his own. Cook has solidified himself in this league and is a champion."

 Though Atlanta hasn't been successful as a club, the 29-year-old Bates has racked up career accolades. He reached the Pro Bowl in 2023, his first year with the Falcons, and is a two-time second-team All-Pro selection.

 This season, he has been just as dynamic. According to ESPN Research, Bates and the New York Giants' Jevon Holland are the only safeties with multiple forced fumbles, an interception and at least four pass deflections.

 And the impact goes beyond the numbers. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said Bates was one of the best players he had ever been around in nearly three decades in the NFL.

 "As long as you've got Jessie Bates on your defense, you've got a chance because he's going to make sure he's going to touch every single human being from the front to the back and make sure we get the best version of them," Ulbrich said.

 On Sunday, it will be the Bengals' turn to account for Bates. On Thursday in Madrid, he said it will be exciting and bittersweet to go up against players he knows well and a franchise that produced "some of the best times of my life."

 And it will be a reminder of just how things can go in the NFL.

 "That's just part of the business," Bates said. "Sometimes, you got to leave a spot that you love, and there's more blessings on the other side of it."
