title: Week 9 betting preview: Analysis, best bets, TD predictions for Sunday
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 9 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: Find betting value.

 Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 9.

 From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 Jump to: 
 Bowen's favorite bets 
 Solak's plays  | Walder's props 
 Clay's TD projections 

 

 

 Bowen's favorite bets 
 Heading into the Week 9 Sunday slate, I'm going to start with the late-window Packers-Patriots matchup in New England, giving you my pick for the game. I have some thoughts there on the Green Bay defense based on what it is showing on the tape. Plus, I have a couple more game picks to look at -- including a two-team teaser -- and I'll throw down some props, too.

 Green Bay Packers  at New England Patriots 
4:25 p.m. ET on Fox; Line: NE -3.5, O/U: 45.5

 

 I'll start with the Packers' defense under coordinator Jonathan Gannon. This unit is playing its best football of the season, allowing 14.8 PPG over the past four while giving up just 4.5 yards per play. The Packers are taking the ball away, too, recording 11 turnovers in this four-game stretch. We'll see a lot of late movement in the secondary, with multiple fronts and disguised pressures, which will force Patriots quarterback Drake Maye to read it out post-snap with a wide receiver group that is still banged up. Offensively for the Packers, the combo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden creates vertical opportunities for quarterback Jordan Love . My concern here? Can Green Bay get the running game going with Josh Jacobs ? I don't see a burst yet from Jacobs, which the Packers will need to attack the edges on outside zone run concepts. But with the added prep time, I like Green Bay to cover here .

 Denver Broncos -2.5 at Carolina Panthers 

 

 The Panthers' offensive line is beat up, and they can't protect consistently on the edges, as quarterback Bryce Young has been sacked 11 times over the last two games. That's trouble versus a Denver pass rush that has a pressure rate of 40.4% (second highest in the league). Yes, Jonah Coleman can give the Broncos' run game a boost versus a Panthers defense allowing 140.7 rushing yards per game (third most), but I'm taking Denver because of its ability to disrupt the pocket.

 Two team, 6.5-point teaser (-143): Arizona Cardinals +15 at Seattle Seahawks , Detroit Lions -0.5 at Miami Dolphins 

 Moving the Cardinals to +15 points at Seattle, which will have Drew Lock making the start for an injured Sam Darnold , feels more comfortable. I like this Cardinals offense with Gardner Minshew II at quarterback, too. Minshew is fearless with the ball. And while that can lead to turnover situations, Minshew has the movement traits to keep plays alive, which will allow Arizona to compete at a higher rate on Sunday.

 Teasing the Lions down to almost a moneyline play is the smart move here on the road in Miami. Detroit showed us last week that it can go run-heavy with Jahmyr Gibbs to close out games, and we know the Lions will have pass-game answers for a Miami defense that has been more zone-heavy this season.

 
 Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . 

 

 Jahmyr Gibbs receiving yards OVER 26.5 (-116) 

 I missed on Gibbs last week, but this is a good matchup for him in the passing game. Miami is allowing 40.6 receiving yards per game to opposing running backs, and Gibbs has 27 or more yards in six of seven games played this season.

 Bryce Young passing yards UNDER 237.5 passing yards (-113) 

 I rarely play the under, but Young has thrown for fewer than 210 yards in each of his past two starts. And as we discussed above, the Broncos' pass rush has matchup advantages here on the edges.

title: Jacoby Brissett brings hope but realistic expectations for spiraling Ravens
summary: The Ravens know what they're getting in acquiring veteran journeyman QB, but does Jacoby Brissett know what he's in for?
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens understand what they're getting in acquiring veteran journeyman quarterback Jacoby Brissett . But does Brissett realize the situation he's coming into with the Ravens? 
 
 The Ravens officially finalized their trade with the Arizona Cardinals on Friday by sending a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-rounder in exchange for Brissett and a 2027 fourth-round selection. Baltimore knows it's adding an experienced starting-caliber quarterback who has a track record of completing over 60% of his passes and directing a middle-of-the-road offense. 
 
 For Brissett, he's not just coming into a situation where he's trying to keep the Ravens' season afloat in case an injured Lamar Jackson (right thumb) can return by the end of the season. Brissett is taking over an offense that looks broken, from the lack of discipline to poor blocking to the historic struggles to score. 
 
 
 
 The Ravens (4-5) have failed to score more than 14 points in four straight games, which is a team record in futility. This didn't happen when Baltimore went through a five-game touchdown drought in 2000. This didn't happen when first-round quarterback Kyle Boller turned out to be a bust in 2003. This didn't happen in 2015 when the Ravens started Matt Schaub, Jimmy Clausen and Ryan Mallett after Joe Flacco suffered a season-ending knee injury. 
 
 The players aren't blaming the loss of Jackson for the offensive flop, even though the lack of a two-time NFL MVP has certainly pulled the plug on Baltimore's explosiveness. It hasn't helped that top backup  Tyler "Snoop" Huntley  is out for the season with a turf toe injury. 
 
 The arrival of Brissett brings hope but also realistic expectations. 
 
 "I think that'll bode well for us," Ravens offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley said after Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . "But there's a lot of things that we need to fix on our end. I don't think anyone can just come in and fix all the problems." 
 
 Let's take a look at the problems: 
 
 

 

 
 
 
 Pre-snap penalties 
 
 
 It really feels like the Ravens' offense leads the league in hurting itself. With four false-start penalties Thursday, Baltimore has now been flagged for false starts 24 times this season, the most in the league. 
 
 The Ravens already have more false-start penalties through nine games this season than they did in all 17 games last season (19 false starts). Part of the problem could be the constant changes due to injuries. Baltimore has had three different starting centers and three different starting quarterbacks. 
 
 "It's very frustrating, and again, it's just ownership," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "It's ownership of players and coaches [when] it keeps happening, [but] it's a ninth game, so there's no, 'We haven't done this, we haven't done that or whatever. We've got a new guy in there [at quarterback].' He's been here all season [and] been here all training camp. So, the pre-snap penalties are unacceptable."  
 
 Stanley tops the Ravens with seven false starts, which is more than the tallies of seven teams. The others who have committed multiple false starts are: tight end Mark Andrews (six), guard John Simpson (five) and offensive tackle Roger Rosengarten (five). 
 
 "I just have to be better," Stanley said. "I'm trying to get off the ball as soon as I hear the quarterback, but that's too fast, so I need to hone that back a little bit and maybe come off slower. But whatever the case, we have to be on the ball. We can't afford to have pre-snap penalties. They stall drives and take away points from us."  
 
 
 
 
 
 Pressure on the quarterback 
 
 
 The frustration with the offensive line boiled over Thursday night, when offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford spiked his tablet while yelling at his players on the sideline. 
 
 "He was fired up about the little things that we mess up," said Ravens guard Olaivavega Ioane , the team's rookie first-round pick. "You look at it the wrong way, and you think that's a problem. That's not a problem. Like, he was doing the right thing. Sometimes it's the right thing to be a little aggressive with it. That's just what everybody needs, and with the way the game went, it's what we needed."  
 
 
 
 The Ravens' offensive linemen have taken it personally after watching their top two quarterbacks leave with injuries in the first half of Sunday's loss at Buffalo. Jackson injured his right thumb when he was attempting to pass and his hand hit Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau , who had gotten too much penetration on the right side. Then, Huntley hurt his toe after Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver twisted him to the ground after he got rid of the ball. 
 
 Baltimore's pressure rate allowed is 36%, which ranks 24th in the NFL. It's also the third-worst rate for the Ravens since pressure rate began getting tracked in 2009. 
 
 Brissett needs better play out of Baltimore's offensive line. Since the start of the 2025 season, Brissett has been sacked the fifth-most times (62) in the league. 
 
 "We know it's not our standard, and all the guys in the room know that," Ioane said. "I'll be the first one to say it. You don't have to hear it from [anybody] else. We already know ourselves. We take a lot of pride in going out there and protecting the quarterback. Some games it doesn't go like that, but I have big faith in our O-line, and I still do. The guys that went out there and played, they did their job to the best of their ability, and that's all there is to it."  
 
 
 
 
 
 Lack of scoring 
 
 
 With a healthy Jackson, the Ravens averaged 29 points in the first four games, which ranked sixth in the NFL. Without Jackson, Baltimore's scoring has plummeted to 14.6 points over the last five games, which is 30th over that span. 
 
 Are the struggles simply the result of the Ravens missing Jackson? 
 
 "Lamar is incredible. He is obviously going to be sorely missed," Andrews said. "He's such a special player and a leader on this team, and has been for a long, long time. But again, we have guys that are going to step up. We have so many great players on this team, and we deserve to put out a better product because we have such talented players and coaches and guys that really want to get this thing going." 
 
 One of the reasons the Ravens have lost four straight and fallen into last place in the AFC North is that Baltimore's other star players have not stepped up. Without Jackson over the last five games, running back Derrick Henry is averaging 63 yards rushing (15th during that stretch) and wide receiver Zay Flowers has averaged 52.3 yards receiving (42nd). 
 
 Jackson, who was placed on injured reserve before Thursday's game, is eligible to be activated for the Dec. 13 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . In the next three games without Jackson, Brissett will look to turn around the Ravens against defenses that all rank in the bottom half of the league in points allowed: Los Angeles Chargers (20th), Carolina Panthers (28th) and Houston Texans (18th). 
 
 "We need all hands on deck," Henry said. "I feel like [Brissett] can come in and help us. We'll be excited to have him, and we'll see where it goes."

title: Inside the evolution of Caleb Williams' MVP candidacy
summary: Williams has the fourth-shortest odds to win MVP as the Bears are currently favored to win the NFC.
full_text:
Chicago Bears  wide receiver  Luther Burden III ran back to the visitors sideline at Seattle's Lumen Field on Monday night with a message for quarterback Caleb Williams .

 The Bears had just accomplished a rare feat. Before Burden caught a 1-yard touchdown pass at the end of an opening drive that spanned 8 minutes, 32 seconds, the last team to score a touchdown against Seattle on its first possession was the 49ers in Week 1 of the 2025 season.

 "I went up to him and told him I don't care who they is," the wide receiver said about the defending Super Bowl champs. "No. 1 defense, I don't care."

 After slapping hands with his teammate, Williams stood up from the bench and echoed Burden's sentiment.

 "I don't give a f--- who they are!" Williams yelled.

 Chicago's 34-17 takedown of the Seahawks capped a unique set of primetime performances as the Bears beat Super Bowl runner-up New England in Week 7 and the defending champs in back-to-back games. It was the first such sequence in franchise history.

 

 The victory made the Bears the favorites to represent the NFC in Super Bowl LXI, and it planted Williams firmly in the MVP conversation. Williams entered Week 9 with the fourth-shortest odds (+500) to win MVP, according to DraftKings Sportsbook. He trailed the Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen (+165), San Francisco 49ers' Brock Purdy (+450) and Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow (+475).

 The Bears (6-2) have won all three games since Williams returned from a hamstring injury that sidelined him Weeks 3-5. In fact, they haven't trailed in any of the three and have topped 30 points each time. That streak will be challenged Sunday night by a visiting Tampa Bay Buccaneers team yielding just 18.9 points per game, the fifth-best mark in the league.

 Then again, no quarterback had thrown for 200 yards on Seattle's defense in 2026 until Williams reached 247. That was his third game with at least one touchdown, no interceptions and a 70% or higher completion percentage this season, tying him for the league lead, according to ESPN Research.

 Williams ranks second in completion percentage (70.9%), fourth in interception rate (0.6), seventh in success rate (51.1), fifth in yards per attempt (8.0) and 11th in yards per game (253.4). He is third in QBR (78.9), third in EPA per dropback (0.24) and fifth in win probability added (117.0%).

 Here's a look at how Williams has played his way into the MVP mix.

 Why Caleb Williams' decisiveness wins 
 One of the last things Williams and USC coach Lincoln Riley would utter during Trojans quarterback meetings was to be decisive.

 "When you're hesitant, bad things happen," Williams said. "So, decisiveness wins is what I go by, a slogan I go by."

 While he was sidelined for three games, Williams often thought about ways he could demonstrate better decisiveness when he got back on the field. The things that would allow him to play faster and deliver a cleaner ball to his intended target meant having conviction in where his reads would take him.

 "Most of the time, you're seeing less of the superhero plays," backup quarterback Tyson Bagent said. "He's only letting that come when it presents itself.

 

 "Other than that, he's anticipating things like I haven't seen him do before, and he's just in a good rhythm, playing at a high level."

 That decisiveness has generated more consistency in the passing game. Williams became the first Bears quarterback since Mitchell Trubisky in 2018 to throw for 300 yards in back-to-back wins over the Falcons and Patriots.

 It has also elevated the play of his top pass catchers. After totaling 13 receptions for 110 yards in the first five games of the season, tight end Colston Loveland has turned 20 catches into 199 yards and two touchdowns since Williams' return in Week 6.

 Williams' decisiveness has allowed him to become the NFL's most successful quarterback when not under duress. He has completed 86% of his passes (96 of 112 attempts) when not pressured, the highest completion percentage when not pressured by any quarterback through five starts of a season since ESPN began tracking pressures in 2009.

 And most impressively, he has yet to throw an interception on those 112 attempts.

 That's considerable improvement from last season, when he completed 66.2% of his passes without pressure, the third-lowest rate in the league along with the fourth-highest off-target rate (16.1%).

 In his past three games, Williams is 63-of-70 (90%) when not pressured. He leads all quarterbacks with an 85.7% completion rate when not under duress.

 Less Superman, more checkdowns are not a bad thing 
 One hallmark of Bears training camp practices was long-drive drills as the offense ate up the clock while deliberately moving the ball downfield.

 Those grind-it-out periods translated to the regular season. In total, the Bears have run 21 drives that went 10-plus plays (second most in the NFL), with 15 of those drives culminating in a touchdown or field goal.

 On the Bears' opening drive in Seattle, Williams led his unit 80 yards on 17 plays while attempting 10 short throws, none that resulted in more than a 15-yard completion.

 "I would say I've grown in that area," Williams said. "I can go back to high school; all I did was take shots. I went to college and scrambled around a little bit. I took a few checkdowns, very little.

 

 "And then my first year [in the NFL] was very little. I got sacked a lot, all that. Then this past year, I found a few more [checkdowns], scrambled still a little bit. And then this year, it's just being a lot more comfortable with the playbook and understanding it and what we want to do with certain plays. From there, being able to, when they don't get the specific coverage, just being able to check the ball down and keep the drive alive."

 That mindset is the catalyst behind Williams' 71% completion percentage, which ranks second behind Burrow. Williams ranks fifth in the NFL in yards per attempt (8.0) and 28th in air yards per attempt (6.5)

 The Bears' quarterback already has three games during which he has completed at least 70% of his passes after having none in 2025.

 "He's hitting the top of the drop and the ball's coming out where it's supposed to be or he's quickly down to a progression or checkdown to keep us on schedule," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. "I think he and a lot of our guys realize now if we can in these normal-down situations, we're just going to keep unloading the clip, and we're going to keep firing and keep doing all this. When it's there, take it; when it's not, put it in play."

 Putting more on Caleb Williams' plate 
 In preparation for the reigning Super Bowl champion defense, Ben Johnson and his coaches created a game plan to combat the variety of fronts and pressures Seattle runs out of the same personnel groupings.

 The goal was to generate explosive runs while simultaneously reducing negative plays. It was a complex plan that demanded more from Williams to put the offense in position to succeed.

 "There were probably more kills on each and every run play than we normally have," Taylor said. "So, he's got a lot of responsibility in terms of diagnosing what the front is, understanding why we're killing a play or why we're changing a play based on what the look is, because they're not all the same."

 Williams battled through the stress that came with mastering this heavy pre-snap mental load. Taylor noted how frustrated the quarterback grew with himself in walk-throughs while spitting out the calls, well before this task got harder with the element of Seattle's crowd noise.

 By game time, the hiccups Williams had experienced were in the past.

 

 "He has so much going on," right tackle Darnell Wright said. "He'll start the week, he'll have all of his stuff and then by the time we get to the game, I don't know how -- he's obviously studying -- but for some reason, it starts off pretty bumpy. We all have our little bumps and then by the…

title: NFL Week 9 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
summary: QB controversy in Minnesota? Browns upsetting the Saints? Touchdowns for two rookie RBs? Let's predict 15 things for Week 9.
full_text:
Week 9 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Jaguars easily handled the Ravens on  Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 14 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Can the Browns bounce back with an upset win over the Saints? Will rookie running backs Jonah Coleman  (Broncos) and  Kaelon Black  (49ers) score touchdowns this weekend? Does Colts WR Keenan Allen have fantasy potential against the Cowboys? And could  Carson Wentz cause some QB controversy in Minnesota?

 Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Green Bay Packers +3 (+140 moneyline) at New England Patriots 

 Green Bay's defense can take away the throws driving New England quarterback  Drake Maye 's hot streak in Sunday's game . On passes traveling 10-plus yards, the Packers have allowed just two touchdowns and snagged seven interceptions.

 Maye could still hurt the Packers with his legs, but his receiving group is banged up -- the Patriots are again without  A.J. Brown , who has played just 26% of their offensive plays this season. On the other end, Green Bay quarterback  Jordan Love  can create enough big plays throwing to  Christian Watson and Matthew Golden  to win outright.

 
 

 

 Cleveland Browns +3 (135 moneyline) at New Orleans Saints 

 Quarterback Tyler Shough has cooled off after leading the NFL in passing yards through the first two weeks. His early production depended heavily on passing volume while trailing, and that volume has dropped substantially.

 Cleveland's strong pass defense and top-10 pressure rate make this a difficult spot for Shough to rebound Sunday . The Saints are much easier to attack on the ground, giving Browns RB Quinshon Judkins a chance to keep QB Shedeur Sanders and the offense more balanced. Cleveland's protection is a concern, but its defense can keep this ugly.

 

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 Alim McNeill , DT, Detroit Lions : 1.5 sacks, 5 pressures, 25% pass rush win rate

 McNeill, who has 4.5 sacks on the season, leads all defensive tackles in pass rush win rate. And he has an excellent chance to convert that into sacks Sunday because Miami quarterback  Malik Willis has been sacked on 9.3% of his dropbacks this season -- third highest among qualifying quarterbacks. Plus, even if guard Kadyn Proctor returns from a concussion this week, all three members of the Dolphins' interior line are either average or below average in pass block win rate.

 
 

 Jonah Coleman , RB, Denver Broncos : 15 carries, 79 rushing yards, 4 receptions, 29 receiving yards, 1 touchdown

 Coleman looks well positioned to follow up his productive game against the Chiefs with another strong performance against the Panthers . Carolina's run defense isn't good, ranking 26th in EPA allowed per designed carry, 28th in yards allowed per carry, 24th in yards before contact allowed per carry and 28th in yards after contact allowed per carry.

 But it's more than that. The Panthers also have a run-inducing defense, with the sixth-lowest pass rate over expected against them, per NFL Next Gen Stats. That means Coleman's rushing attempts should go up.

 
 

 Sauce Gardner , CB, Indianapolis Colts : 34 coverage snaps, 4 targets, 2 receptions allowed, 17 receiving yards allowed

 Gardner had a rough start to the season, though NFL Next Gen Stats' metrics and player-tracking work I've done suggest he played sticky coverage and simply gave up a couple more catches than expected. Regardless, he has played better recently, allowing a tiny 0.3 yards per coverage snap over the past three games and almost getting an interception last week .

 Gardner should mostly face off against Cowboys WR  George Pickens , who is coming off a two-reception performance against the Cardinals . Sunday's game  could mark another strong performance for the fifth-year cornerback.

 

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Keenan Allen , WR, Indianapolis Colts (43.6% rostered in ESPN leagues) 

 Allen caught seven passes for a team-high 67 yards  last week in Jacksonville and leads the Colts with 34 receptions this season. On Sunday , he'll face a Cowboys defense that has allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

 Allen has scored just one touchdown this season, but his reception volume (at least six catches in four games) makes him a viable flex option in deeper leagues. He has scored at least nine fantasy points in three of his past four games, including one with 16.2 points.

 

 
 

 Malik Willis , QB, Miami Dolphins (16.0%) 

 Despite Miami's struggles on offense, Willis has scored at least 18 fantasy points in two of his past three games. His rushing ability has helped, with 225 yards and three touchdowns on the ground this season. All of that makes him one of my favorite Week 9 streamers, especially against a Lions defense that has allowed the most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks. Willis is worth holding on to even after this week, as Miami will face weak defenses in the Colts, Bills and Jets.

 
 

 Devin Singletary , RB, New York Giants (9.9%) 

 Courtesy of a 2-yard touchdown run  against the Texans in Week 7 , Singletary turned eight touches into 14.5 fantasy points. He could see more work this Sunday against the Eagles , as  Tyrone Tracy Jr . is on IR ( hamstring ) and  Cam Skattebo  -- who has had fumbling issues -- is doubtful to play ( hamstring ).

 The matchup against Philadelphia is also encouraging. The Eagles have allowed the fifth-most rushing yards per game and 10 rushing touchdowns this season. Singletary should be on the flex radar for fantasy managers in deeper leagues.

 

 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Tee Higgins , WR, Cincinnati Bengals 

 Higgins has caught at least one touchdown in back-to-back games, and he has seen a total of 18 targets during that stretch. In a Cincinnati offense that must be more pass-heavy due to a lack of rushing efficiency, Higgins will get opportunities versus a Falcons defense that plays man-free coverage (man coverage with a safety in the middle) on 41.8% of opponent dropbacks, the second-highest rate in the league. Look for quarterback Joe Burrow  to target Higgins on those one-on-one matchups.

 
 

 Malachi Fields , WR, New York Giants 

 Fields has just one touchdown reception on the season ( Week 4 against the Cardinals ), but he caught four of five targets for 83 yards from quarterback J.J. McCarthy in Week 7 . With his physical profile, Fields can create favorable matchups for himself on the boundary. And he did see an end zone target from McCarthy in their last game before the bye. Let's take Fields to score on a fade route against the Eagles.

 
 

 Kaelon Black , RB, San Francisco 49ers 

 Black scored his first NFL touchdown in a Week 7 loss to the Falcons , and he has seen his role expand as a change-of-pace runner behind  Christian McCaffrey . Black has at least nine touches in each of his past two games, and the Week 9 matchup is perfect for him to find the end zone again. The Raiders are allowing 146.4 rushing yards per game, the second most in the league.

 

 

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 Vikings' Carson Wentz will create QB controversy

title: Joe Burrow makes time for art in Madrid ahead of Bengals-Falcons
summary: While in Spain, the Bengals quarterback is finding time for one of his off-field interests: art.
full_text:
MADRID -- Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow knows what he wants to do with his free time exploring Madrid ahead of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons . Forget football -- well, at least the American kind. The Cincinnati star, who attracted a massive media gathering Friday, said that if he gets a chance to wind down, he'd like to indulge one of his many off-field interests and see the art around the Spanish capital.

 "I'd like to go see some more museums and go to an art gallery and do a little shopping, but we'll see," Burrow said.

 The Pro Bowler and two-time MVP finalist already accomplished some of that earlier in the week when he stopped by the Museo del Prado during Cincinnati's first off day in Madrid. The team arrived from Cincinnati on Wednesday morning, which allowed him some time to go explore.

 And even if he wasn't back home, it doesn't mean he didn't go unnoticed. He said he ran into a group of students from the United States who are studying abroad who recognized him. It's fitting for a person whose profile has grown well beyond the game in recent years.

 "It's often a little more than I expect when I'm in a different country," Burrow said. "I usually expect to go pretty incognito and not have anybody recognize me. It's usually a little more than that. But I love being out here because I can feel like a normal person for a little bit."

 Burrow and the Bengals (5-2) have spent the week trying to balance being tourists and also preparing for a showdown against the Falcons (3-5) at the historic Santiago Bernabeu stadium, which is home to Real Madrid .

 Former Real Madrid keeper Thibaut Courtois and ex-Atletico Madrid star Koke were among those who came out to see the Bengals at the training grounds of the Spanish men's and women's national teams, which is roughly 20 miles northwest of downtown.

 Burrow talked about his love for international soccer and how much he played video games using the Real Madrid and Barcelona teams. Unfortunately, Burrow and Cincinnati will be out of town by the time Barcelona visits Atletico on Sunday evening.

 

 But he should be able to still enjoy his other hobbies and interests that make him as unique as the city he'll be playing in this weekend.

 "I play a little piano," Burrow said. "I build Legos. I play chess. I like art. I like music. I certainly like more things than just football."

title: 3 ways Browns QB Shedeur Sanders can show growth vs. Saints
summary: The opportunity is a big one as the second-year quarterback's first start of the season comes at a critical time.
full_text:
Before Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken announced on Aug. 24 that he was naming Deshaun Watson the team's starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders , he spoke with Sanders in his office about his forward-looking approach.

 Ten weeks later, Sanders is poised to make his first start of the 2026 NFL season Sunday at the New Orleans Saints  ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ) as Watson remains sidelined in the NFL's concussion protocol.

 "He's very diligent and he likes to play football, has a natural confidence about him," Monken said Friday. "Just like any young player, they've got to play. ... Where he's improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections. There were so many things he needed to work on, and he's done that like any young player. Any young player has a lot to work on, especially at the quarterback position.

 "And you can see that from the moment we got here and that's why we opened up the competition and we split the reps was because of his ascent."

 Sanders' first start of the season comes at a critical time. The Browns are 5-3 after a Week 8 road loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers that knocked Cleveland out of first place in the AFC North. ESPN Analytics gives the Browns a 16.5% chance of making the playoffs. A win against the Saints would increase their odds to 25.4% ahead of four straight home games.

 

 Sanders made seven starts as a rookie last season and went 3-4 in those games, but he posted a 19.0 Total QBR, the fifth-lowest mark among 696 quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts in a season in the QBR era (since 2006). He has spent the first eight weeks of the regular season as the backup, getting minimal practice reps, but he has familiarity with the starting offense after splitting reps with Watson in the quarterback competition during training camp.

 "I'm just excited to see him go play and hopefully let it rip, which I think he'll do," Browns offensive coordinator Travis Switzer said this week. "He did it [Wednesday] in practice. Go lead, be in command, which I think he's grown tremendously in that area, really since we got here.

 "And I think Monk[en] mentioned this the other day, but when you're going through training camp, and we were splitting, and really all the spring, we were splitting a lot of those reps as we were going through all the installs, and we were able to see him in a lot more reps than probably a typical backup would be, because obviously we were finding out who our quarterback was going to be. So, hopefully he can review back to some of those things if it were to be him, and yeah, let it rip. Play with confidence."

 Coaches and teammates have praised Sanders' growth in recent months. In New Orleans, he will get the opportunity to display that progression and lead a struggling offense that ranks 29th in points per game (17.4).

 

 Here are the three ways Shedeur Sanders can showcase his progress: 

 Playing within structure 
 The tendency for Sanders to hold on to the ball has been a talking point since his time at Colorado. Sanders has acknowledged he tends to hold the ball in efforts to make a big play -- sometimes to his own detriment. As a rookie, Sanders averaged 3.24 seconds to throw, the slowest among 38 quarterbacks who made at least six starts in 2025.

 In August, Monken highlighted Sanders' growth in striking a balance between playing within structure and also making plays by holding on to the ball.

 "Being able to check the ball down and get it out of his hands; he's such a playmaker that that's hard for him," Monken said. "For a guy that is always looking to make a play, super competitive, that is a win. Trying to get super competitive quarterbacks to understand that throwing the ball away and eliminating lost yardage plays is a win."

 In 25 dropbacks across two games in the preseason, Sanders had an average time to throw of 3.10 seconds, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. The Browns have the fifth-most yards after catch in the NFL (1,019) this season.

 Getting the ball to pass catchers in the flow of the offense plays a big role in that. It also helps to prevent sacks. Watson has taken the most sacks in the league (33), in part because he has held the ball for too long at times.

 

 

 Taking care of the ball 

 Sanders threw 10 interceptions from Weeks 11 to 18 last season, which led all quarterbacks in the league during that time frame. Not every pick was the result of a bad decision or throw; some were caused by dropped passes or batted balls.

 But at times, Sanders played a risky brand of football that lent itself to turnovers. He had four dropped interceptions from Weeks 11 to 18, twice as many as the next-closest quarterback during that same time span, according to ESPN Research, and tied for the most by any player all of last season.

 This season, Watson has only thrown three interceptions, but he has seven fumbles, which leads all quarterbacks, and has lost three fumbles.

 

 Pre-snap operation 

 A major point of emphasis for Monken during the quarterback competition was the pre-snap operation. Monken heaps plenty of responsibility on his QBs to get the offense in and out of the huddle properly, make the correct adjustments at the line of scrimmage, use cadence correctly and limit pre-snap penalties.

 

 The latter has been an issue for Cleveland through eight games. According to ESPN Research, the Browns have five delay of game penalties, tied for the fifth most in the league, as well as five illegal formation penalties, which are tied for the fourth most. Not all of those infractions fall on the quarterback, but it is largely their responsibility to take control of the pre-snap operation and "eliminate anxiety," in the words of Monken.

 When asked to assess Sanders' brief three plays against Pittsburgh while Watson was checked for a concussion, Monken alluded to "a couple plays he could have helped us out with a check" but added that it was unfair to grade Sanders with such limited practice reps.

 A raucous environment at the Caesars Superdome will provide a tough test for Sanders, but coaches have said they don't anticipate needing to adjust the game plan or pre-snap operation with Sanders under center.

 "The more anxiety that we can relieve pre-snap, which usually comes down to the play clock, just having as much time as possible before the play clock to allow us to operate and relieve that anxiety, I think that's going to be huge," Switzer said.

 "As far as the snap count goes, when we're in the gun we'll be in silent [count], and we've been in silent every road game this year. So that part I don't think is really a whole lot different, but certainly just trying to put a premium, like we always do, but especially this week with them being indoors and it being a loud place, we talk about the four twos. Our pre-snap, in and out of the huddle. Shortening calls as a staff as much as we possibly can.

 "Monk[en] will talk about getting the play in as fast as possible, which he always tries to do. All those things are certainly at a premium when you play at a place like that," Switzer said.

title: Regrading 2025 NFL deadline trades: How Gardner, Williams deals look right now
summary: How do the Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams blockbuster trades look one year later? What about the Jakobi Meyers, Rashid Shaheed and Jaelan Phillips deals?
full_text:
I'm a firm believer in evaluating trades the moment they happen. But we should check in on the results after they've played out, too. One year removed from a trade, how does it look in retrospect? Let's look back at the 2025 NFL trade deadline one year later. We're including blockbuster trades for Quinnen Williams and Sauce Gardner , along with other deals that sent players like Jaelan Phillips , Jakobi Meyers and Rashid Shaheed to playoff teams.

 In this exercise I'm grading trades like I always do, taking into account player quality, draft pick compensation, contract details and team time horizons. But in this case we have results of a year of play, too. These grades are descriptive of the past 12 months -- meaning they reflect the results of how they panned out -- along with my expectations for the remaining effects of the trade going forward.

 How should we feel about the Williams deal now? How about the Odafe Oweh for Alohi Gilman swap? Or the Shaheed deal, especially considering the Seahawks' Super Bowl LX victory ? Before this year's trade deadline hits on Nov. 10, let's finish up our evaluation of the last one.

 
 More trade deadline content: 
 Trade tracker | Trade grades 

 
 

 
 Jump to a 2025 regrade: 
 Gardner/Mitchell | Williams/Smith 
 Meyers  | Oweh/Gilman | Phillips 
 Shaheed | White | Campbell/Newsome 

 
 

 

 CB Gardner to the Colts for WR Mitchell, more 
 Colts got: CB Sauce Gardner 
 Jets got: WR Adonai Mitchell , 2026 first-round pick, 2027 first-round pick

 Original grade for Colts : D 
 New grade for Colts: F

 Original grade for Jets : A 
 New grade for Jets: A

 I had a sliver of empathy for the Colts when this trade was made given the situation they were in. At that moment, ESPN's Football Power Index gave Indianapolis an 11% chance to win the Super Bowl. Here's what I wrote, "Not only is this their best chance in years, but it's probably the best chance they will have for the next few years."

 I feel pretty good about that assessment 12 months later. But that didn't even come close to negating the obvious, instant takeaway from this trade when it was made: It was an ill-advised and reckless overpay. It's fine for NFL teams to push their chips in while contending. But there must be a price limit to every transaction, and the Colts blew past what was reasonable. It looks even worse now, because everything that has happened since has been a disaster for Indianapolis.

 Gardner suffered a calf injury in his third game with the Colts, which cost him all but one game the rest of the season. One week later, quarterback Daniel Jones suffered a season-ending Achilles injury . The Colts won only one game after trading for Gardner, plummeting from 7-2 to 8-9 and finishing the season out of the playoffs.

 

 With Gardner and Jones both healthy in 2026, there was still a chance for the trade to have some value. But neither has played great. Jones ranks 29th out of 30 qualifying quarterbacks in QBR while Gardner has allowed 1.1 yards per coverage snap this season -- average for an outside cornerback. Gardner also has plus-8.5 EPA allowed on targets (worse than average). While I believe some of Gardner's numbers are a result of contested catch variance and that he's playing better than his 1.1 number suggests, the results have not been great.

 Ultimately, the Colts lost their first-round pick last year (which the Jets turned into tight end Kenyon Sadiq ) and now don't have a first-round pick in 2027 -- right as they begin a rebuild. It's extremely unideal, especially since the Colts would have the No. 4 overall pick if the season ended today. That pick could go even higher, as Indianapolis fired GM Chris Ballard on Oct. 19 and has already traded multiple veteran players preceding this year's deadline.

 

 One part of this trade I haven't mentioned thus far is Mitchell, but he shouldn't be overlooked. This deal would have been an A for the Jets without him, but he's no throw-in. Mitchell had always shown an ability to get open, but that hadn't resulted in serious production. That might be in progress this season. Though he missed time with a finger injury , Mitchell has put up an extraordinary 2.6 yards per route run when he has been on the field. The Jets look like they also got a starting-caliber wide receiver out of this trade, making it even better.

 For the Jets, this move in conjunction with the Quinnen Williams trade has given New York the draft capital it needs to put together a talented young core and have a shot at a top quarterback in the 2027 draft. It has been a long, painful road for the Jets, but their willingness to deal their stars at last year's deadline has set them up for future success.

 

 

 DT Williams to the Cowboys for DT Smith, more 
 Cowboys got: DT Quinnen Williams 
 Jets got: DT Mazi Smith , 2026 second-round pick, 2027 first-round pick

 Original grade for Cowboys : F 
 New grade for Cowboys: D

 Original grade for Jets : A 
 New grade for Jets: A

 At the time of this trade, I was completely dumbfounded at Dallas' decision to make this deal. Prior to dealing for Williams, FPI gave the Cowboys a 7% chance to reach the playoffs, which is precisely when a team should not deal away future first-round picks for veterans.

 Part of my criticism was that Williams could play well in 2025 and that it wouldn't matter because of the hole the Cowboys had dug themselves. That's precisely what happened -- from Week 11 on, Williams ranked second in pass rush win rate and ninth in run stop win rate at defensive tackle. Those are incredible rankings! But they were not enough to get Dallas to the playoffs, as the Cowboys finished the season 7-9-1.

 This season, Williams still ranks in the top 10 in run stop win rate for interior defenders, but his pass rush win rate has fallen to average (though he does have five sacks). And the Dallas defense? It's still bad, ranking 31st in EPA allowed per play.

 So my belief then is my belief now: Williams is a great player, but the Cowboys gave up far too much for him, especially considering where they were in the standings at the time of the deal. At the time of the original grade, I'm not sure we knew that the Cowboys were surrendering the better of their two 2027 first-round picks -- theirs and the Packers' -- which only furthered the downside for the Cowboys (and upside for the Jets).

 There were ripple effects, too. With a surplus at defensive tackle, the team traded Osa Odighizuwa ( for not enough ) to the 49ers in March, keeping Williams and Kenny Clark -- who came over in the Micah Parsons trade . The Cowboys also extended Williams with a lucrative three-year, $105.9 million extension in August.

 

 

 As for the Jets? This was a home run then and a home run now. The team wasn't going anywhere in 2025, and it was able to gain a ton of surplus value via draft capital, which is helping build a group of talented young players. The Jets were the biggest winners of last year's trade deadline, and it set them up for success in 2027 and beyond. It doesn't even matter that Smith didn't stick in New York .

 

 

 WR Meyers to the Jaguars 
 Jaguars got: WR Jakobi Meyers 
 Raiders got: 2026 fourth-round pick, 2026 sixth-round pick

 Original grade for Jaguars : C+ 
 New grade for Jaguars: B+

 Original grade for Raiders : A- 
 New grade for Raiders: B+

 This trade was made to help replace lost wide receiver production due to poor performance from Brian Thomas Jr . and a season-ending injury to Travis Hunter . Which is funny, because it turns out the perfect person to step up was already on Jacksonville's roster.  Parker Washington  emerged last season and has elevated his play even further in 2026 to where he is now the Jaguars' clear No. 1 wide receiver.

 Even though Washington has produced a superb 2.6 yards per route run since the trade for Meyers, Meyers has been a helpful player in his own right, recording 1.6 yards per route run since arriving in Jacksonville.…

full_text:
While Week 8 meant the debut of two "Rivalries" jerseys, another alternate look returns to the field in Week 9, and a popular throwback comes back. 

 

 The Los Angeles Chargers are wearing their "Super Chargers" all-navy threads against the Houston Texans . Unveiled in 2025, the Chargers deemed the navy uniforms "a true modern throwback." It's a nod to threads worn in the 1990s and early 2000s, which coincided with a Super Bowl XXIX appearance and four AFC West titles. The navy jersey includes white modern numbers with an old-school outline and gold trim. The navy pants boast a bolt on the side, while a bolt also runs on the shoulders and helmet. "Super Chargers" is stitched in white on the neckline. 

 In a trend that's becoming more common around the league, the New York Giants and Philadelphia Eagles offer a matchup of throwback uniforms. The Eagles are rocking their "Kelly Green" threads, while it's a "Vintage White" look for the Giants. "Thursday Night Football" between the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks in Week 6 also brought a throwback threads matchup. Philadelphia brought back the iconic Kelly Green combination in 2023, while New York's look returned in 2025 after a one-year hiatus. 

 Alternates are still represented well throughout the week, though.

 The Baltimore Ravens are wearing their "Purple Rising" combination on "Thursday Night Football" against the Jacksonville Jaguars . Baltimore unveiled the look in the offseason as part of their wardrobe overhaul. It includes a new "Purple Rising" helmet, first introduced in 2024 with the alternate purple jersey. The primary logo appears on the metallic purple lid instead of the front-facing Ravens one. Different from the previous all-purple combination is a new "midnight purple" color, which is meant to emulate the iridescence of a raven's feather, and "Purple Rising" running on the inside collar.

 The New Orleans Saints are going gold against the Cleveland Browns . And it's another navy look for the Dallas Cowboys against the Indianapolis Colts , who are doing a rare home white out.

title: The New York Giants 'don't care' that they're NFC East favorites
summary: It's an unfamiliar role for a franchise that hasn't claimed the NFC East crown since 2011.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The tides have turned in an upside-down NFC East. The New York Giants , once massive underdogs to win the division, are now the favorites. 
 
 It's an unfamiliar role for a franchise that hasn't claimed the NFC East crown since 2011. 
 
 "Yeah, I don't know. To me, it's all kind of meaningless," coach John Harbaugh said. "I mean, if you're betting, it's important, but it doesn't matter to us because there's still 10 games left to play. And I'm quite sure every one of the teams in the division believes that in those 10 games, they can make up ground. I've had experience with that in my coaching career. Players know that it's what you do; it's not what anybody says about you or where you get ranked or anything like that. It's just about what you do. You've got to go win games." 
 
 The Giants (4-2-1) still have to beat the Eagles in Philadelphia on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox) for the first time in 13 years, but if they do, it will be the latest step in regaining legitimacy against their once-dominant rival. The Eagles have won the past two NFC East titles and five division championships since the Giants' last.   
 
 But with Philadelphia (2-6) decimated by injury and the surprising Giants off to a strong start in Harbaugh's first season, there is an unfamiliar pecking order in the division. Almost at the midway point of the season, New York has officially evolved into the favorite to win the NFC East. Perhaps even several weeks late with the Cowboys and Eagles struggling so badly. 
 
 "It doesn't mean anything," Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor said. "All that stuff is for Vegas. Obviously, it was annoying that they kept saying other teams were favorites. But I think at this point, we just don't care. If you handle your business, you're going to win. The oddsmakers don't go out there on Sunday. If we continue winning, like I said, it handles itself." 
 
 
 
 The Giants are currently the only team in the NFC East with a winning record. The Cowboys (3-5) and Commanders (2-4-1) are struggling, much like the Eagles. It's not out of the realm of possibility that if the Giants go 4-6 in their final 10 games, they still manage to win the division. A record of 8-8-1 might get it done this season. 
 
 As a result, the Giants are currently -150 to win the NFC East, according to DraftKings sportsbook. The Cowboys are second at +245, while the Eagles are massive long shots at +3300, creating a true role reversal from recent years. 
 
 New York came into the season +600 and had a 12% chance to win the NFC East, according to ESPN Analytics. The Eagles were +120 and had a 44% chance to win the division. 
 
 The Giants were dealt the underdog card, but they didn't seem to agree. 
 
 "In my mind, I feel like every time we play, we should be the favorite," tight end Isaiah Likely said. "And that's just the mentality I have." 
 
 Likely came from Baltimore with Harbaugh where they won the division two of the past four seasons. The Giants, meanwhile, had become regular basement dwellers before Harbaugh's arrival. They finished last in the NFC East in five of the past nine seasons. 
 
 This four-day stretch when they play Sunday against the Eagles and Thursday night against the Commanders could signal a changing of the guard. It's an opportunity for the Giants to show they should be taken seriously, even with their third quarterback of the season, J.J. McCarthy , starting games. 
 
 "I think you can use these games to put the entire league on notice," Eluemunor said. 
 
 The Giants are also expected to add some sort of reinforcements prior to the trade deadline Tuesday. Among the players they've made an offer for is Colts running back Jonathan Taylor , sources told ESPN. 
 
 The rest of the division's struggles have certainly opened the door for the Giants to be aggressive. So far, they've taken advantage. New York already thrashed the Cowboys in the opener at MetLife Stadium. It was just their third win in 19 matchups with Dallas. 
 
 This is their chance to end the skid in Philadelphia and grab command of the division in a down year for the NFC East. 
 
 "Definitely," outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux said. "I think it's definitely when you get on a roll in football, you got to keep going. You don't want anything to stop your momentum because it's hard to get it back once you lose it." 
 
 Nobody knows for sure if this will stick with the Giants or it's a one-year hiatus for the Eagles. Just about everything has gone wrong this season in Philadelphia, including starting quarterback Jalen Hurts being out indefinitely because of blood clots in his lungs. 
 
 At least for now, the Eagles appear to be a team on the decline. The Giants, with a new coach and some exciting young talent, look like a team on the rise. Winning the division would be an accomplishment. NFC East titles matter to the executive level of the New York Football Giants organization.

title: ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame honors Drew Bennett's 53-point game
summary: Drew Bennett's 53-point gem in Week 14 of 2004 propelled many a team towards a fantasy football championship.
full_text:
Fantasy football is all about fun, competition and camaraderie, but it's also another way to appreciate the best of the best in the NFL. For more than three decades, ESPN Fantasy has been here with you, celebrating peak performers and magical moments.

 Presenting the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame   , which honors the best players and acknowledges the most memorable moments since the advent of our game in 1995, the first year that fantasy football was available on ESPN.com. 

 Take me to the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame 

 Class of 2026 Week 9 Inductee: Drew Bennett's 53-point Game 
 Dec. 13, 2004 (Week 14) 
 53.3 fantasy points 
 12 receptions, 233 receiving yards, 3 receiving TDs 

 One of the most memorable late-season hot streaks during the ESPN fantasy era, Bennett's run -- and to a lesser extent his quarterback, Billy Volek's -- decided many a league title in 2004. An undrafted free agent playing his first season as a full-time starter, Bennett began his December by posting the three best single-game fantasy point totals of his eight-year career, accentuated by this 53.3-point masterpiece in Week 14. Volek, meanwhile, scored 91.88 fantasy points during that same Week 13-15 span. Despite their valiant efforts, the Titans lost all three games by a combined score of 140-97, but their fantasy managers likely fared better in their matchups!

 Bennett will be inducted Sunday during " Fantasy Focus Countdown " (10 a.m. ET on ESP2). Tune in each week through Week 16 as we reveal all 18 members of the inaugural class of the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame.
